You don’t want me practicing the footwork inside Vespera’s vessel first?"
Morwenna shook her head, running a hand through her messy, sea-swept hair.
"It’s better to learn new physical techniques when you are at your absolute full, native strength," Morwenna explained logically with her sharp eyes meeting his.
"Your original frame has your true reach, your true muscle density, and your natural center of gravity.
If you try to learn the foundational mechanics of a new sword style inside a lightweight single-armed body first, your brain will adapt to a shorter reach and a shifted axis.
Learn it in your real form until the muscle memory is burned into your soul... then translating it to the lady’s body will be child’s play."
Silas listened quietly, the sheer pragmatic wisdom behind her words settling instantly in his mind.

’She’s completely right,’ Silas thought, impressed by her natural martial intellect. ’Building the neural pathways in my true body makes way more sense than trying to hack it together inside a disguise.’
Without another word, Silas reached up with his single right hand and pulled the black disguise ring off his left ring finger.
BOOM!
A brief brilliant wave of golden Gold Core mana erupted from his chest, wrapping around his frame in a warm swirling vortex.
In a fraction of a second, the single-armed female Lord dissolved completely.

Standing on the stone training floor was Silas Graves... restored to his imposing six-foot-two height, his broad, muscular shoulders, his short dark hair, his glowing golden-ringed eyes, and both of his powerful calloused hands.
Silas flexed his left fingers, rolling his shoulders with a satisfied grunt.
"Alright.
Back in the main driver’s seat."
Morwenna folded her arms over her leather-clad chest, a faint, approving smirk touching her lips as she looked up at his true form.
"Now then," Morwenna began, her tone shifting into that of a seasoned swordmaster.
"Do you still remember the First Style of the Tidal-Blade Arts?"
Silas let out a short confident laugh, resting his right hand casually on the pommel of his wooden practice sword.
"How could I possibly forget?" Silas answered smoothly.
"I literally executed it yesterday during our spar."
Morwenna remembered it clearly.
Not only had Silas executed the First Style but he had managed to weave the directional mana vector while suspended mid-air!
For a man who had only learned this a short time ago, executing advanced water-blade mechanics while airborne was a staggering feat of spatial awareness...
It was one of the primary reasons her pride as a Dread Queen swelled whenever she looked at him.
He wasn’t just some lucky person sitting behind a desk... he was a natural martial sponge who absorbed combat techniques at a terrifying speed.
"Good," Morwenna acknowledged, a rare glint of genuine pride shining in her gray eyes.
"Your execution of the First Style proved to me that your core control is ready for the next level.
But before I teach you the Second Style... we need to cover the Sub-Style."
Silas paused, his eyebrows pulling together.
"The Sub-Style?"
He recalled her words from earlier tonight when they had met in the Keep’s entry hall.
She had explicitly mentioned wanting to teach him the Tidal-Blade Sub-Style alongside the Second Style.
"That’s right," Morwenna nodded, taking a slow step forward.
Her boots made a crisp echoing tap against the granite floor.
She stopped five paces away, looking into his golden eyes.
"Tell me, Captain... do you know what makes a blade a blade?"
Silas stared at her, entering deep thought.
He was a guy from Earth who had spent years studying combat theory, physics, and weapon mechanics back at the academy.
He figured she was asking a deep philosophical question about the essence of martial arts.
"Well," Silas began, clearing his throat as he delivered a structured analytical answer, "fundamentally speaking, a blade is an instrument designed for kinetic force concentration.
By tapering metal down to a microscopic wedge, you minimize the surface area of impact.

When you swing the hilt, the energy produced by your hips, shoulders, and core is concentrated entirely along that razor-thin edge, allowing the shear stress applied to a target’s material structure to exceed its ultimate tensile strength.
Combined with proper edge alignment and fluid mass distribution—"
"Stop.
Just stop," Morwenna interrupted flatly, raising her hand to cut him off mid-sentence.
She rubbed her forehead with a heavy, exasperated sigh, looking at him like he was an alien speaking gibberish.
"What?" Silas blinked, completely thrown off.
"Was my explanation incorrect?"
"You’re saying far too much," Morwenna grumbled, shaking her head.
She held up a single finger, delivering her answer in the most blunt simple terms possible.
"What makes a blade a blade... is its ability to cut."
Silas froze completely.
He stood there in the vault, staring at the Pirate Queen in utter deadpan silence for three solid seconds.
It wasn’t because her words were so profoundly philosophical that they shattered his entire perspective on life...
No.
It was the exact opposite.
"Isn’t that literally what I’ve been saying this whole time?!" Silas complained out loud, gesturing with his hands in disbelief.
"I just explained the physics of cutting!
You just summarized my entire explanation into seven words!"

chapters.title: Chapter 262: Morwenna’s Lesson [II]
paragraphs: Morwenna paused, looking away with a nonchalant shrug as she casually scratched her ear.
"Your explanation was too long," Morwenna admitted with shameless honesty. "So I stopped listening after the word ’kinetic’."
Silas almost spat out his own saliva.
A massive sweatdrop formed on the back of his head as he pinched the bridge of his nose, groaning in silent defeat.

’I’m running an army of lunatics,’ Silas thought to himself with a wave of familiar exhaustion washing over his mind. ’She literally asked me a question, ignored my answer because it had too many syllables, and then repeated the exact same conclusion...’
Morwenna cleared her throat, unsheathing the wooden sword she was carrying at her hip.

"In the war we’re about to face in six days," Morwenna continued, her tone regaining its sharp serious edge, "you will be fighting against heavily armored vanguard troops, reinforced iron shields, and high-tier defensive barriers. You will need raw overwhelming cutting power in your sword... far more than standard physical steel or raw mana reinforcement can provide. And fortunately... water can be used to achieve that exact effect."
Morwenna fluidly dropped her center of gravity, sinking into a low balanced dueling stance.
She looked up at Silas, gesturing toward his Lord Inventory.
"Pull out a real steel sword, Captain," Morwenna instructed. "I want you to attack me with everything you’ve got."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "A real steel blade? Against your wooden practice sword?"
"Don’t worry about my sword," Morwenna smirked arrogantly. "Just draw your steel."
Silas reached into his spatial storage, channeling a quick wave of inventory mana.
FLASH!
In a flash of light, a sleek, double-edged steel longsword materialized in his right hand.
It was a standard high-grade military steel blade... one of the weapons Silas had originally purchased from the commercial market back in the city for Martha, his household guardian back on Earth.
Unfortunately, Martha knew absolutely nothing about swordsmanship and had ended up using the expensive steel blade as an overpriced prop to keep her cellar doors propped open.
Silas discarded the leather scabbard to the side, gripping the steel hilt firmly with his right hand.
Across the training floor, Morwenna took a deep steady breath.
FWOOSH!
A subtle hypnotic transformation occurred around her wooden practice cutlass.
A paper-thin completely transparent film of clear water materialized over the wooden surface.
The layer of water was so microscopic it was almost invisible to the naked eye... but as Silas focused his Gold Core perception, his jaw tightened.
That thin film of water wasn’t stationary.

It was spinning around the wooden blade at an astronomical high-frequency rotational speed... vibrating so rapidly that it generated a microscopic high-pitched hum that buzzed through the air like a saw.
"Come at me, Captain," Morwenna commanded, her stormy gray eyes locking onto his. "Don’t hold back."
Silas didn’t hesitate. He knew better than to underestimate the Dread Queen, even when she was wielding a piece of carved timber.
STOMP!
Silas drove his right boot into the granite floor, exploding forward with high-speed physical momentum.
He closed the five-pace distance in a fraction of a second, raising his steel longsword high above his right shoulder.
To ensure his strike possessed absolute destructive force, Silas didn’t just swing blindly... he ignited his Gold Core!
BOOM!
A surge of blinding liquid gold mana erupted from his arm, aggressively coating the entire length of the steel longsword in a dense radiant aura of sovereign power.

’Ironwood is remarkably tough,’ Silas calculated in his mind mid-charge, ’and her water control is divine... but once I pour my unsuppressed Gold Core mana directly into a solid steel blade, there is zero chance a wooden blade can block a full-power downward strike without getting splintered!’
"Alright, now!" Silas roared, bringing the golden-coated steel blade crashing down in a brutal, vertical execution arc.
SWISH!
Morwenna didn’t dodge and she didn’t retreat. Hell, she didn’t even shift her boots on the stone floor.
With a single and terrifyingly casual flick of her wrist, Morwenna whipped her wooden blade upward in a sharp diagonal parry, meeting his falling steel blade mid-air.
SHING!
There was no deafening explosion of metal...
There was only a sound so impossibly crisp, so sharp, and so frictionless that it sounded like a hot needle gliding through soft silk.
Silas’s momentum carried him forward with his boots skidding across the stone floor as he passed right by Morwenna’s flank, coming to a halt behind her.
Silas blinked, looking down at his right hand.
The hilt of the steel longsword was still firmly in his grip... but the top half of the blade was completely gone.
CLINK... THUD.
Two feet behind him, the top half of his gold-reinforced steel sword hit the stone floor, cleanly severed in twain.
The cut across the solid steel was so smooth and so perfectly polished that it reflected the torchlight like a pristine mirror.
Silas slowly turned his head, staring at Morwenna’s wooden blade in mind-shattering shock.
The wooden practice sword was completely untouched.
There was not a single dent, a single splinter, or a single microscopic scratch on its polished surface.
The paper-thin high-frequency film of water was still spinning smoothly around the wood, humming quietly in the air.
Silas stood there with his mouth slightly open as he looked from his severed steel blade back to her untouched wooden sword.

"The Tidal-Blade Sub-Style," Morwenna explained casually, lowering her wooden sword to her side, "is a fluid manipulation technique designed strictly for increasing the raw cutting power of your edge. By compressing water into a high-frequency microscopic spinning sheath around your weapon, you eliminate physical friction entirely. The water blade slices through matter at a molecular level before the physical edge of your sword even touches the target."
Morwenna turned around, offering him a sharp proud smile.
"And the best part? Because it is a foundational Sub-Style, you can stack it seamlessly on top of the First Style, the Second Style, or any physical sword technique in your arsenal."
Silas looked at the severed piece of steel resting on the floor, then threw the ruined hilt to the side.
CLANG!
He walked over to the weapon rack, picking up his original wooden training longsword.
Holding the polished timber in his hand, Silas looked up at the Pirate Queen, his golden-ringed eyes burning with intense determination.
"Teach me, Master," Silas said earnestly. "I want to get stronger."
The second the word "Master" left Silas’s lips—
Morwenna’s entire posture instantly stiffened.
Her stormy gray eyes widened slightly with her jaw tightening as if she had just swallowed something unexpectedly sour.
To an ordinary martial artist or Swordsman, hearing an elite pupil call them "Master" would be an intoxicating fulfilling moment of authority.

But to Morwenna... hearing her Captain... the man who commanded her loyalty, the man whose bed she shared, and the man whose touch made her heart race address her with the formal distant title of "Master" felt completely wrong.
That was not the kind of relationship she wanted to have with Silas.
Morwenna let out a quiet breath, stepping out of her low combat stance.
She stood up tall, placing her left hand firmly on her hip with her gray eyes locking onto his face with an unusually intense confrontational glare.
"Before I teach you another single thing, Captain..." Morwenna spoke up. "I wanted to ask you something."
Silas blinked his golden eyes, slightly confused by her sudden shift in demeanor. "Ask me what?"
Morwenna looked him dead in the eyes, her lips pressing into a tight line as she blurted out her complaint without a single shred of hesitation:
"Why don’t you kiss me, Captain?"
Silas went completely speechless.
He stood there holding his wooden longsword with his brain momentarily short-circuiting as he stared at the formidable fierce Dread Queen standing five feet away from him.
"You..." Silas stammered out, thoroughly caught off guard, "you’re asking about... kisses?"
Morwenna’s hand fell from her hip to her side, her fingers scratching her thigh awkwardly as a dark flush began creeping up her neck, dusting her high cheekbones with a rare flustered red.
Yet, despite her obvious shyness, her pirate pride refused to let her back down.

"Yes! Kisses!" Morwenna demanded loudly, venting her bottled-up frustration. "You kiss Eluned for every single little thing! You kissed her at the gates, you kissed her after she cast that barrier, and you kissed her in your room! I can’t stop hearing about it because she won’t stop talking! She won’t stop coming into the main hall and bragging about it to me, Captain!"
Morwenna crossed her arms over her chest, looking away toward the stone wall with an annoyed defensive pout with her raspy voice dropping into a vulnerable tone.

"She uses it to brag..." Morwenna admitted softly, her toes curling slightly inside her leather boots. "And honestly... it’s starting to make me feel less of myself. Am I not entitled to kisses as well? Are you... are you not attracted to my body the same way you are with Elune—"
Before Morwenna could finish her insecure rambling sentence...
STEP.
Silas didn’t let her say another word.
He had closed the five-pace distance on silent feet.

Before the Dread Queen even realized he was standing directly in front of her, Silas reached out his broad, muscular right hand, cupping the back of her neck firmly, and leaned down, taking her full, soft lips in a deep captivating kiss.
MMMPH!
Morwenna went completely rigid.
Her stormy gray eyes widened to the size of saucers with her breath catching in her throat as the warm intoxicating scent of her Lord flooded her sentences.
Inside Silas’s mind, a subtle wave of apprehension had lingered right up until the moment their lips touched.
Truth be told, Silas had half-expected the fierce woman to react on instinct and drive a sharp elbow straight into his ribs or punch his face!
Instead... contrary to all his fears... Morwenna didn’t punch him at all.
The moment she felt the warm strength of his hand at the back of her neck and the firm pressure of his lips against hers, the fierce intimidating pirate captain completely melted away.
Her stiff shoulders softened, her long eyelashes fluttered shut, and she eased into the kiss with a shy breathless hesitation that was adorable.
Her lips were soft and tasted like sweet ocean air if it had a taste.
Silas felt her gentle hesitant yield with a slow smirk forming against her lips.
He tightened his grip on her neck, leaning in deeper and using a gentle pressure to pry her soft lips open.
SLIDE...
Silas slid his tongue past her teeth, tangling it directly with hers.
"Mmm~"
Morwenna let out a soft shuddering gasp against his mouth, her mind spinning in a dizzying haze of pure pleasure.
For three seconds, she stood there passively, allowing him to dominate her senses.
Then... her innate, fiercely competitive pirate spirit kicked in.
The moment her dazed brain realized that this physical exchange was a battle of dominance... a mutual high-stakes competition of passion, Morwenna’s eyes snapped open mid-kiss.
Her gray eyes burned with a fierce battle-hungry light.
’I’m a Dread Queen of the high seas!’ Morwenna swore stubbornly in her mind. ’I refuse to get completely overwhelmed by my Captain!’
SWISH!
Morwenna threw her arms around Silas’s broad neck, pulling his head down aggressively as she fought back.
She wrapped her tongue around his with a wild and fierce intensity, wrestling for control of the kiss with pure passion.
Silas’s golden eyes sparkled with amusement.
’This is why Morwenna is really cute...’
Silas didn’t try to out-wrestle her tongue with pure speed.
Instead, he smoothly slid his free left hand down her lower back, wrapping his calloused fingers firmly around the plump soft curve of her right buttock and gave her rear a heavy squeeze.
"AHNNN~!"
Morwenna let out a loud and deeply melodious moan right into his mouth.

The sudden intense physical sensation sent an electric shockwave straight up her spine as her knees went completely weak, her competitive defenses were instantly pulverized, and she lost the tongue-wrestling battle, slumping helplessly against his broad chest as Silas claimed complete victory over her lips.
After a long breathless moment that left the vault echoing with their soft gasps, Silas slowly pulled his face back.
A single glistening delicate strand of saliva connected their parted lips for a second before breaking softly in the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 263: Morwenna’s Lesson [III]
paragraphs: Morwenna rested her forehead against his chest with her face flushed a deep burning crimson and her chest heaving violently as she tried to catch her breath.
Her stormy gray eyes were wide, dazed, and thoroughly glossy with affection.
Silas smiled warmly, leaning down to plant a soft gentle kiss right on her smooth forehead.
He looked down at the flustered Dread Queen in his arms with his gravelly voice dropping into a low reassuring whisper.
"Truth be told, Morwenna... I was scared of kissing you before. I was afraid you would punch my jaw through the ceiling if I made a sudden move."
Silas cupped her flushed cheek, his golden eyes filled with genuine sincerity as he added.
"But I’m not scared anymore. From now on... I promise I will ensure to shower you with kisses always."
Morwenna stood there in his arms with her heart hammering against her ribs so loudly it felt like a war drum.

She had commanded fleets, slain sea leviathans, and faced down god-tier beings without blinking an eye... yet right now, looking into Silas’s golden-ringed eyes and hearing his sweet promise, she felt helplessly overwhelmed.
Morwenna didn’t know how to react.
Overcome by dizzying embarrassment, Morwenna suddenly pushed off his chest, leaping backward three full paces with a loud sound of wind.
WHOOSH!
She landed in a low crouch, holding her wooden sword in front of her face, trying frantically to hide her bright red cheeks behind the timber blade.
Her gray eyes flickered with a messy and fiercely happy light.
"Y-You better...!" Morwenna stammered out, her raspy voice trembling slightly as she cleared her throat aggressively. "You... you better keep that promise, Captain! Or... or I’ll cut your boots off!"
Silas chuckled warmly, shaking his head as he adjusted his grip on his wooden longsword.
"I always keep my word. Now... show me the stance."
Morwenna took three deep breaths, forcefully suppressing the blissful fuzzy sensation swirling inside her chest, forcing her master-swordsman composure back into place.
"Right! The stance!" Morwenna called out, dropping into position.
She demonstrated the footwork clearly.

"The Tidal-Blade Sub-Style requires a wide fluid base," Morwenna explained, pointing her wooden blade forward. "Unlike regular styles that anchor your weight solidly into the ground, water styles require your weight to float continuously between your heels and the balls of your feet... like a ship riding rolling ocean waves. Turn your hips thirty degrees, lower your center of gravity, and align your lead shoulder with the target."
Silas carefully observed her positioning, adjusting his stance to mirror hers perfectly.
STEP!
Silas shifted his feet, sinking his hips and aligning his lead shoulder with her wooden cutlass.
His weight distribution shifted seamlessly between his boots, mimicking the fluid motion of sea waves.
Morwenna inspected his form, walking around him and gently tapping his right hip with the flat of her sword to correct his angle by an inch.
"Good. Perfect posture," Morwenna praised. "Now... for the water film itself."
Morwenna held her wooden sword out in front of her.

"You need to channel a paper-thin layer of water mana directly over the surface of your wooden blade. It cannot be thick like a defensive shield, nor can it be sloppy like a wave. It must be a microscopic uniform sheath... no thicker than a single strand of hair."
Silas closed his eyes, focusing his mind.
Inside his chest, his Gold Core responded instantly to his command.

Because Silas had already achieved high-tier mastery over the fundamental water element... having previously learned [Tidal Impact] and various water manipulation spells, gathering the water element was second nature to him.
FWOOSH!
A gentle cooling wave of blue water mana flowed down his right arm, travelling into the hilt of his wooden training longsword.
Silas meticulously compressed the fluid, spreading the water out across the timber until a pristine paper-thin film of clear liquid wrapped around the wooden blade from guard to tip.
Silas opened his eyes, looking at his sword. "Like this?"
Morwenna looked at his wooden blade with her jaw dropping slightly in genuine surprise.
He had achieved the uniform paper-thin liquid sheath on his very first attempt!
"By the sea..." Morwenna murmured softly under her breath. "Your elemental affinity truly is absurd..."
She cleared her throat quickly, regaining her composure.
"Ahem! Yes! That part is correct! But now comes the difficult part... the high-frequency rotation."
Morwenna tapped her blade, showing him the internal mana flow.

"A static film of water is just wet wood," Morwenna explained clearly. "To give the water its terrifying cutting power, you must force the liquid film to spin around the blade at extreme rotational velocity... You must create thousands of microscopic, spinning fluid saws running along the edge simultaneously."
Silas focused his mind on the thin layer of water covering his wooden sword.
He channeled his Gold Core mana, trying to force the stationary film of water to begin rotating rapidly around the wooden edge.
’Spin...’ Silas thought, concentrating his core output. ’Spin at high frequency!’
ZZZZZZZT!
However... controlling the fluid dynamics of a high-speed rotational sheath was infinitely harder than simply holding a static film.

The moment Silas applied centrifugal acceleration to the water, the rotational force broke out of sync as the water mana expanded unevenly, creating a violent, unbalanced wobble along the wooden blade.
VRRR... BANG!
"Whoa—?!" Silas gasped out.
The extreme uncontrolled vibration generated by the uneven water rotation caused the wooden training sword to violently jerk out of his hand.
The sword shot straight out of his grip like a pressurized missile, flying across the training vault and embedding itself deep into the granite wall with a loud sound.
THWACK!
Silas stood there with his empty right hand still extended in mid-air, blinking in deadpan shock.
Across the room, Morwenna stared at the wooden sword sticking out of the stone wall, held her breath for two seconds... and then threw her head back, bursting into a loud hysterical laugh.

"AHAHAHAHAHA!" Morwenna cackled loudly, clutching her stomach as her hearty laughter echoed off the stone arches. "Oh, Captain! That was bloody brilliant! You didn’t slice the enemy, you disarmed yourself!"
Silas turned his golden eyes toward her with a prominent vein popping on his temple as he glared at the laughing Dread Queen.
"It’s called trial and error, Morwenna," Silas grumbled dryly, walking over to the wall and yanking his wooden blade out of the stone.

"Heh... fair enough, fair enough," Morwenna chuckled, wiping a tear of laughter from her eye. "Try it again. Don’t force the whole film to spin at once... Start the rotation at the hilt, and let the centrifugal wave carry the fluid up to the tip."
Silas walked back to the center of the floor, taking a deep breath.

He closed his eyes, resetting his core rhythm. He recalled Morwenna’s advice... visualizing the water not as a solid metal shell, but as a rolling ocean current starting from a narrow river mouth and expanding into a roaring vortex.
FWOOSH...
Silas wrapped the wooden blade in the thin liquid film once more.
Starting at the crossguard, he gently applied a spinning rotational frequency to the mana.
He guided the spin upward, allowing the fluid momentum to build naturally along the wooden fuller until it reached the tip.
ZZZZZZZZZT!
The wooden longsword began to hum softly.
Silas opened his eyes.
The paper-thin film of water covering his practice sword was now rotating seamlessly at high frequency.
The liquid looked almost invisible, vibrating so rapidly that the air around the wooden edge shimmered with a faint razor-sharp blue distortion.
Morwenna stopped laughing with her eyes widening as she looked at his stable high-frequency water blade.
"Outstanding..." Morwenna praised genuinely, a proud smirk spreading across her face. "You mastered the rotation in two tries. That’s remarkably good, Captain."
She raised her own wooden cutlass, her high-frequency water film humming in response.
"That’s very good..." Morwenna declared, her gray eyes flashing with fierce competitive excitement. "but let’s see whose blade is sharper!"
BOOM!
Morwenna didn’t give him a single second to celebrate as she launched off her back boot, shooting across the stone floor like a blue wave.
Silas’s Gold Core instincts flared instantly.
He dropped low into his wide stance, shifting his weight between his boots, and brought his high-frequency wooden blade up to intercept her incoming horizontal slash.
"Come on!" Silas shouted, swinging his blade forward with all his might.
KRA-THOOM!

The two spinning-water wooden blades collided in the dead center of the vault as a shockwave of pressurized water mist and wind exploded outward from the point of impact, blowing back the torch flames along the walls.
For one second, their weapons locked mid-air...
Then—
SLICK!
Morwenna’s centuries of refined fluid compression completely overrode Silas’s newly learned execution.
Her high-frequency water film cut cleanly through Silas’s water layer, gliding straight through his wooden longsword like a hot razor through butter.
CLINK... THUD!
The top half of Silas’s wooden training sword was cleanly severed, falling to the stone floor.
Morwenna’s momentum carried her past his left shoulder.
She spun gracefully on her heel, coming to a smooth elegant halt right behind him, holding her sword at her side.
Silas stood there, looking down at the half-length wooden stick remaining in his hand, letting out a long quiet sigh.
"Dammit," Silas muttered drily. "Still got chopped."
Morwenna sheathed her wooden cutlass with a crisp click then she turned around, looking at Silas’s back with a wicked mischievous grin spread across her gorgeous face.
"Now then, Captain..." Morwenna purred softly. "As for your punishment for losing this round..."
Before Silas could turn around to ask what she meant—
STEP.
Morwenna strode up right behind him.
She reached out her long, muscular arm, wrapping her fingers around the broad curve of Silas’s right rear, giving his butt a firm and completely shameless squeeze.
SQUEEZE!
Silas flinched, his golden eyes going wide in utter surprise.
Before he could react, Morwenna grabbed his shirt collar, forcibly spinning him around and pulling his sharp face down to meet hers!
She stood on her tiptoes, capturing his lips in her own version of a kiss.
Because she was still relatively new to soft romantic affection, her kiss was terribly clumsy... Even worse than Eluned...
She essentially slammed her lips against his with a loud and aggressive smack, tangling her mouth against his with unrefined enthusiastic passion.
After five seconds of clumsy, passionate lip-locking, Morwenna pulled her flushed face back, resting her hands boldly on her hips.
Her stormy gray eyes sparkled with joy with her face glowing bright red as she delivered her new training rule.
"From now on, Captain... each time you fail a clash during practice... I’m going to squeeze your butt like that and kiss you!"
Silas stood there holding his broken wooden stick, looking down at the bold, blushing and completely shameless Dread Queen standing before him.
Inside his mind, Silas let out a slow degenerate smirk.
’A penalty where an SSS-Rank gorgeous pirate goddess squeezes my ass and kisses me every time I mess up...?’ Silas thought to himself with his golden-ringed eyes twinkling with playful mischief.
He tossed the broken wooden handle aside, picking up a fresh practice sword from the rack.
"Is that so?" Silas smirked, dropping back into his low stance. "Well then, Master... let’s clash again. I might just have to fail a few more times."
No...
Silas regretted agreeing to this punishment arrangement.
What he had originally assumed would be a fun flirtatious training incentive between a Lord and his SSS-Rank pirate goddess had devolved into something nothing short of pure hell.
CLANG! ZZZZZZT!
Their wooden swords collided once again in the center of the vault.
High-frequency, microscopic films of spinning water roared along the edges of both timber blades, spraying fine mist across the damp air as the friction generated a high-pitched buzzing drone.
"Hehehehahaha~"
Morwenna threw her head back, letting out a husky melodic laugh that echoed off the granite arches.
Hearing that hearty laugh, Silas couldn’t help but feel a cold terrifying chill run straight down his spine.
His muscles locked up, his Gold Core pumping liquid gold mana through his arm just to keep his wooden blade from getting deflected.
Truth be told, Silas was managing to hold his own against her strikes just fine.
His fluid stance was solid, his weight distribution between his boots was balanced, and his high-frequency water sheath was humming smoothly.
In fact... he was holding his own because he was genuinely terrified.
’If I let go of this momentum for even a fraction of a second...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes wide with frantic focus as sweat dripped down his temple. ’she is going to do it again.’

chapters.title: Chapter 264: Morwenna’s Lesson [IV]
paragraphs: Sure, the punishment deal had sounded cute and appealing the first and second time.
Getting kissed by an SSS-Rank gorgeous pirate after making a mistake during sword practice sounded like a dream come true for any man on Earth.
But the reality of Morwenna’s "punishment" was a complete nightmare.
A horrific memory from ten minutes ago flashed vividly through Silas’s mind.
During their third clash, Silas had miscalculated the rotational frequency of his water film, allowing Morwenna’s cutlass to chop his wooden blade in half.
The moment his sword broke, Morwenna let out a triumphant pirate cheer, lunged forward, and wrapped her long muscular fingers around his right butt cheek.
She hadn’t just given him a playful affectionate pinch.

With her unsuppressed SSS-Rank physical strength, Morwenna had grabbed his butt cheek so violently hard that Silas felt like his gluteus maximus was being compressed inside an industrial hydraulic vise.
It hurt so badly that tears had literally welled up in the corners of his eyes!
And worse yet... her kissing was garbage.
Morwenna had zero romantic finesse, zero soft delicacy, and zero understanding of how a human mouth functioned.

When she had pulled his face down to kiss him as a penalty, she had slammed her teeth directly against his lips, thrusting her tongue into his mouth with the raw chaotic force of a cannonball tearing through a ship’s hull.

... She didn’t know when to stop, she didn’t know how to breathe, and during her enthusiastic unrefined wrestling for dominance, she had gripped his tongue so aggressively that Silas felt like his tongue was about to get physically ripped out of his throat.
There was nothing he could do about it...
Against an immortal who possessed raw physical strength that could shatter battlecruisers, Silas was completely helpless whenever she locked her hands around his face.

’My ass cheek is literally bruised...’ Silas cried silently in his own mind with his teeth grinding together as he parried another strike. ’And my tongue is still numb! If I lose one more clash, she’s going to tear my lower lip off!’
ZIP!
Silas drove his back boot into the stone floor, executing a high-speed backward dash to create distance.
Morwenna’s gray eyes sparkled with playful disappointment as she watched him retreat.
She glided forward, her boots moving with fluid ocean-wave grace as she closed the gap effortlessly.
"Where are you going, Captain?" Morwenna teased, her raspy voice dripping with mischievous amusement.
CLANG! CLANG!
Their wooden swords collided two more times in rapid succession.
Silas was forced completely onto the defensive, sweeping his blade in tight circular parries just to deflect her relentless pressure.
"Come on, be a good boy for your master," Morwenna coaxed, offering him a broad toothy smirk. "Just drop your guard and let me kiss you again."
Morwenna stepped in, bringing her wooden sword around in a heavy horizontal execution slash meant to shear through his blade.
Silas’s Gold Core instincts flared.
Instead of meeting her strike head-on, Silas ducked his head low, letting her high-frequency blade whistle harmlessly inches above his dark hair.
SWOOSH!
While crouching beneath her swing, Silas drove his right heel into the granite and thrust his wooden longsword upward in a sharp, rising counter-cut aimed directly at her chest.
Morwenna’s eyes widened slightly in surprise.

Rather than blocking his rising strike with her cutlass which would have resulted in a heavy weapon clash... she smoothly leaned her upper body backward, executing an effortless backflip to disengage, landing lightly on her boots four paces away.
She stood there with her chest heaving softly under her leather tunic, staring at Silas with a complex conflicted expression in her stormy gray eyes.
Morwenna knew that if she had allowed her cutlass to collide with his rising blade just now... Silas’s high-frequency water sheath might have actually succeeded in repelling her strike.
’He’s improving way too quickly...’ Morwenna thought internally with her brow furrowing slightly as she looked at her Captain.
A subtle conflicting emotion churned inside her chest.

On one hand, her heart swelled with immense pride. Silas was the man she loved, the Lord she had chosen to serve, and seeing him absorb her centuries of refined martial arts in a matter of hours was proof of his genius.
On the other hand... it was slightly invalidating to her pride as a swordmaster.

She had spent centuries on the roaring high seas, fighting kraken lords and navy admirals, bleeding and sweating to perfect every nuance of the Tidal-Blade Arts... and Silas was picking up the mechanics after a few practice swings.
And more importantly... if he kept improving at this ridiculous rate, the spar was going to end.
’If he doesn’t make any more mistakes...’ Morwenna thought, her eyes dropping to the firm broad shape of his lower waist, ’then I won’t get to grab his butt anymore.’
Morwenna’s lips pouted slightly.
She genuinely enjoyed grabbing and squeezing his rear... It felt firm, muscular, and incredibly satisfying in her palms.

’Besides...’ Morwenna pondered in her own mind, thoroughly puzzled, ’I enjoy my butt being grabbed and squeezed by him... so shouldn’t he enjoy it when I do it to him? Why isn’t he moaning like I do? Why is he looking at me like I’m a demon coming to collect a debt?’
She tilted her head with her thoughts drifting to her kissing technique.
’And is my kissing really that bad...?’ Morwenna wondered innocently. ’I’m putting all my passion into it! I’m giving him 100% of my strength!’
Regardless of her internal confusion, Morwenna raised her wooden sword once more, her gray eyes flashing with playful determination.
"Let’s go again, Captain!" Morwenna called out, dropping back into her stance.
Silas didn’t reply to her teasing.
He stood five paces away with his golden-ringed eyes laser-focused on her wooden sword and the paper-thin high-frequency film of water spinning around its edge.

’As long as her sword stays intact...’ Silas calculated silently in his mind, his lips pressing into a thin determined line, ’I am in constant danger of getting my ass cheek mauled and my tongue ripped out.’
He had to end this spar... And he had to end it right now...!
STOMP!
Silas exploded forward across the granite floor with his wooden longsword humming with high-frequency water mana.
CLANG! BANG! ZZZZT!
The two warriors engaged in a high-speed exchange of sword strikes.
Wooden blades blurred through the damp vault air, leaving trails of pressurized water mist and blue light in their wake.
However, as the clash continued, Silas’s sharp mind noticed a glaring pattern in Morwenna’s movements.
Whenever Silas executed a strike that carried enough rotational force to potentially break her blade, Morwenna didn’t parry... she fluidly stepped back, dodged, or redirected his momentum.
She was deliberately avoiding any clash that could bring the spar to a conclusive end, deliberately dragging out the match so she could find another opening to punish him.
’She’s stalling on purpose...’ Silas thought with his eyebrows twitching in sheer exasperation. ’She’s actively hunting for a flaw so she can grab my rear again!’
Silas thinned his lips, his mind working at light speed to devise a solution.
’If she refuses to engage in a direct blade-breaking clash... then I’ll just have to force her into one. I need to trap her...’
Silas’s golden eyes glinted with wicked cunning strategy.
WHOOSH!
Mid-swing, Silas deliberately loosened his grip on his hilt by a fraction of an inch.
His lead foot dragged slightly against the stone floor, making his upper body sway as if his physical stamina was rapidly flagging.
He feigned a blunder.
Morwenna’s sharp gray eyes caught his sudden "stumble" instantly.
But as an experienced veteran, she didn’t immediately bite.
She maintained her distance, executing a cautious probing sweep with her cutlass to test if it was a trap.
Silas anticipated her caution.
He didn’t rush the play.
Over the next three sword exchanges, Silas deliberately allowed his water film to wobble, letting out heavy gasps of breath, making his footwork appear increasingly sluggish and exhausted.
Morwenna watched his ragged breathing and wobbly stance with her cautious restraint completely evaporating.
’He’s tired!’ Morwenna realized in her mind, her heart leaping with pure, unadulterated joy. ’His core reserves are flagging! It’s time!’
Morwenna couldn’t resist the temptation any longer... She completely threw her defensive caution to the wind, stepping forward with an explosive surge of footwork.

She brought her wooden cutlass back, preparing a heavy downward execution strike meant to shatter his weakened guard with her mind already anticipating the glorious feeling of her palms squeezing his firm butt cheeks once more.
’Got you, Captain!’ Morwenna cheered internally.
FWOOSH!
Morwenna brought her cutlass crashing down with maximum speed.
At that exact second—
The sluggish exhausted look on Silas’s face instantly vanished...
A confident and thoroughly wicked grin spread across his sharp features.
’No, Morwenna...’ Silas thought, his golden eyes blazing with golden light. ’Got YOU!’
Silas didn’t retreat... He tightened his calloused grip around his hilt like an iron vise, channeling a massive concentrated surge of his Gold Core mana directly into the wooden blade.
ZZZZZZZZZZZT!
Silas didn’t just maintain his water film... he violently accelerated the rotational velocity of his high-frequency water sheath by three hundred percent!
During their previous clashes, Silas had reached a profound physical realization regarding fluid dynamics.
High-frequency water rotation wasn’t just an offensive cutting tool.
If the rotational speed of the liquid film was raised to an extreme frequency, it created a centrifugal barrier.
When an opposing rotational blade struck it, the mismatched directional velocity would cause the incoming weapon to violently bounce off.
KA-BOOM!
Morwenna’s downward cutlass strike slammed flush into Silas’s hyper-accelerated water blade.
The moment the two high-frequency water films collided, the extreme difference in rotational velocity generated a violent backlash.
BANG!
Morwenna’s wooden cutlass was violently repelled backward.
The sudden overwhelming shockwave traveled up her arm, completely shattering her grip alignment and leaving her entire chest wide open to retaliation.
Morwenna’s stormy gray eyes widened to the size of dinner plates.
She was so thoroughly immersed in her thoughts of grabbing his rear that her brain couldn’t process her guard getting broken in time.
"Got you," Silas declared smoothly.
SWISH!
Silas didn’t hesitate. He executed a clean high-speed horizontal follow-up slash with his hyper-accelerated water blade!
SHING!
His wooden longsword glided effortlessly through her wooden sword.
The top half of Morwenna’s practice sword was cleanly severed, flying through the air and landing on the stone floor with a dull sound.
THUD!
The spar was officially over...
Morwenna staggered backward two steps with her body coming to a complete halt.
She stood there holding her half-length wooden stick, her mouth slightly agape as she stared at the clean cut across her weapon.
Silas let out a long and deeply relieved sigh. He lowered his practice sword, wiping a bead of sweat from his forehead.
Morwenna blinked, her cheeks turning a bright lovely shade of pink.
A sheepish and thoroughly flustered smile spread across her pale face.
"Fair... fair enough, Captain," Morwenna admitted softly, tossing her broken wooden handle aside.
She held her hands out, her gray eyes sparkling with playful surrender. "You got me fair and square! As your reward for winning... you can grab my butt all you want and kiss me as much as you like!"
Silas looked at her outstretched hands, then crossed his arms over his broad chest, offering her a cold and uncompromising stare.
"No," Silas rejected flatly.
Morwenna froze.
Her gray eyes blinked in total speechless shock.
"Huh...?" Morwenna gasped out, her mind completely short-circuiting. "N-No...?"

"You heard me. No," Silas repeated neutrally, resting his hand on his hip. "You were deliberately stalling the fight and dragging out the spar just so you could find excuses to punish me. As a penalty for your unsportsmanlike conduct... I am not going to touch you at all tonight."
Morwenna stood there in the center of the vault.
Hearing her Captain flatly refuse to touch her, her pale face flushed a deeper red.
Her lower lip began to tremble slightly, a rare heartbreaking look of genuine pouty rejection flickering across her stormy gray eyes.
"B-But..." Morwenna stammered softly, looking like a disappointed kitten whose favorite toy had just been taken away.
She stared at his golden eyes for three seconds, seeing his firm unshakeable stance... and then, suddenly, Morwenna threw her head back and burst into a hearty melodic laugh.
"AHAHAHA!" Morwenna laughed out loud, shaking her head as her pirate pride reclaimed her demeanor. "Fair enough, Captain! Fair enough!"
However... behind her hearty laughter, a deeply mischievous and thoroughly degenerate scheme began rapidly brewing inside the Dread Queen’s mind.

’He thinks he can avoid touching me tonight just because he won a spar...?’ Morwenna plotted silently in her thoughts, her gray eyes narrowing with desire. ’He forgets that we sleep in the exact same bed at night!’
Morwenna’s mind ran wild with glorious shameless plans.

’Tonight... once the torches are out... I am going to wrap my arms and legs entirely around his body! I am going to touch him, rub against him, and squeeze his chest as much as physically possible while he tries to sleep! I’ll do it so much that he’ll have no choice but to lose his patience and take aggressive revenge on me!’
And what would that "aggressive revenge" inevitably lead to...?
Morwenna looked down at her own long leather-clad legs.
Her knees suddenly trembled slightly with an intense wave of heat washing over her lower stomach as her heart hammered violently against her ribs.
’S-Sex...’ Morwenna thought, her face burning hot as a dizzying blush covered her entire neck. ’I... I want to feel him inside me so badly...’

STOMP!

ZZZZT!
The two warriors engaged in a high-speed exchange of sword strikes.

Whenever Silas executed a strike that carried enough rotational force to potentially break her blade, Morwenna didn’t parry... she fluidly stepped back, dodged, or redirected his momentum.

’She’s stalling on purpose...’ Silas thought with his eyebrows twitching in sheer exasperation. ’She’s actively hunting for a flaw so she can grab my rear again!’
Silas thinned his lips, his mind working at light speed to devise a solution.
’If she refuses to engage in a direct blade-breaking clash... then I’ll just have to force her into one.
I need to trap her...’
Silas’s golden eyes glinted with wicked cunning strategy.
WHOOSH!
Mid-swing, Silas deliberately loosened his grip on his hilt by a fraction of an inch.
His lead foot dragged slightly against the stone floor, making his upper body sway as if his physical stamina was rapidly flagging.
He feigned a blunder.

chapters.title: Chapter 265: Morwenna’s Lesson [V]
paragraphs: The Dread Queen cleared her throat loudly, forcefully slapping her cheeks with both hands to snap herself out of her shameless fantasy.
"Ahem! Right!" Morwenna announced, her voice slightly higher-pitched than usual.
She walked over to the weapon rack, picking up a fresh wooden training sword and handing another one to Silas. "Moving on! It’s time for the Second Style of the Tidal-Blade Arts!"
Silas took the wooden sword, raising an eyebrow. "Alright. What’s the name of the Second Style?"
Morwenna held her wooden blade in front of her, offering him a mysterious mischievous smirk.
"I’m not going to tell you the name just yet," Morwenna replied smoothly. "Only after I’m done with the live presentation will I reveal its name."
Silas thinned his lips, thoroughly suspicious. "Why the mystery?"
Morwenna didn’t explain. She simply dropped into a strange unusual combat stance, her raspy voice filled with an ominous warning.
"Just come at me with everything you’ve got, Captain. Because... this presentation is going to be quite painful for you. And while you attack... try your best to perceive what’s happening."
Silas looked at her serious expression, letting out a quiet sigh through his nose.
’As long as she doesn’t go after my ass cheek...’ Silas thought, ’it’s fine. A little physical pain during sword practice is normal.’
Silas raised his wooden blade, carefully analyzing Morwenna’s new stance.
Morwenna was holding her wooden cutlass unusually high... positioning the blade high above her right shoulder with her elbows flared outward.
To any trained martial artist, this stance was completely absurd.
By holding her sword that high, her lower torso, stomach, and ribs were left completely bare, wide open, and exposed to an immediate thrust or slash.
’It’s really going to hurt for Captain...’ Morwenna thought internally, feeling a brief pang of sympathy for him.
Truth be told, Morwenna actually disliked the Second Style slightly.

Out of all the various techniques in the Tidal-Blade Arts, the Second Style was the one that had taken her the longest time to master... requiring decades of intense atmospheric perception and core refinement back during her ocean days.
In a logical martial progression, a style this complex and painful should have been placed much later in the curriculum... perhaps as the Tenth or Eleventh Style.
But Morwenna loved variety!
In her mind, training should never be boring or predictable.
She preferred a rhythm where the First Style was easy, the Second Style was brutally hard, the Third Style was easy again, and the Fourth Style was a nightmare!
That chaotic unpredictable progression kept her mind sharp and her combat instinct razor-focused.
"Ready when you are, Captain!" Morwenna called out!
Silas didn’t hesitate.
Seeing her stomach left completely wide open and exposed by that bizarre high-sword stance, Silas’s instincts told him to exploit the opening immediately.
BOOM!

Silas exploded forward across the stone floor at high speed, he closed the distance in a fraction of a second, bringing his wooden longsword around in a devastating high-speed horizontal thrust aimed straight into her bare undefended stomach.
However...
That glaring undefended stomach opening was exactly what Morwenna wanted him to target.
The second Silas initiated his forward thrust—
Morwenna activated the technique!
’Tidal-Blade Second Style...’ Morwenna thought.
FWOOSH.
A subtle invisible pulse of high-pressure water mana erupted into the ambient air around Silas’s body.
To Silas, nothing seemed to change but to Morwenna... her entire perception of reality underwent a mind-boggling cosmic shift.
Time visually slowed down to a crawl.
In Morwenna’s hyper-focused perception, Silas’s high-speed forward thrust looked like a snail crawling through thick molasses.
But more importantly... the pressure-sensing water aura surrounding his body instantly highlighted dozens of microscopic flaws, delays, and structural weaknesses in his combat stance.

Lines of glowing blue light current materialized across Silas’s body in her vision... pointing to a slight weight imbalance in his left heel, a microscopic delay in his shoulder rotation, an open gap under his armpit, and an undefended rib alignment!
Naturally, Morwenna targeted the weakest and most vulnerable flaw!
ZIP!
Morwenna didn’t block his sword and she didn’t dodge backward.
Pressurized water mana violently erupted through her legs like a roaring ocean rip-current.
In an instantaneous terrifying burst of velocity that completely bypassed the concept of linear speed, Morwenna vanished from his line of sight.
BANG!
"UGHHH!" Silas let out a sharp painful groan of agony.
Before Silas’s brain could even register that she had moved, a brutal strike from her wooden cutlass slammed flush into his exposed left ribs.
The impact knocked the breath straight out of his lungs, sending him stumbling three paces forward.
Silas spun around, gasping for air, only to find Morwenna standing behind him with her back casually turned to him, her wooden sword resting on her shoulder.
’What the fuck...?!’ Silas thought, his golden eyes wide with utter shock. ’How did she get behind me?! I didn’t even see her pivot!’
Refusing to yield, Silas grit his teeth, reset his footing, and launched a second attack... He executed a lighting-fast diagonal slash aimed at her back.
SWISH!
Morwenna’s gray eyes glowed with a bright sapphire-blue light.
ZIP!
Time slowed down for her once more as she saw the new flaw in his wrist alignment instantly.
BANG!
"AGHH!" Silas groaned again as her wooden blade struck his right shoulder joint with pinpoint brutal precision, completely canceling his swing before the wood could even touch her clothes.
"Heh," Morwenna chuckled softly with her voice cool and relaxed.
Silas gritted his teeth, his Gold Core roaring as he launched a third ultra-fast thrust.
ZIP... BANG!
"URGH!" Silas groaned a third time as her blade struck his hip joint, throwing his balance entirely off.
Silas refused to give up as he gathered every ounce of his Gold Core speed, unleashing a furious four-hit combination slash.
ZIP... KRA-THOOM!

Morwenna didn’t just counter the fourth attack... she executed an instantaneous explosive rip-current step that brought her wooden cutlass slamming straight into the center of Silas’s solar plexus with catastrophic physical force!
"GHA-HAKK!"
The brutal blow completely knocked every single drop of air out of Silas’s lungs.
His vision flashed white, his knees buckled, and his wooden training sword slipped from his fingers, clattering against the granite floor.
CLATTER! THUD!
Silas collapsed flat onto his back on the cold stone floor, his chest heaving violently as he desperately wheezed for air with his entire body drained of physical energy.
"W-What... the... fuck... just happened...?" Silas wheezed out, his gravelly voice cracking as he stared up at the vaulted ceiling in total bewilderment.
Morwenna walked over, standing beside his fallen body, looking down at his sharp, wheezing face with a proud, breathtaking, and radiant smile that illuminated the torch-lit room.
"This," Morwenna announced softly. "is the Tidal-Blade Second Style: Rip-Current Perception."
She leaned down slightly, her stormy gray eyes sparkling with love and pride as she delivered the final truth of the style.
"And as you can tell, Captain... this technique allows me to see the future."
Silas laid in the center of the vault, holding his half-broken wooden practice sword while staring at Morwenna with a deadpan unimpressed expression.
"Future sight?" Silas raised an eyebrow. "I immediately call bullshit."
Morwenna froze for a fraction of a second, held her breath, and then threw her head back, bursting into a loud unrefined laugh that rattled the torch sconces.
"AHAHAHA!" Morwenna cackled, wiping a tear from her eye as she rested her wooden sword against her shoulder. "You caught me, Captain! I can’t actually see the future!"
Silas let out a dry exasperated breath, rolling his broad shoulders.
He was well aware of that.
How on earth could a fundamental manipulation of the water element allow someone to peer into the literal fabric of future time?
Time magic was a legendary near-mythical branch reserved for primordial cosmic entities, not a sword style developed on the high seas.

"I knew you were full of it," Silas muttered, crossing his arms over his broad chest. "So what were you actually doing just now? How did you dodge my thrust and hit my ribs four times in a row before my eyes could even track your boots?"
Morwenna’s laughter died down into a satisfied sharp smirk.
She took a step forward, tapping the tip of her wooden sword against the stone floor to emphasize her words.

"What you experienced wasn’t future sight, Captain," Morwenna explained. "It was pure swordsmanship... When I activate the Second Style, I release a dense microscopic field of water mana into the air surrounding us. Water naturally seeks out the lowest point which is the path of least resistance."
She gestured toward Silas’s torso with her blade.

"The second you shift your weight to initiate an attack, your muscles tense, your breathing pauses, and your internal mana flow experiences a microscopic lag," Morwenna continued clearly. "The water field around you senses that sudden drop in atmospheric pressure... To my eyes, your body lights up with clear, flowing current lines pointing directly into your exposed weaknesses before your sword even moves an inch."
Silas listened intently, his golden-ringed eyes narrowing as his sharp mind processed the mechanics.
"So you aren’t seeing what I will do ten seconds from now," Silas analyzed smoothly. "You’re reading the physical telegraphs my body makes before I even realize I’m making them."

"Precisely," Morwenna nodded with a proud glint shining in her stormy gray eyes. "Your brain sends the nervous signal to your arm, but before your muscle can contract, the water current has already delivered the answer to my blade. Combined with an explosive burst of rip-current footwork, I can slip into your flaw and strike before your guard can close."
Silas looked down at his calloused palms, shifting his grip on the wooden longsword.
"How do I learn it?" Silas asked directly, looking back up into her eyes. "How do I train my core to sense those fluid pressure drops?"
Morwenna let out a quiet sigh, looking at him with a complex, almost sympathetic expression.

"The ability to create openings, or to use water to view and exploit an opponent’s flaws in real-time... isn’t as easy as everything you’ve faced up until this moment, Captain," Morwenna warned him honestly.
She wasn’t exaggerating in the slightest.
The First Style of the Tidal-Blade Arts was simple momentum manipulation... a basic wave slash that required decent footwork and mana flow.
The Sub-Style was merely high-frequency rotation... a technical trick to eliminate surface friction.
To a natural monster like Silas, who possessed Gold Core and an insane comprehension speed, those two were mere child’s play.

"If you manage to learn the Second Style in less than a single day," Morwenna grumbled, crossing her arms defensively over her chest, "I swear on the seven seas, I will officially quit being a swordmaster. It took me decades of bloody combat on the ocean just to perfect this single style."
Silas chuckled dryly, but didn’t argue. He could respect the sheer, painstaking effort it took to invent a style from scratch.
Morwenna looked away, her gray eyes staring blankly at the stone wall as old dusty memories from her past resurfaced in her mind.
Truth be told, Morwenna had never considered herself a true master of the blade.
Back during her early years before she awakened her power, she had met countless prodigies, martial geniuses, and legendary swordsmen who possessed far superior innate talent than her.
Naturals who could master sword styles in their sleep.
...But talent didn’t mean a damn thing if you ended up dead in a ditch.
And almost every single one of those talented prodigies she had known in her youth was long dead, buried beneath the ocean bed or turned to dust by the passage of centuries.
Except for one.
Morwenna’s jaw tightened with her fingers clenching into a tight fist as a sudden, intense spike of cold irritation flared in her chest.
’That fucking bastard...’ Morwenna cursed silently in her mind. ’The Sword God.’
Centuries ago, before the ocean claimed her, Morwenna and that insufferable man had been fellow disciples under the exact same legendary master.

While Morwenna had relied on gritty survival instincts and relentless repetition to build her Tidal-Blade Arts, he had been a natural terrifying monster who could cut down mountains with a flick of his wrist.
She wondered... if fate ever brought them face-to-face again in this modern era, and her ocean sword style went head-to-head against his absolute cutting path... who would walk away victorious?
’Meh, it’ll probably be me.’
