"...We did Standing Carry against the wall, we did the Mating Press, we did Sideways, and we did three different variations I don’t even have names for yet.
My Lord knows many..."
Morwenna stood there in the doorway with her mouth slightly open, her brain completely flatlining as she listened to the Nature Goddess detail her entire nocturnal itinerary.
Eluned then turned to face her directly, placing her hands beneath her chest and gently lifting her petite breasts.
Her delicate pink nipples were flushed, swollen, and surrounded by distinct dark red bite marks.
"And look here," Eluned continued with an extraordinarily smug grin, her green eyes sparkling with pure victory.
"This is where my Lord bit me repeatedly, sucking on me as if he were frantically searching for breast milk.
Even though my chest is smaller than yours... he was far more obsessed with mine than he could ever possibly be with yours."
Eluned raised her hand, gesturing to the right side of her neck, her pale back, and her delicate belly button... all of which carried bite marks and dark red hickeys etched directly into her flesh.
Eluned stepped forward, taking a plush white towel and wrapping it around her waist.
She looked at Morwenna’s pale, speechless face, offering the Dread Queen a sweet waving gesture with her hand as if shooing away a minor pest.
"In short, Morwenna..." Eluned announced, her voice filled with undisputed triumph, "...I officially have a hubby now.
And you... are still a virgin.
So shoo, shoo.
Go away.
When you finally manage to lose your virginity... then you may come back and talk to me as an equal."
Morwenna stood frozen in the bathroom doorway.
The color completely drained from the Dread Queen’s face, leaving her looking paler than a ghost.
She had survived centuries of brutal ocean warfare... yet right now, looking at the smug towel-clad Nature Goddess standing before her, Morwenna realized the devastating truth.
She had been completely out-maneuvered, out-schemed, and left behind in the absolute dust by this terrifying yandere deity.
’I want to have sex too...!’
Meanwhile, on the top floor of the Keep...
CREAK!
Aeli gently pushed open the heavy oak door to Silas’s private executive office.
Sitting behind his broad mahogany desk, bathed in the warm golden sunlight pouring through the floor-to-ceiling windows, was Silas.
He was wearing a crisp, long-sleeved dark shirt buttoned neat at his wrists, paired with tailored black trousers.
His short dark hair was combed back, his posture upright, and his sharp handsome features radiated an effortless commanding intelligence.
Seeing his silver-haired arcanist step into the room, Silas looked up from his desk, a warm, confident smile touching his lips.
"Good morning, Lord Silas," Aeli greeted him warmly, bowing her head politely as she held a glass pitcher filled with fresh golden fruit juice.
"Good morning, Aeli," Silas greeted her back.
In truth, Silas was feeling like an entirely new man today.
And technically... he was.

Inside his chest, his newly evolved Royal Gold Core was pulsing with liquid gold energy, having officially broken through to Stage 2 of Core Advancement, permanently expanding his maximum mana pool to a staggering 30,000 points.
And on top of that physical breakthrough... he had officially taken Eluned as his wife, spending the entire night engaged in wild passionate lovemaking until the break of dawn.
’Hehe...’ Silas chuckled internally, a wave of satisfaction washing over his mind.
He almost let out an audible laugh, but caught himself in time, maintaining his cool professional composure behind his desk.
’If Elu doesn’t mind having kids eventually...’ Silas reflected in his thoughts. ’I certainly don’t mind either.
A family sounds nice.’
However... a sudden concern flickered in the back of Silas’s mind.
He remembered the fundamental laws of the Blessed Land territory.
The territory had strictly enforced a female-only rule for all resident units.

’Wait a minute...’ Silas thought with his dark eyebrows pulling together slightly. ’If Elu eventually gives birth to a child... and that child turns out to be a boy... would the territory’s system laws try to forcibly eradicate or banish my own son from the domain?’
That would be a nightmare.
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He silently invoked his system interface, submitting an immediate direct query to his Upgrade system.
’System,’ Silas queried in his mind. ’Clarify territory population laws regarding direct lineage.
If a male child is born to the Lord, how does the domain aura react?’
A sleek translucent blue holographic tab instantly materialized in his field of vision:
[System Query Processing...]

[Territory Rule Clarification: While external male entities are strictly prohibited from establishing residency within the Blessed Land (excluding non-human mounts and beast assets), an exemption exists for the Lord’s direct biological bloodline.]
[Notice: Any biological children or direct blood relatives produced by the Lord inherit the Sovereign’s Authority, granting them unrestricted residency and full immunity to territorial rejection.]
Reading the blue text, Silas let out a long quiet breath of genuine relief.
"Phew..." Silas exhaled softly.
Aeli, who was walking up to his desk with a glass of fresh juice, paused.
She looked at him with curious silver eyes, tilting her head.
"What was that sigh for, My Lord?" Aeli asked gently.
"Are you feeling unwell?"
Silas looked up at her, offering a warm genuine smile that made her heart skip three beats.
"Nothing at all, Aeli," Silas answered smoothly.
"I’m just really glad to see you this morning."
Aeli’s pale cheeks instantly flushed a bright, lovely shade of pink.
Her silver ears twitched shyly as she hurriedly set the glass of fresh golden fruit juice onto his desk.
I brought you some fresh Basin fruit juice, My Lord!" Aeli reported quickly, her voice trembling with sweet flustered excitement.
"I prepared it myself using Kaelia’s special recipe!"
Silas looked at the glass of golden juice sitting on his desk.
He looked at the liquid, then looked back up at Aeli’s blushing face, an eyebrow twitching slightly as a wave of post-traumatic caution washed over his mind.
After getting drugged into oblivion by Eluned last night, Silas was taking zero chances with unknown drinks.
Silas squinted his golden eyes playfully, asking in a deadpan voice.
"Aeli... you didn’t happen to spike or drug this drink, did you?"
Aeli went completely rigid.
Her eyes widened in shock and her face exploded into a burning red flush as she frantically waved her hands in front of her chest.
"N-NO!
OF COURSE NOT!" Aeli squeaked out frantically, her voice reaching a high-pitched adorable squeak.
"I WOULD NEVER DRUG YOU, MY LORD!
WHY...
WHY WOULD YOU ASK SUCH A HORRIBLE QUESTION?!"
Silas looked at her innocent reaction, let out a soft chuckle, and picked up the glass.
"Just making sure," Silas smiled.
"You can never be too careful in this Keep nowadays."
Silas brought the glass to his lips, taking a long refreshing gulp of the sweet, chilled fruit juice.
It tasted light and completely free of any divine slumber-herbs.
GULP!
Silas set the empty glass back down, letting out a satisfied breath.
"That was delicious, Aeli.
Thank you."
Aeli beamed proudly, clutching her hands behind her back.
"I’m glad you liked it, My Lord!"
Silas leaned back in his leather chair, crossing his hands over his desk, his tone shifting into business mode.
"So, Aeli," Silas began, "what is our official schedule for the territory today?"
Aeli instantly straightened her posture, taking on her role as his primary secretary.
’Speaking of Secretary...
Kadi should be coming soon.’
"As you instructed yesterday, My Lord," Aeli reported clearly, "today is dedicated entirely to territory renovation and structural expansion.
We need to prepare our living facilities for the incoming recruits and upgrade our internal infrastructure before war day."
"Right," Silas nodded.
Silas swiped his right hand through the air, summoning his Sovereign Realm territory interface.
He navigated directly to the Architectural Blueprint Menu... the construction tab he had unlocked when the Blessed Land officially reached Level 10.
A sleek glowing blue holographic tab materialized directly over his desk, displaying dozens of available civic, military, and residential blueprints.
Silas scrolled past the automated ballista arrays and basic stone walls, stopping at the residential section.
His eyes locked onto a specific blueprint.
[Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters]
[Type: Residential Infrastructure]

[Structure Overview: A three-story, reinforced multi-unit residential building featuring forty individual private suites, soundproofed living quarters, private washrooms, and climate-control rune arrays.]
[Materials Required: 600 Units of Ironwood Beams, 300 Units of Obsidian-Slate Stone.]
[Description: Upgrades the territory’s living standards from communal group barracks to private individual suites.
Drastically boosts resident morale, physical recovery rates, and privacy.]
Silas scanned the detailed requirements, nodding his head in deep satisfaction.
"This is perfect," Silas muttered aloud, his golden eyes analyzing the wireframe diagram.
While the Barracks were fantastic for military drills, group briefings, and housing new recruits during their initial orientation...
Silas knew that long-term, his elite female soldiers deserved proper, private living spaces where they could rest without sleeping in a crowded sixty-person room.
"Six hundred units of Ironwood Beams and three hundred units of Obsidian-Slate Stone..." Silas calculated in his mind.
He checked his current inventory reserves.
Thanks to Eluned’s massive timber harvests from the Umbral Basin treeline, Silas possessed over eight hundred units of raw Ironwood stored in his spatial inventory.
The wood requirement was completely covered.
...However, he had zero units of Obsidian-Slate Stone.

Obsidian-Slate was a dense, fire-resistant, and highly magic-conductive stone quarried primarily from deep volcanic ridges... a material that wasn’t naturally abundant in the immediate vicinity of his Territory.
Silas leaned his chin on his palm, a thoughtful sly smirk spreading across his face.
"I don’t have the stone..." Silas mused drily to himself, "...but that doesn’t mean Lord Sky doesn’t have a massive mountain of it sitting inside the lower holds of his rolling war-rig."
Sky ran a massive multi-million-credit streaming empire.
A Classic Lord like him undoubtedly carried heavy construction bundles, refined stone crates, and raw building materials in his mobile fortress’s supply holds.
Silas looked up from his blueprint screen with his golden eyes fixing onto Aeli.
A slow and meaningful smile spread across Silas’s features... a smile that made Aeli’s heart flutter wildly against her ribs.
"Aeli..." Silas asked softly.
"...would you like to grow stronger?"
Aeli’s silver eyes widened to the size of dinner plates.
Her breath caught in her throat.

She instantly remembered what Silas had done for Tasmin and Brida not too long ago... how he had placed his hand on them, ignited his golden aura, and forcefully mutated their baseline abilities, transforming them into terrifying S-Rank combatants.
Aeli took a step forward, her silver eyes glowing with fierce unshakeable determination as she nodded her head vigorously.
"Yes, My Lord!" Aeli answered passionately, her voice ringing clearly through the office.
"I want to get stronger!
I want to get so much stronger so I can protect you and serve you better!"
Silas chuckled warmly, nodding his head.
"Good.
Then let’s do this properly."
Silas reached into his inventory, checking his Upgrade Point balance...
PING!
[Current UP Balance: 1,240 UP]
He had more than enough points saved up from yesterday’s massive monster raids to execute two full S-Rank evolutionary ascensions.
"Aeli," Silas instructed, "go fetch Rowenna.
I’m going to upgrade the two of you together before—"
Before Silas could even finish his sentence—
"YES, MY LORD!" Aeli shouted happily.
Without waiting for him to complete his words, the silver-haired elven arcanist spun on her heel, sprinted out of the office door, and the second her boots crossed the threshold—
FLASH!
Aeli triggered her short-range spatial teleportation, vanishing from the hallway in a brilliant burst of silver light.
Silas sat behind his desk, his hand still extended in mid-air, staring at the empty doorway where Aeli had been standing a second ago.
Silas let out a short amused laugh, resting his hand back on the mahogany wood, tapping his fingers rhythmically against the desk.
"Man..." Silas chuckled softly to himself, his golden eyes glinting with genuine pride.
"I really love how excited they get about gaining power."
Upgrading Aeli and Rowenna to full S-Rank status was a critical tactical move.

Elevating both of his primary casters to S-Rank would give the Blessed Land an god-tier magical backline... further guaranteeing that next week’s official Lord War against "The Unmovable Wall" would end in a complete overwhelming landslide victory.
Silas leaned his head back against his leather chair, staring up at the ceiling rafters with a thoughtful smirk.
"Now then..." Silas mused, his mind shifting to his next objective.
"...how exactly should I approach Lord Sky to trade for those three hundred units of Obsidian-Slate stone...?"
[Author’s Note]
Happy new month in advance and I’m grateful for the support heh, let me go plan my mass release.
See you guys tomorrow.
Tch, might as well gift a castle or two this new month.

chapters.title: Chapter 277: Girls Being Girls
paragraphs: Rowenna sat upright on the edge of her wooden cot inside the barracks, both of her hands buried deep in her hair as she stared blankly at the floorboards.
The morning sun had barely crested the eastern ridges of the Umbral Basin, casting pale golden shafts of light through the high barracks windows.
Around her, the quiet breathing of sleeping recruits echoed softly through the long dormitory wing.
Yet, Rowenna’s mind was spinning in a chaotic storm of frustration.
She was still desperately trying to figure out how in the world she had fallen asleep yesterday evening.

One moment she had been standing near the Keep’s courtyard after returning from scouting, and the next moment she was waking up at dawn flat on her back with a dull persistent ache throbbing behind her temples.
A high-tier spell cast...
’It had to be.’
Rowenna raised her right palm with her fingers flexing as she channeled her internal pool of arcane mana.
CRACKLE!
A delicate glowing violet runic circle materialized three inches above her palm.

The intricate geometric circles rotated smoothly, pulsing with a low-frequency hum as Rowenna attempted to reconstruct the residual atmospheric signature that had washed over the territory last night.

She cycled her mana through the rune, trying to force the array to isolate the specific frequency of the sleep aura... but the violet light merely flickered, wobbled, and dissolved into fine harmless sparks.
"Tch... it’s not strong enough," Rowenna cursed softly under her breath, her jaw tightening in bitter disappointment.
Her current runic capabilities as a B-Rank caster were certainly nothing to scoff at.
She could inscribe elemental traps, reinforce physical armor, and dismantle standard magic circles with relative ease.
...But last night had proven the limits of her current standing.
If a high-tier sleeping spell or an advanced spatial anomaly targeted the Blessed Land without leaving a visible physical casting circle on the ground, Rowenna was completely powerless to counter it.

She couldn’t dispel what her eyes couldn’t break down. If an enemy Lord deployed a similar wide-area neutralization field during the war, her entire backline would be neutralized before they could even draw their staffs.
A warm calloused hand rested firmly against Rowenna’s left shoulder.
Rowenna flinched slightly, snapping her head up from her cot, standing directly beside her bed was Tasmin.
Rowenna swallowed hard, her throat going dry as her blue eyes locked onto the Shadow Commander.
Under the crisp morning light, Tasmin looked dangerously beautiful.

The bright silver-white streaks woven through her dark hair glistened like spun moon-silk, her luminous silver eyes carried a sharp glint, and her tall athletic frame radiated a cold aura that made the surrounding air feel noticeably denser.
Yet, despite her intimidating physical presence, Tasmin looked down at the runic caster with a look of genuine quiet concern.
"Is something troubling you, Rowenna?" Tasmin asked softly. "You’ve been glaring at your palm like it owes you money for the last ten minutes."
Rowenna quickly closed her fist, extinguishing the lingering violet sparks, and looked away toward the far wall.
"Nothing is wrong, Tasmin. Just waking up."
Tasmin didn’t remove her hand from Rowenna’s shoulder.
She raised a single dark eyebrow, giving the runic caster a sharp deadpan stare that clearly communicated she wasn’t buying the lie for a single microsecond.
Rowenna held out for three seconds under that intense silver glare before letting out a long, defeated breath, running her fingers through her dark hair once more.

"I’m just... annoyed," Rowenna admitted quietly, her voice laced with deep, lingering insecurity. "I’m annoyed that I wasn’t strong enough to detect or dispel whatever hit us last night. I’m a mage after all. When high-tier threats show up, or when strange magical anomalies target our Territory... I feel like a liability. I feel like I’m holding everyone back."
Hearing her honest confession, Tasmin’s sharp features softened completely.
A rare, genuine, and extraordinarily warm smile spread across the assassin’s lips... a smile so striking and unexpectedly gentle that Rowenna felt her heart melt slightly inside her chest.

"You’re plenty strong, Rowenna," Tasmin assured her smoothly, her silver eyes holding unwavering conviction. "You’re strong in your own right... None of us could operate at full capacity without your work."
Tasmin leaned down slightly, her voice dropping into a reassuring whisper.
"And if you really feel like you’ve hit your natural physical limit as a B-Rank... our Lord will know. When the time is right, he will upgrade you."
Tasmin knew firsthand the reality-bending miracle of Silas’s power after all.
She had been a simple C-Rank Wilderness Huntress before Silas had placed his hand on her shoulder, ignited his Gold Core, and transformed her into an S-Rank Shadow Commander.
Rowenna looked up into Tasmin’s confident face, feeling a massive wave of emotional relief wash over her chest.
The heavy weight that had been pressing down on her shoulders since dawn seemed to lighten instantly.
"Thank you, Tasmin," Rowenna said genuinely, offering a small, appreciative smile. "I needed to hear that."
"Don’t mention it," Tasmin smiled back.
Then, her tone instantly shifted as she patted Rowenna’s shoulder with a sudden eager glint flickering in her silver eyes.
"Now then... since you’re wide awake and feeling better, I need your help with my morning training routine."
Rowenna tilted her head, slightly intrigued. "Your training? What kind of training are you doing inside the barracks?"
Before Tasmin could answer—
"Haauuuu~"
From two cots over, a massive muscular figure sat up on her mattress, stretching her broad arms wide while letting out a loud and thoroughly unrefined yawn that echoed off the ceiling rafters.
Brida wiped a thin line of drool from the corner of her mouth with the back of her hand, rubbing her brown eyes as her heavy iron shield rested against her bedframe.
She looked over at Tasmin and Rowenna, blinking groggily.
"What are you two whispering about so early in the morning?" Brida grunted, her deep voice full with sleep.
Tasmin and Rowenna slowly turned their heads, staring at the disheveled Titan Bastion in total deadpan silence.
"You really are quite a character, Brida," Rowenna muttered drily, shaking her head.
Brida snapped her head up, pointing a thick finger at them in offended outrage.
"Hey! What the hell is that supposed to mean?!"
Tasmin completely ignored the giant warrior, standing up from Rowenna’s cot.
Rowenna offered a shy quiet chuckle, standing up as well as they began walking out of the main dormitory wing toward an empty, reinforced stone training room located at the rear of the barracks.
Brida scrambled off her cot, pulling on her leather boots as she stomped after them down the hallway.
"Hey! Don’t just ignore me!" Brida grumbled, trailing behind them like a giant, curious bear. "Where are you two going anyway?"
Rowenna shrugged her shoulders as she pushed open the heavy oak door to the empty training chamber. "Don’t ask me. Tasmin just dragged me along."
They stepped into the square, thirty-foot stone chamber.
The room was completely empty... built specifically for high-intensity physical sparring, featuring reinforced granite walls and shock-absorbing floor mats designed to handle impact.
Tasmin walked straight into the center of the room, stopping in front of Rowenna.
"I need to train my physical movement under extreme environmental pressure," Tasmin explained, her voice taking on a serious tone. "So I want you to drop a 10x Gravity Well directly on top of me."
Rowenna paused, her blue eyes widening in genuine surprise.
"10x gravity? Are you sure, Tasmin? Ten times normal gravitational downforce will crush a person’s internal organs if their physical core isn’t prepared."
Tasmin offered her a sharp confident smirk with her silver eyes flashing.
"I’m positive."
Without another word, Tasmin reached up with both hands, unbuttoning her dark leather tunic and slipping it off her shoulders.
FLOP!
She tossed the heavy tunic onto a bench near the door, leaving her upper body clad only in a tight dark-red leather sports bra that hugged her toned chest and defined abdominal muscles.
Then, she reached down, unbuckling her dark trousers and stepping out of them, tossing them onto her coat.
She stood in the center of the room wearing only her dark sports bra and a pair of tight dark athletic briefs, revealing her long muscular legs and sculpted waist.
Rowenna stood near the doorway, staring at the half-naked Shadow Commander with a massive mental sweatdrop forming on the back of her head.
’Is this a training room or a strip club...?’ Rowenna thought in deadpan disbelief.
Brida pushed her way through the doorway, seeing Tasmin stripped down to her undergarments, and her brown eyes lit up with sudden excitement.
"Oh! High-intensity physical conditioning?" Brida grinned cheekily. "Count me in!"
Tasmin turned her silver eyes toward the Titan Bastion, giving her a skeptical and thoroughly unimpressed look.
"Brida," Tasmin pointed out drily, "you’re an S-Rank with a class that deals with your physical body. Why the fuck would you need to do gravity conditioning with me?"
Brida opened her mouth to argue, but completely failed to come up with a logical comeback.
"Shut up! I do what I want!" Brida grumbled defensively.
Without a shred of hesitation, Brida reached up, yanking her thick leather chest-piece over her head in one swift motion.
THUD!
The heavy leather hit the floorboards, revealing a massive heavy sports bra that strained to contain her voluminous heavy breasts.
Brida then unbuckled her armored trousers, pulling them down to reveal a pair of dark, tight athletic shorts.
Rowenna noticed that unlike Tasmin, Brida wasn’t wearing standard underwear beneath her shorts.
"Haah... I like shorts." Brida said, noticing her look.
Brida had completely quit wearing traditional cotton panties days ago.
Because she engaged in a subconscious physical conditioning routine while sleeping to hone her combat instincts, her body generated massive amounts of heat and sweat throughout the night.
Whenever she woke up, standard cotton panties would be completely soaked through with sweat... making it look like she had embarrassingly wet her bed.
’Tasmin pointed it out... never again...’
Tight, moisture-wicking athletic shorts at least managed to contain the sweat without looking ridiculous, even if they smelled slightly funky and salty before her morning shower.
Brida stepped into the center of the room alongside Tasmin, resting her broad hands against her hips.
She proudly flexed her back muscles, admiring her own reflection in the polished granite wall.
"Man..." Brida mused out loud, her brown eyes twinkling with a sudden shameless thought, "...I wonder what it would feel like to get rammed in by our Lord and bred until morning?"
Rowenna’s face instantly flushed a bright, burning crimson at the crude, out-of-nowhere question.
Tasmin, however, didn’t flinch. She adjusted her leather briefs, offering a calm, pragmatic answer.

"We have to prove our potential and make ourselves valuable in order to bear his children first," Tasmin stated flatly. "We aren’t a Goddess like Lady Eluned, nor are we like Morwenna. We are ourselves. As long as we become indispensable assets to his empire... getting bred by him is just a matter of time."
Tasmin turned her silver eyes toward Brida’s rear, rolling her eyes with a scoff.
"Though honestly, sweatshop... your ass isn’t even that good."
Brida’s jaw dropped in theatrical outrage.
"Oho!" Brida gasped, placing her broad palm against her right butt cheek.
PAH!
Brida spanked her own rear cheek hard, sending a visible ripple running across her firm, curvaceous cheek even through her dark athletic shorts.
"My ass is far better than yours, shadow-girl!" Brida declared proudly. "You got upgraded to S-Rank and all it gave you was some extra hip fat... Look at these curves!"
Brida wasn’t necessarily wrong.

When Silas had upgraded Brida to S-Rank, her Titan Bastion class had enhanced her tall, muscular, and hourglass proportions to perfection... giving her a plump, sculpted rear that put most warriors to shame.
Tasmin’s S-Rank evolution had certainly enhanced her hips and waist as well, but compared to Brida’s heavy, muscular curves, Tasmin was far more streamlined for high-speed assassination.
Tasmin simply flicked Brida off with her middle finger, refusing to waste another second arguing about butt sizes.
She turned back to Rowenna, taking a deep breath.
"Alright, Rowenna. Fire up the gravity."
Rowenna nodded, pushing her insecurities aside as she raised her right hand.
"Runic Gravity Well: 10x!" Rowenna commanded!
CRACKLE... FWOOSH!
A massive eight-foot-wide glowing violet rune instantly flared to life on the stone floorboards beneath Tasmin and Brida’s boots!
KA-THOOM!
The second the violet array activated, a terrifying invisible wave of ten-fold gravitational downforce slammed down onto the room like a falling mountain.

Rowenna offered a shy quiet chuckle, standing up as well as they began walking out of the main dormitory wing toward an empty, reinforced stone training room located at the rear of the barracks.
Brida scrambled off her cot, pulling on her leather boots as she stomped after them down the hallway.
"Hey!
Don’t just ignore me!" Brida grumbled, trailing behind them like a giant, curious bear.
"Where are you two going anyway?"
Rowenna shrugged her shoulders as she pushed open the heavy oak door to the empty training chamber.
"Don’t ask me.
Tasmin just dragged me along."
They stepped into the square, thirty-foot stone chamber.
The room was completely empty... built specifically for high-intensity physical sparring, featuring reinforced granite walls and shock-absorbing floor mats designed to handle impact.
Tasmin walked straight into the center of the room, stopping in front of Rowenna.
"I need to train my physical movement under extreme environmental pressure," Tasmin explained, her voice taking on a serious tone.
"So I want you to drop a 10x Gravity Well directly on top of me."
Rowenna paused, her blue eyes widening in genuine surprise.
"10x gravity?
Are you sure, Tasmin?
Ten times normal gravitational downforce will crush a person’s internal organs if their physical core isn’t prepared."
Tasmin offered her a sharp confident smirk with her silver eyes flashing.
"I’m positive."
Without another word, Tasmin reached up with both hands, unbuttoning her dark leather tunic and slipping it off her shoulders.
FLOP!
She tossed the heavy tunic onto a bench near the door, leaving her upper body clad only in a tight dark-red leather sports bra that hugged her toned chest and defined abdominal muscles.
Then, she reached down, unbuckling her dark trousers and stepping out of them, tossing them onto her coat.
She stood in the center of the room wearing only her dark sports bra and a pair of tight dark athletic briefs, revealing her long muscular legs and sculpted waist.
Rowenna stood near the doorway, staring at the half-naked Shadow Commander with a massive mental sweatdrop forming on the back of her head.
’Is this a training room or a strip club...?’ Rowenna thought in deadpan disbelief.
Brida pushed her way through the doorway, seeing Tasmin stripped down to her undergarments, and her brown eyes lit up with sudden excitement.
"Oh!
High-intensity physical conditioning?" Brida grinned cheekily.
"Count me in!"
Tasmin turned her silver eyes toward the Titan Bastion, giving her a skeptical and thoroughly unimpressed look.
"Brida," Tasmin pointed out drily, "you’re an S-Rank with a class that deals with your physical body.
Why the fuck would you need to do gravity conditioning with me?"
Brida opened her mouth to argue, but completely failed to come up with a logical comeback.
"Shut up!
I do what I want!" Brida grumbled defensively.
Without a shred of hesitation, Brida reached up, yanking her thick leather chest-piece over her head in one swift motion.
THUD!
The heavy leather hit the floorboards, revealing a massive heavy sports bra that strained to contain her voluminous heavy breasts.
Brida then unbuckled her armored trousers, pulling them down to reveal a pair of dark, tight athletic shorts.
Rowenna noticed that unlike Tasmin, Brida wasn’t wearing standard underwear beneath her shorts.
"Haah...
I like shorts." Brida said, noticing her look.
Brida had completely quit wearing traditional cotton panties days ago.
Because she engaged in a subconscious physical conditioning routine while sleeping to hone her combat instincts, her body generated massive amounts of heat and sweat throughout the night.
Whenever she woke up, standard cotton panties would be completely soaked through with sweat... making it look like she had embarrassingly wet her bed.
’Tasmin pointed it out... never again...’
Tight, moisture-wicking athletic shorts at least managed to contain the sweat without looking ridiculous, even if they smelled slightly funky and salty before her morning shower.
Brida stepped into the center of the room alongside Tasmin, resting her broad hands against her hips.
She proudly flexed her back muscles, admiring her own reflection in the polished granite wall.
"Man..." Brida mused out loud, her brown eyes twinkling with a sudden shameless thought, "...I wonder what it would feel like to get rammed in by our Lord and bred until morning?"
Rowenna’s face instantly flushed a bright, burning crimson at the crude, out-of-nowhere question.
Tasmin, however, didn’t flinch.
She adjusted her leather briefs, offering a calm, pragmatic answer.
"We have to prove our potential and make ourselves valuable in order to bear his children first," Tasmin stated flatly.
"We aren’t a Goddess like Lady Eluned, nor are we like Morwenna.
We are ourselves.
As long as we become indispensable assets to his empire... getting bred by him is just a matter of time."
Tasmin turned her silver eyes toward Brida’s rear, rolling her eyes with a scoff.
"Though honestly, sweatshop... your ass isn’t even that good."
Brida’s jaw dropped in theatrical outrage.
"Oho!" Brida gasped, placing her broad palm against her right butt cheek.
PAH!
Brida spanked her own rear cheek hard, sending a visible ripple running across her firm, curvaceous cheek even through her dark athletic shorts.
"My ass is far better than yours, shadow-girl!" Brida declared proudly.
"You got upgraded to S-Rank and all it gave you was some extra hip fat...
Look at these curves!"
Brida wasn’t necessarily wrong.

When Silas had upgraded Brida to S-Rank, her Titan Bastion class had enhanced her tall, muscular, and hourglass proportions to perfection... giving her a plump, sculpted rear that put most warriors to shame.
Tasmin’s S-Rank evolution had certainly enhanced her hips and waist as well, but compared to Brida’s heavy, muscular curves, Tasmin was far more streamlined for high-speed assassination.
Tasmin simply flicked Brida off with her middle finger, refusing to waste another second arguing about butt sizes.
She turned back to Rowenna, taking a deep breath.
"Alright, Rowenna.
Fire up the gravity."
Rowenna nodded, pushing her insecurities aside as she raised her right hand.
"Runic Gravity Well: 10x!" Rowenna commanded!
CRACKLE...
FWOOSH!
A massive eight-foot-wide glowing violet rune instantly flared to life on the stone floorboards beneath Tasmin and Brida’s boots!
KA-THOOM!
The second the violet array activated, a terrifying invisible wave of ten-fold gravitational downforce slammed down onto the room like a falling mountain.

chapters.title: Chapter 278: Aeli’s Upgrade
paragraphs: The atmospheric pressure inside the room instantly shifted, turning the air misty red to their eyes... a natural sensory phenomenon caused by the sudden extreme blood pressure spike in their eyes.
"Ghk...!" Tasmin’s knees buckled slightly with her breath catching in her throat as ten times her physical body weight pressed down on her shoulders.
Beside her, Brida let out a sharp grunt, her heavy boots sinking two inches into the shock-absorbing floor mats.
Ten times gravity was no joke.
Even for an S-Rank warrior, having your internal organs, your blood, and your muscle tissue suddenly weigh ten times their natural mass was a brutal disorienting experience.
’But it feels good as well...’ Tasmin thought.
Rowenna watched them nervously from the doorway.
In her pocket, she carried the amulet Silas had given her yesterday.
She briefly wondered if she should use it to increase the gravity, but quickly decided against it... she knew Tasmin and Brida were testing their true limits.
’Besides I’m not trying to kill them, am I?’
Brida had completely underestimated the sheer downforce of 10x gravity, but her pride refused to let her yield.
"Tch... piece of cake!" Brida growled through gritted teeth.
Brida dropped flat onto her hands and toes, assuming a wide push-up position on the glowing violet rune.
Her heavy un-bound breasts hung down, locked rigid under the intense gravitational pull, but she locked her core and began slowly lowering her chest toward the floorboards.
"One... Lord... Silas..." Brida grunted out, her arms trembling violently as she pushed her heavy frame back up.
"Two... Lord... Silas..." Brida counted out slowly, her muscles burning as she fought the ten-fold downforce.
Beside her, Tasmin didn’t do standard push-ups.
The Shadow Commander drove her palms into the floor, kicked her long legs straight up into the air, and assumed a vertical handstand position against 10x gravity.
"Hnnn-gh...!" Tasmin gritted her teeth, her silver eyes glowing as sweat instantly beaded across her forehead.
Tasmin slowly bent her elbows, lowering her head toward the floor, and then forced her shoulders to push her entire ten-fold body weight back up.
Tasmin had a lingering gut feeling.
With the official Lord War against "The Unmovable Wall" approaching in six days, she knew Lord Sky’s two-hundred-man army undoubtedly possessed high-tier elemental control casters.
What if they deployed heavy gravity arrays or suppression traps on the battlefield?
If she couldn’t move, react, and fight under extreme gravitational pressure, she wouldn’t be able to protect Silas when the war began.
THUD!
Mid-push-up, Tasmin’s left elbow buckled under the immense weight, and she tumbled out of her handstand, hitting the mat with a sharp exhale.
"Agh!"
Even with an S-Rank Shadow Commander class, 10x gravity was an excruciating physical test.
Tasmin gritted her teeth, wiping the sweat from her eyes, and looked over at Brida.
The Titan Bastion was still grinding through her push-ups with her face red and her muscles straining as she continued.
"...Three... Lord... Silas... Four... Lord... Silas...!"
’Fuck you.’
Tasmin’s silver eyes flared with fierce unyielding pride. She flipped back over, drove her hands into the mat, and kicked back up into her handstand position.
"HAAA!" Tasmin growled, forcing her shoulders to press upward against the crushing downforce.
She executed five handstand push-ups in a row, her athletic frame trembling with raw effort.
Once her shoulders hit near-exhaustion, Tasmin dropped back onto her boots, sank into a low combat stance, and began throwing rapid sharp shadow-punches into the heavy air.
Though they were very slow and she could barely move... at least it was going.
SWISH... SWISH...
Her punches were noticeably much slower than her usual high speed, but every single strike was forcing her neural pathways and muscle fibers to adapt to the heavy atmospheric resistance.
She could have easily used her [Shadow-Submersion Drift] to bypass the physical weight entirely... but Tasmin wanted her physical body to grow stronger on its own merit.
Watching the two S-Rank warriors push themselves to their physical limits inside her gravity well, Rowenna felt a sudden powerful wave of motivation surge through her chest.
’They’re working so hard...’ Rowenna thought, her blue eyes shining with admiration. ’I want to train too! I want to push my limits alongside them!’
Rowenna took a step forward, intending to step into the gravity well to test her own core endurance—
FLASH!
Before Rowenna’s boot could even touch the edge of the violet rune... A sudden brilliant burst of silver spatial light erupted beside her!
Aeli materialized out of thin air, grabbing Rowenna’s wrist.
"Borrowing her for a moment!" Aeli announced happily.
ZIP!
Before Tasmin or Brida could even react, Aeli triggered her short-range spatial teleportation again, vanishing from the training room with Rowenna in a flash of light.
The moment Rowenna vanished, the active [Runic Gravity Well] instantly collapsed, the violet light extinguishing from the floorboards.
THUD!
The sudden instantaneous removal of 10x gravity caught Brida completely off-guard.

With the crushing downforce suddenly vanishing into thin air, Brida’s fully tensed arm muscles pushed upward with maximum S-Rank force... sending her heavy muscular body shooting forward like a catapult.
Brida flew across the mat and crashed flat on top of Tasmin with her heavy chest and body pinning the woman to the floor.
BANG!
"GAH!" Tasmin let out a sharp gasp, pinned beneath the Titan Bastion.
Tasmin’s silver eyes flared with murder-filled rage as she glared up at the giant woman lying on top of her.
"Bitch..." Tasmin growled through gritted teeth. "...get the fuck off of me!"
Brida grinned cheekily, rubbing the back of her head. "Oops. My bad."
FLASH!
Aeli and Rowenna materialized cleanly inside Silas’s top-floor office.
They appeared directly in front of the broad mahogany desk. Silas was sitting in his leather chair, looking up from his holographic blueprint menu with a calm smile.
Rowenna blinked her blue eyes, looking around the office in total, speechless confusion as she tried to catch her breath from the sudden spatial jump.
Silas rested his hands on his desk, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto both of his primary mages.
"Are you both prepared for today?" Silas asked. "I assume Aeli already filled you in on why you’re here?"
Neither woman spoke for a second.
Silas didn’t wait for them to answer.
He leaned forward slightly, his sharp features radiating unshakeable Warlord confidence as he continued.
"I have chosen the two of you to rank up next. You will be evolving to S-Rank today... joining the ranks of Brida and Tasmin as our territory’s primary anchors. Are you both ready?"
Hearing his words, Rowenna’s heart completely stopped beating inside her chest.
Her blue eyes widened to the size of dinner plates with her throat going completely dry.
S-Rank?!
He was going to upgrade her from a simple B-Rank Runic Arcanist straight into an S-Rank legend?!
Beside her, Aeli’s eyes were glowing with intense tearful joy.
Both women stood up straight, bowing their heads deeply toward their Lord.
"We are ready, Lord Silas!" Aeli and Rowenna answered in synchronized passionate harmony. "Thank you for this incredible honor, My Lord!"
Silas smiled warmly, nodding his head.
"Good."
He looked at Aeli first.
"Aeli, step forward."
Aeli stepped up directly to the edge of his desk, her silver hair swaying over her shoulders and her heart hammering wildly against her ribs with breathless excitement.
Silas looked at her, channeling a mental command to his system interface.
’System,’ Silas commanded internally. ’Initialize Aeliana’s evolution screen.’
Inside his mind, Silas reflected on the Upgrade Point costs.

’Upgrading Aeli from A-Rank to S-Rank shouldn’t cost as much as C-rank to S-Rank did,’ Silas calculated. ’My priority right now is establishing a solid core roster of S-Rank commanders to secure the territory, while gradually elevating the average ranks of the girls so nobody feels left behind.’
PING!
A sleek blue system prompt tab materialized in Silas’s vision.
[Would you like to upgrade Aeliana’s A-Rank [Starlight Arcanist] to S-Rank [Astrea Archon Of The Stars]?]
[Cost: 300 UP]
[Y / N]
Silas’s golden eyes glinted with deep satisfaction.
300 UP! That was a massive 200 UP savings compared to a baseline S-Rank evolution!
’Astrea Archon of the stars is a cool name too though...’
Silas reached his broad right hand across the desk, placing his palm firmly on Aeli’s smooth shoulder.
Silas tapped [Y]!
BOOM!
The second his mental finger confirmed the selection... A blinding explosion of pure, radiant white starlight mana erupted from Silas’s palm, instantly engulfing the entire office in a cosmic flash.
Aeliana felt her conscious perception instantly detach from the polished mahogany floorboards beneath her boots.

The familiar desk, the tall arched windows overlooking the Umbral Basin, the scent of cedar wood, and even the towering six-foot-two physical presence of her Lord vanished in a fraction of a second, swallowed whole by a vast boundless ocean of pure radiant luminescence.
It was a physical and spiritual sensation unlike anything the elven arcanist had ever experienced in her centuries of existence.

During the past few days, she had stood on the sidelines of the Blessed Land, watching with a mixture of quiet awe, deep curiosity, and subtle envy as Tasmin and Brida underwent their own miraculous transformations under Silas’s direct touch.
She had spent late nights in her quarters wondering what it actually felt like to have one’s baseline physical and magical essence forcefully reconstructed from the ground up by their Lord.
Now, she finally understood.
The white energy didn’t merely wrap around her skin or envelop her clothes like a physical blanket.
It penetrated straight through her flesh, pouring into her soul and washing through her internal mana channels like warm liquid starlight.
Every single cell in her body vibrated at a hyper-accelerated harmonic frequency.
The sensation was so overwhelmingly intense, it was so heavenly and intoxicating, that Aeliana’s lips parted completely against her will.
"Mnnn-ahhh~"
A soft breathless sensual moan escaped her throat, echoing softly into the endless white void.
Gradually, the blinding radiance surrounding her figure began to shift.
The infinite light pulled inward, condensing around her floating body until it formed a tight, smooth, reflective dome that isolated her completely from the outside universe.
Aeliana blinked her eyelashes, her breath catching in her throat as she looked around the sealed space in utter bewilderment.
’What the hell...?’ Aeli thought, her mind spinning in a hazy cloud of confusion.
She felt completely trapped within the dome.
Her boots rested on a floor that felt like smooth, liquid glass, completely static and motionless.

She looked at her surroundings, realizing that the inner walls of the white dome were entirely reflective... acting as a seamless high-definition mirror that reflected her image back at her from every conceivable angle.
She stepped forward, leaning her upper body closer to inspect her reflection and flinched back in speech-depriving shock.
"Who... who is this?"
Aeli didn’t recognize herself.
She stood there in the center of the dome with her mouth slightly agape as her silver-gold eyes scanned her reflected image.
Her delicate elven ears, which had previously been elegant but modest in length, were noticeably longer now, sweeping upward in sharp incredibly graceful curves.
Aeli raised her trembling fingers, lightly brushing her fingertips against the pointed tips of her ears.
The second her skin made contact with the tips, a sharp, electric jolt of heightened feedback shot straight to her brain.
Her ears felt infinitely more sensitive than before... capable of picking up atmospheric pressure shifts, thermal currents, and distant mana ripples with terrifying crystalline clarity.
"My... my hair..." Aeli whispered softly, her melodic voice carrying a gentle celestial echo that vibrated against the reflective dome.
Her pristine moonlight-silver hair had completely transformed. It was no longer silver.

It had transmuted into a breathtaking radiant shade of starlight blonde... not a flat natural or artificial blonde, but a brilliant shimmering blonde that mirrored the exact celestial bodies she loved to observe through her telescope late at night when she was a child.
"Beautiful..."
Tiny microscopic specks of glowing cosmic dust drifted gently from the ends of her hair, floating in zero-gravity waves around her shoulders.
And her eyes were different too.
Her previously simple green irises had shifted into multi-layered luminous cosmic orbs that constantly pulsed with mana.
’I don’t even need a disguise...’ She thought, she looked nothing like the original Aeliana so there was no other need to hide her face for Lord Sky and his stream.
She looked down at her body with her breath hitching in her throat for a third time.
’H-huh...’

chapters.title: Chapter 279: Grand Runemaster
paragraphs: Her chest was noticeably bigger... her breasts swelling against her white arcanist robes to an eye-popping voluminous size that gave her a far more shapely hourglass figure.
Her waist was noticeably slimmer, her hips flared out in a perfect sweeping curve, and her entire posture radiated an effortless grace that belied her previous timidness.
But that wasn’t the only thing.
Her physical body felt lighter than it ever had in her entire life.
She felt as though she was no longer bound by the gravitational pull of the world, practically floating on the edge of spatial wind currents.
A sudden unexpected wave of anxious panic touched her heart. This new form was so divine that it frightened her.
’I’m... I’m a bit scared...’ Aeli thought with her heart hammering wildly against her ribs as she looked at her transformed body.
Seeking an escape from the reflective isolation, Aeli extended her pale hand, lightly tapping her palm against the inner wall of the reflective dome.
CRACK!
The second her skin made contact with the surface, a web of glowing fractures spider-webbed across the mirror.
The entire dome shattered into a million sparkling starlight fragments, dissolving into the air like cosmic rain.
"Hah!"
Aeli snapped her eyes open, taking a sudden deep gulp of air as reality violently slammed back into focus.
She was standing inside the Keep’s top-floor office.
Silas was standing directly in front of her, his broad hands resting firmly on her shoulders, shaking her gently as his golden-ringed eyes scanned her face with genuine protective concern.
"Aeli? Aeli, hey," Silas called out as he looked at her. "Are you okay?"
Aeli blinked her luminous cosmic eyes, looking into Silas’s handsome sharp face.
The sight of her Lord instantly grounded her frantic mind, and a wave of tearful gratitude flooded her chest.
"I... I am fine, My Lord," Aeli stammered out, her voice trembling with emotion as she bowed her head deeply before him. "Thank you... thank you so much for this incredible gift—"
SNIFF!
Before Aeli could complete her sentence of gratitude, a sudden foul odor entered her newly sensitive nostrils.
Aeli froze.
Her long elven ears twitched violently, her nose crinkling in disgust as a wave of pure stench hit her senses like a physical hammer.
"Ugh!" Aeli gasped, covering her nose with her sleeve as her eyes watered. "What... what smells that badly?!"
Standing on the other side of the mahogany desk, Silas and Rowenna looked at her with helpless sympathetic expressions.
Silas gestured downward with his hand, offering a dry smile. "Aeli... look down at yourself."
Aeli looked down at her own body and let out a high-pitched horrified shriek that echoed off the office walls.
"EEEEEK!"
Covering her pristine starlight-blonde skin and her white arcanist robes were dense, thick, tar-like blobs of black physical impurities.
During her evolution to S-Rank, the Gold Core mana had forcefully purged every single trace of metabolic toxin, residual mana blockages, and cellular waste from her body.

Because her elven lineage possessed centuries of accumulated magical residue, the amount of black sludge ejected from her pores was vastly greater than the impurities that had come off Tasmin and Brida combined.
The foul sulfurous stench wafted through the office, completely overpowering the room.
"I-I AM SO SORRY, MY LORD!" Aeli squeaked out in mortified embarrassment, her face exploding into a red flush. "I APOLOGIZE FOR THIS FOUL SMELL! PLEASE EXCUSE ME!"
FLASH!

Without waiting for a single word of response, Aeli panicked, triggered her short-range spatial teleportation, and vanished from the office in a frantic burst of silver-gold light, sprinting toward the Keep’s bathroom at high speed.
Silas stood behind his desk, holding his breath for a second until the lingering air currents cleared the room of the foul odor.
But before her presence had completely faded from his range, Silas had already pulled up her updated system status sheet to inspect the results of his 300 UP investment.
[Name]: Aeliana
[Title]: Starlight Arcanist -> Astrea Archon Of The Stars
[Rank]: S-Rank
[Loyalty]: 100 (Diehard / Love)
[Vitality]: 1000
[Active & Passive Skills]:

[Astrea Starlight Cascade]: Summons an orbital rain of hyper-compressed, celestial starlight beams. Clears massive troop formations, vaporizes defense barriers, and bypasses physical armor. (Cost: 400 Mana/cast)

[Spatial Constellation Drift]: Passively dissolves her physical weight into microscopic spatial folds and wind currents. Allows floating/hovering mobility, boosts evasion by 80%, and grants short-range instantaneous spatial blinks. (Passive)

[Celestial Star-Ward Domain]: Expands a 200-meter radiant perimeter of astral mana. Passively detects all stealthed units, reduces enemy magic resistance by 30%, and provides continuous high-yield mana regeneration to allied casters. (Cost: 150 Mana/minute)

[Supernova Impact]: Compresses stellar mana into a single point and detonates it upon impact, freezing surrounding terrain in absolute-zero frost while releasing an explosive cosmic shockwave. (Cost: 350 Mana/cast)
[Space Compression]: Compresses space itself into a singular point, crushing physical matter and distorting incoming kinetic attacks. (Cost: 500 Mana/cast)
[Ice Creation]: As long as there is mana in the air, the user is able to create ice out of it. (Cost: 10 Mana/cast)
[Long Distance Teleportation]: With the help of spatial currents, the user is able to teleport over long distances. (Cost: 100 Mana/cast)
Silas stared at the glowing blue holographic screen, swallowing hard as he took in the astronomical numbers and skill descriptions.
’5,500 Mana... Space Compression... Long Distance Teleportation...’ Silas calculated in his mind, his eyes widening slightly. ’And there are a bit more spells there...’
She had truly become a powerhouse.
The utility, mobility, and destructive output packed into her new skill set were surprising, to say the least.
’It’s quite surprising...’ Silas thought, leaning back slightly in his leather chair. ’...but does all of this matter? No, Aeli will still be my secretary at the end of the day.’
No matter how terrifying her combat stats became, her core role in his administration remained unchanged.
She was still his primary officer, his scheduler, and his trusted companion.
However, Silas was genuinely interested in what the hell "Astrea Archon Of The Stars" actually meant conceptually.
He invoked his system interface, submitting a direct query to clarify the title’s lore.
’System, what does Astrea Archon Of The Stars mean?’ Silas asked mentally.
A sleek blue text box popped up in his vision, delivering a remarkably vague response.
[System Query Processing...]
[System Response: After research, the title ’Astrea Archon Of The Stars’ denotes one chosen by the stars.]
[Note: If the Host wishes to know more, the Host is strongly advised to go read a book in the Library instead of bothering the system interface.]
Silas’s jaw twitched.
He stared at the blue text box in total deadpan disbelief.
’Is this system being classy all of a sudden?’ Silas thought, rolling his golden-ringed eyes. ’Telling me to go read a book? Unbelievable...’
Silas dismissed the sassy system notification with a flick of his wrist, turning his attention back to the remaining woman in the office.
Rowenna was still standing near the mahogany desk.
She took a step forward, lowering her upper body into a deep, respectful bow before him.
"My Lord..." Rowenna spoke softly, her blue eyes looking up at him with an extraordinarily earnest weight. "...I humbly ask that you focus your attention on me too."
Silas looked at her bowing figure, noticing the subtle tension in her shoulders and the slight trembling of her fingers against her dark skirt.
In truth, Rowenna had been trying her absolute hardest for days to get her Lord’s attention.
But Silas always seemed to be focused primarily on Aeliana.
Rowenna knew why... Aeliana had won that battle a while ago, granting her the right to accompany Silas into the Secret Realm.
Rowenna couldn’t help but think that if she herself had gotten to enter the Secret Realm too, she would have been just as close to him as the elven arcanist was.
She wanted that same closeness and that same level of trust.
Silas looked at the quiet runic caster with a warm gentle expression softening his sharp features.
"Rowenna," Silas called out smoothly. "Come closer."
Rowenna blinked her blue eyes, raising her head.
She hesitantly stepped up to the edge of the mahogany desk, lowering her head slightly as she stood before him.
Silas stood up from his leather chair.
He leaned across the desk, reaching out with his broad hand to gently cup her jaw, and pressed a soft kiss directly onto her forehead.
Rowenna’s entire body went rock-rigid.
Her blue eyes widened to the size of saucers, her face exploding into a bright burning crimson flush as a wave of pure overwhelming warmth flooded her chest.
Her gloomy insecure demeanor vanished in a fraction of a second, completely replaced by a radiant, ecstatic glow.
Silas pulled back slightly, looking into her trembling blue eyes.
"Don’t ever feel less important, Rowenna. That’s not what you are to me."
Silas patted her head gently, adding with a confident warm smirk.
"Besides... after this upgrade... why don’t you come with me to see the outside Lord?"
Rowenna’s breath completely hitched in her throat!
"R-Really, My Lord?!" Rowenna blabbered out, her voice squeaking in breathless shock. "You... you want me to come with you to see Lord Sky?!"
At least that was the name Tasmin had told her.
Silas patted her head once more, offering a firm, reassuring nod.
"Really. I need my best Runic Arcanist by my side."
Rowenna stood there with her heart soaring straight to the clouds!
Deep down inside her soul, a quiet voice whispered that she probably didn’t deserve such incredible favor from her Sovereign Lord... but she accepted it with every fiber of her being.
’I won’t ever wash my forehead again for the rest of my life...’ Rowenna swore fiercely in her own mind.
Silas placed his broad palm flat against the top of her head, feeling the texture of her hair.
His golden-ringed eyes focused, his voice taking on a commanding weight.
"Would you like to get stronger, Rowenna?"
Rowenna raised her head, her blue eyes blazing with unshakeable loyalty and determination as she answered his question.
"I would, My Lord!"
Silas smiled.
PING!
He summoned his system interface, bringing up Rowenna’s evolution prompt.
[Would you like to upgrade Rowenna’s B-Rank [Runic Arcanist] to S-Rank [Grand Runemaster]?]
[Cost: 400 UP]
[Y / N]
Silas looked at the 400 UP cost.
For her case, the higher cost was completely understandable since she was making a massive two-tier leap directly from B-Rank to S-Rank.
Silas didn’t hesitate for a single second as he pressed his thumb against the glowing screen.
Silas pressed [Y]!
BOOM!
Once again, a blinding explosion of pure white mana erupted from Silas’s palm, instantly engulfing Rowenna’s entire body as her world turned completely white.
SWISH.
Rowenna blinked her eyes.
The blinding white light slowly receded, replaced by the quiet majestic atmosphere of a vast ancient room.
Rowenna looked around, her jaw dropping in total, speech-deprived bewilderment.
"Wha..." Rowenna muttered out loud, her voice echoing off distant walls. "Why the hell am I in a Library?!"
She was no longer standing in Silas’s office.
She was standing in the center of an ancient library filled with towering mahogany bookshelves stretching high into the air, packed to the brim with glowing, leather-bound books.
She had just been in her Lord’s presence a second ago... and next she was trapped in a strange room? What in the world was going on?
Regardless of her confusion, Rowenna took a few steps forward across the polished floorboards, calling out into the quiet space.
"Hello...?"
Her voice echoed repeatedly through the silent library, confirming that she was quite alone in this strange realm.
Rowenna caught sight of her reflection in a large, silver-framed mirror resting against a nearby pillar.
She stopped dead in her tracks, staring at the image in speechless shock.
"I... I look so different..." Rowenna whispered.
Her physical appearance was vastly different from how she looked normally.
Her hair was significantly longer, cascading down past her waist in lustrous, silky waves.
Her body figure was far better, taking on a stunning sculpted hourglass curve.
Her chest had expanded from a modest size to a heavy, eye-popping endowment that practically popped out of her arcanist robes.

She realized with a deep blush that she hadn’t even worn a bra underneath, allowing the sensitive shape of her nipples to show clearly through the fabric... yet, strangely, it felt extraordinarily comfortable against her skin.
This was how she had always wanted her body to be after all.

chapters.title: Chapter 280: Plans For The Raid
paragraphs: Rowenna observed her new form in the mirror, reaching down with both hands to gently cup her chest, jiggling her breasts together with a blushing satisfied smile.
"Hehehehe~"
Once she was done admiring her new curves, Rowenna walked over to a dark oak reading table in the center of the library.
Resting on the table was a single glowing violet diagram.
Rowenna leaned over the table, her blue eyes narrowing as she recognized the schematic instantly.
It was the exact same rune she was working on earlier this morning... her [Runic Overwrite] spell.
"Huh?"
But on this table, the schematic wasn’t incomplete or unstable.
The missing geometric lines and mana equations were completely filled in.
Rowenna leaned closer, a brilliant realization-filled smile spreading across her face as she understood what she had been missing all along.
"So that’s how it works..." Rowenna realized happily.
She raised her right hand over the table, channeling her new mana reserves.
CRACKLE... FWOOSH!
The completed [Runic Overwrite] matrix materialized three inches above her palm, stabilizing with perfect clarity.
To test its power, Rowenna instinctively cast a localized gravity well spell toward the far corner of the library, and then immediately triggered her completed overwrite array toward it.
BANG!
The overwrite array negated the gravity spell instantly from a distance... shattering the gravitational field into harmless sparks before it could even take effect.
"AHAHAHA!" Rowenna burst into a victorious joyous laugh. "It worked!"
Suddenly...
RUMBLE!
The towering bookshelves surrounding the library began to vibrate violently.
All the books in the Library seemed to fall from their shelves simultaneously, floating through the air and flying straight toward her.
"Hehehahaha..."
It felt extremely weird, but as the book circled her figure, their glowing pages opened, showing her an infinite array of ancient runes.
So many runes... Fire runes, Ice runes, Lightning runes, Hurricane runes, Earth runes, 20x Gravity runes too?
’Jackpot!’
It was making her go completely crazy with academic bliss...
Rowenna absorbed the flood of ancient knowledge directly into her mind, letting out a wild euphoric laugh.
"Ehehehahaha~!"
Among the infinite floating pages, she even spotted a specialized [Attraction Rune] alongside dozens of other runes.
The ancient books stacked themselves around her figure, climbing up over her arms and shoulders, literally sealing her within a dense cocoon of pure runic knowledge.
"Rowenna... Rowenna, wake up," Silas’s deep voice called out, shaking the woman’s body in his office.
Back inside the Keep’s top-floor office, Silas was leaning over his desk, looking at Rowenna’s unconscious body with a deeply exasperated expression.
This was officially the second time that the person he was upgrading had lost consciousness during the evolution process.
Silas couldn’t help but wonder internally why Aeli and Rowenna had passed out cold, whereas Tasmin and Brida had remained wide awake and active during their upgrades.
Were Tasmin and Brida simply like that due to their physical combat classes, or was the sudden surge of knowledge simply too heavy for a mage’s brain to process in real-time...?
Rowenna woke up, her blue eyes fluttering open as her consciousness returned to the executive office.
The second her mind cleared, she immediately noticed the thick black globs of sulfurous impurities clinging to her perfect newly evolved body.
The foul tar-like sludge coated her arms, her chest, and her robes, emitting a heavy stench.
Rowenna went completely rigid, trembling shyly with mortified embarrassment.
"Congratulations, Rowenna," Silas began, offering a warm smile. "You did—"
"MY LORD!" Rowenna interrupted frantically, her voice reaching a high-pitched squeak.
She violently shifted three steps backward, bowing several times in rapid succession after shifting back.
"I... I URGENTLY NEED TO TAKE A BATH RIGHT NOW! PLEASE EXCUSE ME!" Rowenna yelled in total panicked embarrassment.
STEP... STEP... BANG!
Without offering a single word of explanation, the newly evolved Grand Runemaster turned on her heel, sprinted out of the office door, and ran off toward the Keep’s bathroom at record speed.
Silas sighed, rubbing the bridge of his nose as he watched her disappear down the hallway.
He leaned back in his leather chair and swiped his hand through the air, pulling up her updated system status sheet to see her newly acquired stats.
[Name]: Rowenna
[Title]: Runic Arcanist → Grand Runemaster
[Rank]: S-Rank
[Loyalty]: 100 (Diehard / Love)
[Vitality]: 950
[Active & Passive Skills]:
[Omni-Elemental Runic Array]: Instantly inscribes high-tier multi-elemental runes into empty air or directly onto targets without requiring chant time or a physical staff. (Cost: 120 Mana/cast)

[Runic Gravity Well (20x)]: Inscribes an expanded, deep-purple gravitational array that multiplies downforce up to twentyfold (20x). Instantly crushes heavy iron tanks, grounds flying drakes, and splinters bedrock beneath enemy armies. (Cost: 300 Mana/cast)

[Ultra Runic Disruption]: Passively radiates a 50-meter aura that destabilizes incoming enemy spells, hacks complex barriers, and forces opposing spellcasters into spell-backfire or delayed channeling. (Passive)

[Gravitational Singularity Collapse]: Condenses a 20x gravity well into a microscopic black point, pulling all surrounding enemies, projectiles, and fortifications violently into the center before detonating outward in a force wave. (Cost: 450 Mana/cast)

[Attraction Rune]: Inscribes a specialized gravitational attraction mark on a designated target or surface, pulling all surrounding physical objects, projectiles, or enemies toward the marked point with immense force. (Cost: 150 Mana/cast)
[Runic Barrier Overwrite]: Instantly analyzes, bypasses, and dismantles high-tier enemy defense barriers, sealing arrays, and magical wards. (Cost: 200 Mana/cast)
[More]
Silas stared at the glowing blue status sheet, his golden-ringed eyes widening to the size of saucers as his jaw subtly dropped.
’What the fuck...?’ Silas thought, his mind completely blown by the absurdity of her newly unlocked skills.
She was even more OP than Aeli...
However, as Silas scanned down the translucent interface, he noticed a tiny, glowing golden tab at the bottom of her active skill list labeled
[More...].
It was the first time Silas had ever seen a secondary expansion tab on a unit’s status interface.
Intrigued, he extended his index finger and tapped the floating text.
DING!
The holographic menu instantly expanded downward, unfolding into a secondary and tertiary list of sub-skills, utility runes, passive runes, and so many skills.

Dozens upon dozens of integrated runes cascaded down the screen in neat blue rows including glaciating frost wards, high-voltage lightning traps, atmospheric wind shears, and kinetic deflection circles.
Silas blinked, staring at the endless wall of text.
’Just how many skills does she know now?’ Silas thought, a dry amazed breath escaping his lips.
The volume of magical knowledge pumped directly into Rowenna’s brain during her evolution was simply too much.

Between her primary [Omni-Elemental Runic Array], her brutal [20x Runic Gravity Well], her spatial [Attraction Rune], and this vast library of secondary elemental power, Rowenna had effectively become a walking one-woman magical academy.
’Might as well give her a promotion...’
Silas leaned back in his leather chair, resting his hands on the mahogany desk as he digested the results.
He was genuinely surprised by the jump in power both Rowenna and Aeliana had displayed upon reaching S-Rank.

Taking a step back to analyze the territory’s overall combat roster, Silas realized it was not a far stretch at all to say that Aeli and Rowenna were now, in terms of pure raw destructive output and wide-area battlefield control, significantly stronger than Tasmin and Brida.
’Then again...’ Silas reflected in his thoughts, ’...that was to be expected.’
Tasmin was a specialized Shadow Commander built for single-target assassination, high-speed flank execution, and backline disruption.
Brida was a Titan Bastion designed to be an immovable physical wall, drawing aggro and crushing frontline charges with her massive shield.
Aeli and Rowenna, on the other hand, were pure S-Rank high-tier casters.
Their classes were fundamentally designed to reshape terrain, collapse physical space, and obliterate entire troop formations from miles away.
Comparing a frontline tank to a high level mage was apples and oranges.
Silas let out a long quiet sigh, running a broad hand through his dark hair.
FWOOSH!
He swiped his hand through the air, dismissing both holographic status sheets.

With Aeli and Rowenna having both panicked and sprinted off to the Keep’s bathhouses, the thick sulfurous smell of purged physical impurities that had briefly filled the office completely dissipated, carried out through the open windows by the fresh morning breeze.
Silas sat alone in his chair, his golden-ringed eyes fixing onto his remaining UP balance displayed in the corner of his vision.
[Current UP Balance: 540 UP]
’We need more UP,’ Silas concluded firmly in his mind.
540 UP was a solid safety cushion, but it wasn’t nearly enough for the ambitious territorial overhaul Silas was planning.
Today was supposed to be dedicated entirely to civic renovations and structural expansions... like erecting the Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters, which required 300 units of Obsidian-Slate Stone.
Furthermore, once the structural foundations were set, Silas wanted to look into upgrading Fenna.
Elevating her archery to a full S-Rank master-class would give his army an elite long-range physical sniper to complement Aeli and Rowenna’s magical bombardment.
And after Fenna, Silas intended to elevate the baseline ranks of all seventy-two Vanguard recruits... raising them from basic C-Rank and D-Rank combatants to a solid reliable B-Rank foundation.
That way, none of the women in his territory would ever feel left behind or defenseless during large-scale raids.
’To pull all of that off...’ Silas calculated mentally, ’...I’m going to need thousands of UP.’
The most logical way to farm UP was simple: send his entire army out into the Umbral Basin to clear monster nests, raid high-tier elite caverns, and wipe out regional bosses.
...However, a major dilemma held Silas back.
Silas stood up from his desk, walking over to the glass window and looking out toward the distant perimeter of the Blessed Land.
Out past the treeline, situated a few miles away in the neutral buffer zone, was Lord Sky’s rolling mobile fortress... The Unmovable Wall.

If Silas mobilized his entire force... sending Eluned, Morwenna, Talira, Tasmin, Brida, Aeli, Rowenna, and all the girls out into the open fields simultaneously... Lord Sky’s high-tier optical arrays, long-range scouting drakes, and stream surveillance feeds would immediately pick them up.
Sky would be able to watch them fight from the comfort of his mobile command bridge, meticulously cataloging their abilities, measuring their mana outputs, and analyzing their movement patterns.

Silas was more than willing to show a bit of his hand to maintain a dominant presence, but he had zero intention of handing his rival a complete crystal-clear view of his entire military roster six days before the official Lord War.
’I already assume Sky has figured out a way to deal with Tasmin,’ Silas analyzed coolly with his golden eyes narrowing.
During their initial skirmish near the border, Tasmin had been the primary unit Sky had witnessed in action.

An experienced veteran Classic Lord like Sky had undoubtedly spent the last two days analyzing her shadow-drift mechanics, preparing disruption wards or light-elemental traps to neutralize her routes.
...But Sky hadn’t seen Brida’s S-Rank Titan Bastion defense yet.
He hadn’t seen Aeli’s new [Space Compression] or Rowenna’s [20x Gravity Well].
Silas still held the element of surprise.
Keeping those key assets hidden in the dark until the war officially commenced was a massive strategic advantage that Silas refused to surrender.
’The most fearful thing about a Mobile Territory Lord is how much access to modern technology they have...’ Silas reflected.
Lords like Sky didn’t just rely on ancient magic or summoned units.
Their mobile rigs were equipped with high-grade industrial machinery, automated siege cannons, long-range mana artillery, drone reconnaissance networks, and modern tactical comms.
Silas couldn’t blame Sky for utilizing those tools, nor was it illegal under the Sovereign Realm’s war codes.
At the end of the day, a Lord War was a brutal uncompromising conflict.
If a Lord had access to modern military hardware and chose not to exploit it, they were simply an idiot.
This was especially true for someone like Sky, who was live-streaming his entire campaign to millions of viewers on the network.
If Sky didn’t exploit every single technical edge available to him, his streaming audience would abandon him, and rival Lords would pick his territory apart like vultures.
So, while Silas possessed unshakeable confidence in his ability to utterly crush Sky when the battle started, that confidence didn’t mean he was going to be stupid.
He wasn’t about to give his enemy a free all-access press pass to analyze his top-tier commanders.
’I need a controlled way to farm UP without revealing my main backline...’ Silas thought, resting his hand against the window frame.
CREAK!
The heavy oak door to his office suddenly swung open. Silas paused his thoughts, turning his head around to see who was entering.
Standing in the doorway was Morwenna.
