chapters.title: Chapter 285: Abyss Corsair
paragraphs: Silas walked into the foundry, rolling his golden-ringed eyes with a dry exasperated breath.
"You really are an unredeemable pervert, Thora..." Silas stated flatly.

One of these days... perhaps right after they officially crushed Lord Sky in the upcoming war, Silas was genuinely tempted to test whether Thora would still be able to spout all of those crude, nasty, and shameless jokes once she was actually forced to face his boner right in front of her face.
"Hehehehe~"
Silas let out a low evil chuckle in his throat.
The second that quiet dark chuckle escaped Silas’s lips—
Every single hair on the back of Thora’s neck instantly stood up on end.

A sudden, unexplainable, and terrifying chill ran straight down her spine, making her dwarven instincts scream that her Lord was secretly plotting something extraordinarily dangerous for her rear end.
Thora blinked her dark eyes, looking at him nervously.
"W-What the hell are you laughing like that for, My Lord...?"
Silas didn’t answer her.
He simply offered a calm innocent smile and swiped his hand through the air over the storage racks.
FWOOSH... BOOM!

Four massive reinforced iron crates... filled to the brim with the high-grade elemental ores and metallic alloys Silas had procured from Sky’s trade inventory materialized out of his spatial storage, landing heavily against the stone floorboards.
Thora’s nervous confusion instantly vanished, completely replaced by pure dwarven greed.
She scrambled across the foundry floor, throwing her heavy hammer aside, and popped open the heavy iron lid of the first crate.
Inside were rows of shimmering high-density metallic ingots pulsing with raw energy.
Thora pressed her face directly against the cool surface of the metallic ingots, taking a deep greedy breath of the raw ore fragrance.

"Ahhhh~! Smells like raw metallic progress!" Thora cackled happily, rubbing her hands together. "It’s not quite as high-grade as the pristine ores we mine ourselves from the deep Basin veins... but this will do nicely! Hehehe!"
Silas watched her inspect the shipment, letting out a quiet sigh through his nose.
’Once this war with Sky is over...’ Silas reflected in his mind, ’...we definitely need to resume our deep mining operations in the Basin.’
Raw metal ores were the lifeblood of his territory’s infrastructure.
High-tier alloys allowed Thora to forge better armor for the girls, reinforce their siege weapons, and supply their casters with mana-conductive conduits.
’And on the bright side...’ Silas added in his thoughts, ’...I’m going to be receiving a massive influx of new women from this entire situation.’
Once the Lord War concluded and Sky was officially eliminated, Silas intended to dump his accumulated rewards directly into purchasing a massive batch of Troop Summoning Cards.

Expanding his Vanguard legion with fresh female units would give his territory the manpower needed to establish permanent mining outposts across the Umbral Basin as well as the 70 women he was receiving.
’And wait... right,’ Silas remembered, his golden eyes glinting. ’After the war, I’m also scheduled to meet the official World Council.’

When that meeting with the World Council eventually took place, Silas intended to leverage his Gold Core standing and roster to make a series of absurd, uncompromising, and downright crazy demands from the global governing body.
He couldn’t wait to see the looks on those arrogant council diplomats’ faces when he laid his demands on the table.
...But first, he had to crush Lord Sky’s mobile fortress.
"Hey, Lord!" Thora called out suddenly, snapping him out of his internal monologue.
Silas looked over at the dwarf. "Yeah?"
Thora walked over to a velvet-lined display rack situated near her primary workbench... a rack reserved exclusively for custom master-work items stamped with the official crest of the Blessed Land.
She reached out, picking up a sleek shimmering metallic item wrapped in protective silk, and walked back over to Silas.
"I crafted something special for you," Thora announced proudly, her dwarven voice taking on a rare serious craftsman pitch. "Or rather... for your Vespera form."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "For Vespera?"
Thora carefully unrolled the silk wrapping, revealing a breathtaking piece of master-work armor.
It was a sleek silver-and-gold metallic Arm-Gauntlet... crafted from hyper-dense fluid-sculpted metal plates that swept from the fingertips all the way up to the shoulder joint.
The metal glistered with an indestructible, mirror-like sheen, etched with fine glowing arrays that hummed with passive defensive mana.

"Listen to me, My Lord," Thora explained seriously, pointing her calloused finger at the gauntlet. "In an official Lord War against a guy like Sky, those bastards will try every single dirty, underhanded trick in the book to win. And if you go out there fighting in your single-armed Vespera disguise... those enemy snipers and artillery casters are going to target your only good arm to try and disarm you."
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes widened slightly.
Thora was 100% correct...
In his single-armed Vespera persona, his right arm was his primary weapon conduit.
If an enemy sniper managed to sever or disable his right hand during combat, his combat efficiency in that form would drop significantly.

"So I forged this," Thora continued proudly, tapping the metallic sleeve. "I made it using our specialized indestructible Sil-Grave Alloy. It automatically deploys an instantaneous high-yield defense barrier whenever it senses an incoming strike! With this on, no sniper in the Basin will ever be able to touch your hand."
Silas took the silver gauntlet into his hands, feeling its incredible light-weight balance and dense material structure.
A wave of genuine deep appreciation washed over Silas’s chest.
Thora might be a crude pervert 90% of the time... but as a Master Smith, her loyalty, foresight, and care for her Lord were absolute.
"Thank you, Thora," Silas said sincerely. "This is genuinely brilliant work."
Silas leaned down, pressing a soft kiss directly onto the center of her dwarven forehead.
Thora froze dead in her tracks.
Her dark eyes widened, her pale cheeks exploding into a bright burning crimson flush as her dwarven brain completely short-circuited.
"A-Ah... W-Well...!" Thora stammered out, her voice squeaking in total embarrassment.
In a fit of sudden madness...
Thora violently leaped backward two paces, bent her upper body completely forward, and stuck her large and curvaceous rear straight out into the air directly toward Silas’s face.
"I-IF YOU’RE THAT GRATEFUL, MY LORD..." Thora yelled out frantically, her face burning red. "...YOU CAN SHOVE YOUR MEMBER STRAIGHT INTO MY ASS RIGHT NOW! I’M ALREADY SOAKING WET ANYWAY!"
Silas stood there in the foundry, looking at the bent-over dwarf presenting her rear to him.
His golden-ringed eyes narrowed into a cold, flat, and thoroughly deadpan line.
Silas calmly raised his boot and delivered a swift, firm, and thoroughly unimpressed kick right to her exposed butt cheek.
BANG!
"OWWWWW!" Thora shrieked out, clutching her rear as she stumbled forward, pouting angrily at him over her shoulder. "YOU’RE NO FUN, LORD!"
Silas simply shook his head with a dry amused chuckle, turning on his heel as he walked out of the foundry into the morning air.
"Later Thora!"
"HAARGH!"
Oona screamed at the absolute top of her lungs, stepping forward on the damp, moss-slicked stone ridge and thrusting her mythril-tipped catalyst staff forward with violent explosive force.
KRA-BOOM!
A scorching compressed torrent of crimson fire erupted from the crystal tip of her staff with a deafening thunderous roar.

The high-density jet of elemental flame tore clean through the humid morning mist of the Umbral Basin, illuminating the dark towering Ironwood canopy in a blinding flash of orange and crimson light before colliding directly with the broad chest of a sprawling six-foot shadow-bat monster that had plummeted from the upper branches.
"EEEEEEEEEE!"

The winged beast let out a brief agonizing shriek as the high-yield flame instantly incinerated its leathery wings, carbonized its demonic flesh, and burned its monster core into falling, glowing ash.
Oona slammed the heavy wooden butt of her staff onto the damp earth with a heavy thud with her teeth clenching so hard her jaw muscles throbbed beneath her skin.
She stood there panting heavily, her chest heaving beneath her leather chest-piece, thoroughly and deeply pissed off at herself.
Ever since the Mage Royale had taken place in the Keep’s central courtyard days ago, Oona hadn’t been able to sleep properly.

Because she and several other apprentice casters had been assigned to peripheral perimeter scouting and routine resource gathering at the time, they had completely missed their chance to compete in the main bracket.
’And it was like everybody forgot us...’

’I thought My Lord was just joking when he talked about promotions...’ Oona grumbled bitterly in her own head, wiping a thick line of sweat from her forehead with the back of her leather glove. ’I didn’t think the winner was actually going to get personal training, direct favor, and a massive jump straight into his inner circle!’
...Though, deep down inside her soul, Oona knew the cold hard truth.
Even if she had managed to enter the bracket that day, she knew that she couldn’t have won against Kadi even if she tried.
That woman was simply too strong.
Kadi’s control over Earth was far too oppressive, her mana reserves were too thick, and her execution was far too sharp for any of them to handle in a direct duel.
"Take this, you ugly, overgrown winged rat!" Valeria screamed from twenty paces to Oona’s left!
Valeria... the fierce short-fused Pyromancer with fiery red hair tied back in a messy swinging ponytail swung her bare arms in a rapid, violent circular arc.
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
Three basketball-sized, white-hot fireballs materialized around her broad shoulders and shot forward like mortar shells through the dense foliage.
They slammed straight into a cluster of screeching shadow-bats diving from the upper branches, detonating upon impact in a magnificent shower of blinding sparks, cooked flesh, and exploding ash.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
"Die! Die! DIE!" Seraina shouted boisterously, her loud, cheerful voice ringing out over the roaring forest!

Seraina... the boisterous cheerful Lightning Caster stretching her bare arms near the edge of the defensive barrier channeled raw voltage through the polished copper catalyst rings fitted over her thumbs.
KRA-TATATATA!
Jagged, violent tendrils of blinding purple lightning branched out from her fingertips in a massive, wide-area fan.
The high-voltage arcana leaped wildly from beast to beast, frying the diving bat monsters mid-air, snapping their wing bones with shockwaves, and blasting the rest of the bat monsters with lightning.
"Fuck you! Fuck you! Fuck YOU!" Seraina yelled at the top of her lungs with every jagged discharge, laughing wildly as the pungent, electric smell of ozone filled the clearing!
Standing in a tight, disciplined defensive formation around the clearing’s perimeter, the rest of the specialized magic battalion held their ground, casting continuously to keep the swarm suppressed.
Directly beside Valeria stood Lia... the calm Wind Mage holding a sleek wooden focus staff in both of her hands.

She swept her staff in smooth, fluid, and rhythmic motions, generating razor-sharp wind blades that cleanly bisected any shadow-bat attempting to flank their left wing before the beasts could even screech.
Positioned directly behind her was Thalia... the quiet Earth Shaper who kept her eyes fixed firmly on the dirt beneath her boots.

She didn’t shout, curse, or cast flashy spells as she simply stomped her heavy leather boot against the earth with powerful force, raising jagged stone spikes from the ground to impale falling beasts or constructing instant earth-ramparts to deflect incoming sonic screeches.
Over on the right flank stood Calia... the soft-spoken Water Specialist fidgeting nervously with her long sleeves between casts.
Despite her timid shy nature, her liquid whips were lethal... slicing cleanly through monster hides and instantly dousing any stray forest fires sparked by Valeria’s wild pyromancy.
Standing silently within the dark, shadowy recess of a massive ancient oak tree was Morrigan... a sharp-eyed Shadow Weaver standing quietly in the corner shadows.
’Miss Tasmin doesn’t want to take me as her student.’
She didn’t utter a single sound.
She merely merged her dark frame with the surrounding trunk shadows, extending dark ethereal shadow-tendrils from the mud to snap the necks of stray beasts before they could land.

Further along the perimeter stood Eliora... the stern Ice Sculptor clutching a crystal orb in her hands, freezing shadow-bats solid mid-air so they shattered like delicate glass upon hitting the hard ground.

Beside her was Venma... the Arcane Blaster twirling a bronze catalyst ring on her thumb, firing precise, high-velocity raw mana bolts that punched clean, fist-sized holes through monster skulls with precision then there was Aurelia, the elegant Light Weaver stretching her fingers to project blinding disorienting flashes that grounded the flying swarms.

Together with Sybil, Oona, Ysolde, and Maeve... all thirteen mages were present here in the clearing, working like a well-oiled artillery unit to completely obliterate the high-tier monster nest in seconds.
SWISH... SLICE!

Suddenly, from the far edge of the tree line, a massive twelve-foot Shadow-Bat Alpha... a monstrous beast that had managed to slip past the frontline barrage using its superior stealth camouflage plummeted down toward Lia’s blind spot with its razor-sharp claws extended.

"You really are an unredeemable pervert, Thora..." Silas stated flatly.

One of these days... perhaps right after they officially crushed Lord Sky in the upcoming war, Silas was genuinely tempted to test whether Thora would still be able to spout all of those crude, nasty, and shameless jokes once she was actually forced to face his boner right in front of her face.
"Hehehehe~"
Silas let out a low evil chuckle in his throat.
The second that quiet dark chuckle escaped Silas’s lips—
Every single hair on the back of Thora’s neck instantly stood up on end.

Thora blinked her dark eyes, looking at him nervously.
"W-What the hell are you laughing like that for, My Lord...?"
Silas didn’t answer her.
He simply offered a calm innocent smile and swiped his hand through the air over the storage racks.

She scrambled across the foundry floor, throwing her heavy hammer aside, and popped open the heavy iron lid of the first crate.
Inside were rows of shimmering high-density metallic ingots pulsing with raw energy.
Thora pressed her face directly against the cool surface of the metallic ingots, taking a deep greedy breath of the raw ore fragrance.
"Ahhhh~!
Smells like raw metallic progress!" Thora cackled happily, rubbing her hands together.
"It’s not quite as high-grade as the pristine ores we mine ourselves from the deep Basin veins... but this will do nicely!
Hehehe!"
Silas watched her inspect the shipment, letting out a quiet sigh through his nose.
’Once this war with Sky is over...’ Silas reflected in his mind, ’...we definitely need to resume our deep mining operations in the Basin.’
Raw metal ores were the lifeblood of his territory’s infrastructure.
High-tier alloys allowed Thora to forge better armor for the girls, reinforce their siege weapons, and supply their casters with mana-conductive conduits.
’And on the bright side...’ Silas added in his thoughts, ’...I’m going to be receiving a massive influx of new women from this entire situation.’
Once the Lord War concluded and Sky was officially eliminated, Silas intended to dump his accumulated rewards directly into purchasing a massive batch of Troop Summoning Cards.

Expanding his Vanguard legion with fresh female units would give his territory the manpower needed to establish permanent mining outposts across the Umbral Basin as well as the 70 women he was receiving.
’And wait... right,’ Silas remembered, his golden eyes glinting. ’After the war, I’m also scheduled to meet the official World Council.’

When that meeting with the World Council eventually took place, Silas intended to leverage his Gold Core standing and roster to make a series of absurd, uncompromising, and downright crazy demands from the global governing body.
He couldn’t wait to see the looks on those arrogant council diplomats’ faces when he laid his demands on the table.
...But first, he had to crush Lord Sky’s mobile fortress.
"Hey, Lord!" Thora called out suddenly, snapping him out of his internal monologue.
Silas looked over at the dwarf.
"Yeah?"
Thora walked over to a velvet-lined display rack situated near her primary workbench... a rack reserved exclusively for custom master-work items stamped with the official crest of the Blessed Land.
She reached out, picking up a sleek shimmering metallic item wrapped in protective silk, and walked back over to Silas.
"I crafted something special for you," Thora announced proudly, her dwarven voice taking on a rare serious craftsman pitch.
"Or rather... for your Vespera form."
Silas raised an eyebrow.
"For Vespera?"
Thora carefully unrolled the silk wrapping, revealing a breathtaking piece of master-work armor.
It was a sleek silver-and-gold metallic Arm-Gauntlet... crafted from hyper-dense fluid-sculpted metal plates that swept from the fingertips all the way up to the shoulder joint.
The metal glistered with an indestructible, mirror-like sheen, etched with fine glowing arrays that hummed with passive defensive mana.
"Listen to me, My Lord," Thora explained seriously, pointing her calloused finger at the gauntlet.
"In an official Lord War against a guy like Sky, those bastards will try every single dirty, underhanded trick in the book to win.
And if you go out there fighting in your single-armed Vespera disguise... those enemy snipers and artillery casters are going to target your only good arm to try and disarm you."
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes widened slightly.
Thora was 100% correct...
In his single-armed Vespera persona, his right arm was his primary weapon conduit.
If an enemy sniper managed to sever or disable his right hand during combat, his combat efficiency in that form would drop significantly.
"So I forged this," Thora continued proudly, tapping the metallic sleeve.
"I made it using our specialized indestructible Sil-Grave Alloy.
It automatically deploys an instantaneous high-yield defense barrier whenever it senses an incoming strike!
With this on, no sniper in the Basin will ever be able to touch your hand."
Silas took the silver gauntlet into his hands, feeling its incredible light-weight balance and dense material structure.
A wave of genuine deep appreciation washed over Silas’s chest.
Thora might be a crude pervert 90% of the time... but as a Master Smith, her loyalty, foresight, and care for her Lord were absolute.
"Thank you, Thora," Silas said sincerely.
"This is genuinely brilliant work."
Silas leaned down, pressing a soft kiss directly onto the center of her dwarven forehead.
Thora froze dead in her tracks.
Her dark eyes widened, her pale cheeks exploding into a bright burning crimson flush as her dwarven brain completely short-circuited.
W-Well...!" Thora stammered out, her voice squeaking in total embarrassment.
In a fit of sudden madness...
Thora violently leaped backward two paces, bent her upper body completely forward, and stuck her large and curvaceous rear straight out into the air directly toward Silas’s face.
"I-IF YOU’RE THAT GRATEFUL, MY LORD..." Thora yelled out frantically, her face burning red.
"...YOU CAN SHOVE YOUR MEMBER STRAIGHT INTO MY ASS RIGHT NOW!
I’M ALREADY SOAKING WET ANYWAY!"
Silas stood there in the foundry, looking at the bent-over dwarf presenting her rear to him.
His golden-ringed eyes narrowed into a cold, flat, and thoroughly deadpan line.
Silas calmly raised his boot and delivered a swift, firm, and thoroughly unimpressed kick right to her exposed butt cheek.
BANG!
"OWWWWW!" Thora shrieked out, clutching her rear as she stumbled forward, pouting angrily at him over her shoulder.
"YOU’RE NO FUN, LORD!"

chapters.title: Chapter 286: Intruder
paragraphs: Before the wind mage could even turn her staff to defend herself...
FLASH!
A towering Blessed Wolf tore through the underbrush at high speed and riding on the back of that female Blessed Wolves was Morwenna.
The SSS-Rank Dread Queen didn’t even bother drawing her primary mythril cutlass.
She casually drew a simple iron side-saber from her hip, slashed forward at the big bat monster, and cut through it in an instant before the beast could even register her presence.
VWOOSH... THUD!
The massive bisected carcass crashed into the dirt with black blood pooling into the damp moss.
Morwenna reined in her Blessed Wolf, bringing the giant mount to a halt, and turned her stormy gray eyes toward the fourteen apprentice mages.
Her sharp face was unusually cold with her jaw set tight and her gaze radiating an intimidating reprimanding pressure that made every single girl in the clearing instantly straighten her posture.

"Pathetic!" Morwenna barked sharply, her voice cutting through the quiet forest like a whip. "You were all so busy celebrating your basic elemental volleys that none of you noticed an Alpha beast diving straight into your backline! If this were a real war against an organized army, Lia’s head would already be rolling in the mud!"
Lia swallowed hard, bowing her head deeply.
"I... I apologize, Instructor Morwenna!"
The surrounding mages exchanged nervous, thoroughly skeptical glances under their breath.
They noticed that Morwenna was being remarkably harsh today, almost as if she was deeply pissed off about something personal, and that made the girls quite skeptical.
It felt as though some intense, deep-seated frustration was boiling inside her chest, and she was using this field training session to vent her terrible mood on them.

None of the mages, of course, were aware that Morwenna was still internally reeling from Eluned’s humiliating bathroom confrontation earlier this morning... where the Nature Goddess had smugly flexed her red spank marks and listed off every single sexual position Silas had used on her while Morwenna had been lying unconscious.
Or perhaps they would have felt very sorry for her.
Morwenna rested her hand firmly on her sword pommel, her gray eyes sweeping over the quiet group.
"Listen up!" Morwenna commanded coldly. "Get ready to train... however, that is once we’ve dealt with the intruder."
Hearing her words, all fourteen mages instantly froze with their hands gripping their staffs tightly as their elemental mana flared to life.
Hidden within one of the trees... specifically the upper canopy of an ancient, moss-covered Ironwood tree fifty meters to their left was one of Sky’s Heroes.
He was an elven man wearing black clothes who was actively using nature magic to hide himself and scout on them.
He was channeling high-tier Nature Magic, fusing his mana signature directly with the tree bark and leaves to render himself completely invisible to any kind of sensory magic.
’How... how the hell did she spot me?!’ the elven scout panicked internally, his eyes widening in horror. ’I’m using a Tier 3 Nature Camouflage!’
Seeing Morwenna’s cold gray eyes locked directly onto his branch, the elven scout realized his cover was completely blown.
FWOOSH!
Without a second of hesitation, the scout kicked off the branch, triggering an explosive wind-step.
He turned into a green-and-black blur, shooting backward through the upper canopy at high speed, desperate to escape back to Sky’s territory.
Morwenna sat atop her Blessed Wolf with her hand resting casually on her saddle.
"I won’t step in," Morwenna declared coldly. "Handle him yourselves."
"YES, INSTRUCTOR!" the mages immediately yelled in agreement!
BOOM!
The entire caster team exploded into motion.
WHOOSH!
’I’ve gotten information I needed... I need to escape now!’
However escape in itself was easier said than done, though the man was convinced he could do it.
The elven scout leapt frantically from branch to branch, his neural reflexes firing at maximum capacity as he ran through the trees.
He looked over his shoulder, expecting to see a team of slow fragile squishy casters struggling to keep up through the thick underbrush far behind...
They were mages after all.
...Only for his jaw to drop in horror!
THUD! THUD! THUD!
The mages were not slowly chanting from a distance!

They were sprinting through the rugged terrain at terrifying superhuman physical speeds... leaping over fallen boulders, sliding under massive root systems, and vaulting off tree trunks like seasoned assassins.

’WHAT THE FUCK?!’ the elven scout screamed in his mind, his eyes bulging wide with shock as he stared at the fast-approaching women. ’ARE THEY REALLY MAGES?! WHY THE HELL ARE THEY RUNNING LIKE ROGUES?!’

Thanks to Silas’s continuous physical conditioning requirements, the buffs from Kaelia’s cooking, and their combat training, these mages were physical monsters compared to standard squishy spellcasters.
"He’s taking the high canopy! Block his line!" Valeria yelled, her messy red ponytail flying as she sprinted through the moss.
"On it!" Thalia shouted.
Thalia slammed both of her palms flat against the trunk of a massive oak tree as she ran past it.
"Earth-Pillar Eruption!"
KRA-KOOM!
A massive twenty-foot pillar of solid granite burst violently out of the dirt directly in front of the elven scout’s flight path.
"Gah!" the scout gasped, forcefully twisting his body mid-air to avoid colliding headfirst with the stone pillar.
That split-second maneuver completely ruined his momentum.
"Now! Drop him!" Lia commanded!
Lia swept her wooden staff through the air.
"Eat this... Vacuum Shear!"
A massive invisible blade of compressed wind sliced through the thick Ironwood branch beneath the scout’s boots.
CRACK... SNAP!
The heavy wooden branch snapped cleanly in half as the elven scout lost his footing, tumbling straight out of the canopy and falling thirty feet toward the forest floor!
"Gotcha, rat!" Seraina cackled wildly.
CRACKLE-BOOM!
Seraina fired a high-voltage bolt of purple lightning directly into his chest mid-fall.
BANG!
The electric shockwave shattered the scout’s black leather armor, scorching his skin and sending him crashing violently into the damp mud below.
THUD!
"Ugh... ghk!" the elven scout groaned, spitting a mouthful of blood as he frantically rolled onto his back. ’This... I need to run...’
In order to survive this fight, he needed to attack them.
The scout came to a stop, raising his hand and channeling his remaining nature mana to fire a volley of razor-sharp Thorn-Javelins and sweeping Razor-Vine Whips at his pursuers.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Three thick wooden javelins and sharp vines shot toward the advancing mages.
"On it..." Eliora stepped to the front, raising her crystal orb. "Glacial Shield!"
CRASH!
A thick wall of solid ice erupted from the mud, completely absorbing the thorn-javelins without taking a single crack.
"And we’re on the rest..."
Sybil and Maeve projected kinetic magic circles that deflected his vine whips like minor twigs, shrugging off his nature magic as if it were harmless dust.
Simultaneously, Venma stepped around the ice wall, twirling her bronze ring.
"Arcane Disruption Bolt!"
BOOM!
A pulse of raw arcane force slammed directly into the scout’s right shoulder, shattering his shoulder blade with a sickening sound and completely disabling his casting hand.
CRACK!
Before the scout could even scream in pain—
SWISH!
Morrigan emerged from the shadows behind him, her dark shadow-tendrils shooting out from the dirt to tightly bind his arms, legs, and torso, pinning him flat against the damp earth.
"This pervert was sneaking on us... Kill him!"
Valeria unleashed a concentrated point-blank heat pulse that scorched his side, while Calia slammed a high-pressure water sphere onto his chest to crush his ribs.
Ysolde and Aurelia added blinding mana burns that locked his nerves completely.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Within less than thirty seconds of spotted contact, the elite Guerilla Ranger had been hunted, intercepted, ambushed, and left bleeding in the mud, broken and helpless.
STEP! STEP!
The rhythmic thud of wolf paws echoed through the quiet clearing.
Morwenna rode over on the Blessed Wolf, stopping directly beside the bleeding battered elven scout.
She pointed the tip of her iron side-saber directly at the man’s neck.
"Do you want to live?"
The elven scout, paralyzed by the cold steel against his throat, his shattered shoulder, and his broken ribs, could barely nod as he was seriously injured.
"N-Yes... p-please... let me live..." the scout gasped out with blood trickling from the corner of his lips.
Morwenna held the sword against his throat for three long agonizing seconds.
Then... Morwenna’s cheeks blushed deeply.
A bright dark red flush spread across the SSS-Rank Dread Queen’s pale skin as her fierce terrifying aura instantly collapsed into an intensely awkward shyness.
She cleared her throat softly, leaning forward slightly in her saddle.
"What’s the best approach for a woman to ask her man for sex? If you answer this, I’ll let you go."
The whole clearing fell completely silent. The wind stopped blowing and the birds stopped chirping.
The mages stood in a wide circle around the clearing with their mouths wide open and their eyes bulging out of their skulls as they stared at the fierce Dread Queen.
"...Ah, I’ve never had se—"
BOOM!
Meanwhile, on the dusty border road leading toward the neutral buffer zone...
CLIP-CLOP... CLIP-CLOP.
Two Blessed Wolves walked side-by-side along the dirt trail with their heavy paws kicking up small clouds of dust under the bright morning sun.

Riding atop the lead wolf was Silas in his Vespera disguise and as of right now, Vespera wore a dark, high-collared traveler’s coat that draped gracefully over her broad yet elegant frame, paired with dark tailored trousers and tall leather riding boots.
Fitted securely over her right arm was the sleek silver-and-gold Sil-Grave Arm Guard that Thora had custom-forged earlier.
The indestructible alloy plate glinted brilliantly under the sunlight, fitting her hand and forearm perfectly.
Its embedded defense runes hummed with a subtle comforting warmth that resonated with her mana.
Riding beside her on the second Blessed Wolf was Rowenna.
The newly evolved S-Rank Grand Runemaster looked breathtakingly beautiful.
Her long silky dark hair cascaded past her shoulder in violet-tinted waves, and her mature voluptuous figure filled out her fresh robes to the brim.
Rowenna let out a soft happy breath, stroking the soft fur of her wolf’s neck as she looked over at the Lord.
"I really enjoy riding with you like this, My Lord," Rowenna admitted sweetly, her blue eyes sparkling with quiet affection as she looked at Vespera’s sharp side profile under the morning light.
Vespera, who was wearing the arm guard which fit her hand perfectly, smiled beneath her traveler’s hood.
"I’m glad you decided to tag along, Rowenna," Vespera replied smoothly. "And this arm guard Thora forged feels completely weightless."
Rowenna looked at the sleek silver gauntlet covering Vespera’s right arm, nodding her head enthusiastically.
"It looks absolutely stunning on you, My Lord. Thora’s craftsmanship is truly top-tier. It matches your aura flawlessly."
Vespera offered a warm comfortable smirk from beneath her coat hood.
"Thanks. She certainly knows her metalwork."
They were currently riding their Blessed Wolves over to Unmovable Wall, navigating the rocky terrain and winding paths of the border ridges.
As the two riders rounded the final stone bend leading into the open buffer zone, Rowenna tilted her head, sniffing the morning air curiously.
Up ahead, she could smell something really nice... it was smoking meat.
The rich mouth-watering aroma of slow-smoked barbecue, charred oak wood, savory glazes, and roasted herbs wafted across the morning breeze, entering their nostrils.
And then, they arrived at the Unmovable Wall territory...

Around the base of the mobile fortress, dozens of Sky’s civilian contractors, guards, and low-tier combatants were bustling about, attending to routine tread maintenance, hauling supply crates, and preparing field rations.
Upon seeing them here, the people recognized the single-armed Lord immediately, greeted her respectfully, and cleared a path to Sky.
"Clear the perimeter! Clear a path! It’s Lord Vespera!" one of the fortress guards shouted into a transceiver, hurriedly stepping back to clear a wide walkway for the two wolf riders.
Vespera reined in her Blessed Wolf, bringing the giant mount to a smooth halt near the edge of a grassy clearing beside the main fortress treads.
Sitting comfortably beneath the shade of two large Ironwood trees was Lord Sky, who was chilling in shorts and sitting under a hammock that he had put between two trees.
He was dressed in casual wearing dark sunglasses, a bright Hawaiian print shirt, and casual denim shorts, holding a cold glass of iced juice in his hand as he swung lazily in the shade.
And he sighed as she arrived, greeting her with a relaxed charismatic grin as he slid his sunglasses down the bridge of his nose even though he was wearing a mask.
"Man..." Sky drawled out, looking up from his hammock. "You really know how to make an entrance, Vespera."

VWOOSH...
THUD!
The massive bisected carcass crashed into the dirt with black blood pooling into the damp moss.
Morwenna reined in her Blessed Wolf, bringing the giant mount to a halt, and turned her stormy gray eyes toward the fourteen apprentice mages.
Her sharp face was unusually cold with her jaw set tight and her gaze radiating an intimidating reprimanding pressure that made every single girl in the clearing instantly straighten her posture.
"Pathetic!" Morwenna barked sharply, her voice cutting through the quiet forest like a whip.
"You were all so busy celebrating your basic elemental volleys that none of you noticed an Alpha beast diving straight into your backline!
If this were a real war against an organized army, Lia’s head would already be rolling in the mud!"
Lia swallowed hard, bowing her head deeply.
I apologize, Instructor Morwenna!"
The surrounding mages exchanged nervous, thoroughly skeptical glances under their breath.
They noticed that Morwenna was being remarkably harsh today, almost as if she was deeply pissed off about something personal, and that made the girls quite skeptical.
It felt as though some intense, deep-seated frustration was boiling inside her chest, and she was using this field training session to vent her terrible mood on them.

None of the mages, of course, were aware that Morwenna was still internally reeling from Eluned’s humiliating bathroom confrontation earlier this morning... where the Nature Goddess had smugly flexed her red spank marks and listed off every single sexual position Silas had used on her while Morwenna had been lying unconscious.
Or perhaps they would have felt very sorry for her.
Morwenna rested her hand firmly on her sword pommel, her gray eyes sweeping over the quiet group.
"Listen up!" Morwenna commanded coldly.
"Get ready to train... however, that is once we’ve dealt with the intruder."
Hearing her words, all fourteen mages instantly froze with their hands gripping their staffs tightly as their elemental mana flared to life.
Hidden within one of the trees... specifically the upper canopy of an ancient, moss-covered Ironwood tree fifty meters to their left was one of Sky’s Heroes.
He was an elven man wearing black clothes who was actively using nature magic to hide himself and scout on them.
He was channeling high-tier Nature Magic, fusing his mana signature directly with the tree bark and leaves to render himself completely invisible to any kind of sensory magic.
’How... how the hell did she spot me?!’ the elven scout panicked internally, his eyes widening in horror. ’I’m using a Tier 3 Nature Camouflage!’
Seeing Morwenna’s cold gray eyes locked directly onto his branch, the elven scout realized his cover was completely blown.
FWOOSH!
Without a second of hesitation, the scout kicked off the branch, triggering an explosive wind-step.
He turned into a green-and-black blur, shooting backward through the upper canopy at high speed, desperate to escape back to Sky’s territory.
Morwenna sat atop her Blessed Wolf with her hand resting casually on her saddle.
"I won’t step in," Morwenna declared coldly.
"Handle him yourselves."
"YES, INSTRUCTOR!" the mages immediately yelled in agreement!
BOOM!
The entire caster team exploded into motion.
WHOOSH!
’I’ve gotten information I needed...
I need to escape now!’
However escape in itself was easier said than done, though the man was convinced he could do it.
The elven scout leapt frantically from branch to branch, his neural reflexes firing at maximum capacity as he ran through the trees.
He looked over his shoulder, expecting to see a team of slow fragile squishy casters struggling to keep up through the thick underbrush far behind...
They were mages after all.
...Only for his jaw to drop in horror!
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
The mages were not slowly chanting from a distance!

They were sprinting through the rugged terrain at terrifying superhuman physical speeds... leaping over fallen boulders, sliding under massive root systems, and vaulting off tree trunks like seasoned assassins.
’WHAT THE FUCK?!’ the elven scout screamed in his mind, his eyes bulging wide with shock as he stared at the fast-approaching women. ’ARE THEY REALLY MAGES?!
WHY THE HELL ARE THEY RUNNING LIKE ROGUES?!’

Thanks to Silas’s continuous physical conditioning requirements, the buffs from Kaelia’s cooking, and their combat training, these mages were physical monsters compared to standard squishy spellcasters.
"He’s taking the high canopy!
Block his line!" Valeria yelled, her messy red ponytail flying as she sprinted through the moss.
"On it!" Thalia shouted.
Thalia slammed both of her palms flat against the trunk of a massive oak tree as she ran past it.
"Earth-Pillar Eruption!"
KRA-KOOM!
A massive twenty-foot pillar of solid granite burst violently out of the dirt directly in front of the elven scout’s flight path.
"Gah!" the scout gasped, forcefully twisting his body mid-air to avoid colliding headfirst with the stone pillar.
That split-second maneuver completely ruined his momentum.
"Now!
Drop him!" Lia commanded!
Lia swept her wooden staff through the air.
"Eat this...
Vacuum Shear!"
A massive invisible blade of compressed wind sliced through the thick Ironwood branch beneath the scout’s boots.
CRACK...
SNAP!
The heavy wooden branch snapped cleanly in half as the elven scout lost his footing, tumbling straight out of the canopy and falling thirty feet toward the forest floor!
"Gotcha, rat!" Seraina cackled wildly.
CRACKLE-BOOM!
Seraina fired a high-voltage bolt of purple lightning directly into his chest mid-fall.
BANG!
The electric shockwave shattered the scout’s black leather armor, scorching his skin and sending him crashing violently into the damp mud below.
THUD!
"Ugh... ghk!" the elven scout groaned, spitting a mouthful of blood as he frantically rolled onto his back. ’This...
I need to run...’
In order to survive this fight, he needed to attack them.
The scout came to a stop, raising his hand and channeling his remaining nature mana to fire a volley of razor-sharp Thorn-Javelins and sweeping Razor-Vine Whips at his pursuers.
SWISH!
SWISH!
SWISH!
Three thick wooden javelins and sharp vines shot toward the advancing mages.
"On it..." Eliora stepped to the front, raising her crystal orb.
"Glacial Shield!"
CRASH!
A thick wall of solid ice erupted from the mud, completely absorbing the thorn-javelins without taking a single crack.
"And we’re on the rest..."
Sybil and Maeve projected kinetic magic circles that deflected his vine whips like minor twigs, shrugging off his nature magic as if it were harmless dust.
Simultaneously, Venma stepped around the ice wall, twirling her bronze ring.
"Arcane Disruption Bolt!"
BOOM!
A pulse of raw arcane force slammed directly into the scout’s right shoulder, shattering his shoulder blade with a sickening sound and completely disabling his casting hand.
CRACK!
Before the scout could even scream in pain—
SWISH!
Morrigan emerged from the shadows behind him, her dark shadow-tendrils shooting out from the dirt to tightly bind his arms, legs, and torso, pinning him flat against the damp earth.
"This pervert was sneaking on us...
Kill him!"
Valeria unleashed a concentrated point-blank heat pulse that scorched his side, while Calia slammed a high-pressure water sphere onto his chest to crush his ribs.
Ysolde and Aurelia added blinding mana burns that locked his nerves completely.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
Within less than thirty seconds of spotted contact, the elite Guerilla Ranger had been hunted, intercepted, ambushed, and left bleeding in the mud, broken and helpless.
STEP!
STEP!
The rhythmic thud of wolf paws echoed through the quiet clearing.
Morwenna rode over on the Blessed Wolf, stopping directly beside the bleeding battered elven scout.
She pointed the tip of her iron side-saber directly at the man’s neck.
"Do you want to live?"
The elven scout, paralyzed by the cold steel against his throat, his shattered shoulder, and his broken ribs, could barely nod as he was seriously injured.
"N-Yes... p-please... let me live..." the scout gasped out with blood trickling from the corner of his lips.
Morwenna held the sword against his throat for three long agonizing seconds.
Then...
Morwenna’s cheeks blushed deeply.
A bright dark red flush spread across the SSS-Rank Dread Queen’s pale skin as her fierce terrifying aura instantly collapsed into an intensely awkward shyness.
She cleared her throat softly, leaning forward slightly in her saddle.
"What’s the best approach for a woman to ask her man for sex?
If you answer this, I’ll let you go."
The whole clearing fell completely silent.
The wind stopped blowing and the birds stopped chirping.
The mages stood in a wide circle around the clearing with their mouths wide open and their eyes bulging out of their skulls as they stared at the fierce Dread Queen.
"...Ah, I’ve never had se—"
BOOM!
Meanwhile, on the dusty border road leading toward the neutral buffer zone...
CLIP-CLOP...
CLIP-CLOP.
Two Blessed Wolves walked side-by-side along the dirt trail with their heavy paws kicking up small clouds of dust under the bright morning sun.

Riding atop the lead wolf was Silas in his Vespera disguise and as of right now, Vespera wore a dark, high-collared traveler’s coat that draped gracefully over her broad yet elegant frame, paired with dark tailored trousers and tall leather riding boots.
Fitted securely over her right arm was the sleek silver-and-gold Sil-Grave Arm Guard that Thora had custom-forged earlier.
The indestructible alloy plate glinted brilliantly under the sunlight, fitting her hand and forearm perfectly.
Its embedded defense runes hummed with a subtle comforting warmth that resonated with her mana.
Riding beside her on the second Blessed Wolf was Rowenna.
The newly evolved S-Rank Grand Runemaster looked breathtakingly beautiful.
Her long silky dark hair cascaded past her shoulder in violet-tinted waves, and her mature voluptuous figure filled out her fresh robes to the brim.
Rowenna let out a soft happy breath, stroking the soft fur of her wolf’s neck as she looked over at the Lord.
"I really enjoy riding with you like this, My Lord," Rowenna admitted sweetly, her blue eyes sparkling with quiet affection as she looked at Vespera’s sharp side profile under the morning light.
Vespera, who was wearing the arm guard which fit her hand perfectly, smiled beneath her traveler’s hood.
"I’m glad you decided to tag along, Rowenna," Vespera replied smoothly.
"And this arm guard Thora forged feels completely weightless."
Rowenna looked at the sleek silver gauntlet covering Vespera’s right arm, nodding her head enthusiastically.
"It looks absolutely stunning on you, My Lord.
Thora’s craftsmanship is truly top-tier.
It matches your aura flawlessly."
Vespera offered a warm comfortable smirk from beneath her coat hood.
"Thanks.
She certainly knows her metalwork."
They were currently riding their Blessed Wolves over to Unmovable Wall, navigating the rocky terrain and winding paths of the border ridges.
As the two riders rounded the final stone bend leading into the open buffer zone, Rowenna tilted her head, sniffing the morning air curiously.
Up ahead, she could smell something really nice... it was smoking meat.
The rich mouth-watering aroma of slow-smoked barbecue, charred oak wood, savory glazes, and roasted herbs wafted across the morning breeze, entering their nostrils.
And then, they arrived at the Unmovable Wall territory...

Around the base of the mobile fortress, dozens of Sky’s civilian contractors, guards, and low-tier combatants were bustling about, attending to routine tread maintenance, hauling supply crates, and preparing field rations.
Upon seeing them here, the people recognized the single-armed Lord immediately, greeted her respectfully, and cleared a path to Sky.
"Clear the perimeter!
Clear a path!
It’s Lord Vespera!" one of the fortress guards shouted into a transceiver, hurriedly stepping back to clear a wide walkway for the two wolf riders.
Vespera reined in her Blessed Wolf, bringing the giant mount to a smooth halt near the edge of a grassy clearing beside the main fortress treads.
Sitting comfortably beneath the shade of two large Ironwood trees was Lord Sky, who was chilling in shorts and sitting under a hammock that he had put between two trees.
He was dressed in casual wearing dark sunglasses, a bright Hawaiian print shirt, and casual denim shorts, holding a cold glass of iced juice in his hand as he swung lazily in the shade.
And he sighed as she arrived, greeting her with a relaxed charismatic grin as he slid his sunglasses down the bridge of his nose even though he was wearing a mask.
"Man..." Sky drawled out, looking up from his hammock.
"You really know how to make an entrance, Vespera."

chapters.title: Chapter 287: Vespera On Stream [I]
paragraphs: "I don’t know much about flashy entrances, Sky," Vespera replied smoothly, her voice carrying a calm tone from beneath her dark hood. "I just ride where the business takes me."
She reined in her Blessed Wolf, bringing Valkyrie to a smooth silent halt beside the main treads of the rolling mobile fortress.
Rowenna pulled up alongside her with Luna’s heavy paws kicking up a faint cloud of dry dust against the morning grass.
Vespera tilted her head with her sharp eyes scanning the streaming Lord lounging in the hammock before her.
’Is it just me or does Sky seem a bit more casual...’

Sky was wearing his signature streaming mask... the sleek dark face and silver-shield designed to transmit clean audio feeds to his network servers yet perched right over the eye-lenses of the mask was a pair of dark designer sunglasses.

Combined with a loud, brightly colored Hawaiian print shirt, baggy denim shorts, and casual sandals, the man looked less like a battle-hardened Classic Lord preparing for a territory war and more like a tourist relaxing at a seaside resort.
Vespera couldn’t help but let out a dry amused breath through her nose, pointing a gauntleted finger toward his face.

"Though I have to ask..." Vespera remarked, her voice dripping with sarcasm, "...are the sunglasses really necessary over a full-face streaming mask? Especially when paired with a beach shirt in the middle of a war zone?"
Sky let out a loud laugh, adjusting the dark frames over his mask with a flick of his wrist.

"It’s called brand synergy, Vespera!" Sky defended cheerfully, leaning back against the hammock ropes as he took another sip of his iced juice through a straw. "The network chat eats this stuff up! Contrast is everything in live entertainment... A masked Lord chilling in tropical gear brings in forty percent more viewer retention than a guy sitting around in heavy plate armor looking miserable. You gotta respect the grind."
’Again, he seems a bit more casual... am I missing something?’
Sky then shifted his posture, sliding his sunglasses slightly down the bridge of his mask as his gaze drifted past Vespera, landing squarely on Rowenna.
The Grand Runemaster sat gracefully atop her Blessed Wolf, her long silky dark hair cascading past her shoulder in shimmering violet-tinted waves.
Her newly evolved S-Rank figure filled out her fresh arcanist robes to an eye-popping brim with her mature features radiating an effortless divine elegance under the morning sun.
Sky’s jaw subtly dropped behind his mask. He shook his head in genuine bewilderment.

"Where on earth do you even find women like this?" Sky asked, shaking his head with a wide, appreciative grin. "First that shadow user from our border skirmish, and now this breathtaking mage... your territory is quite stacked."
Vespera laughed smoothly with her deep voice completely composed as she dismounted from her Blessed Wolf.

Her commanding frame stepped onto the grass, and she reached up with her broad right hand... covered in Thora’s indestructible silver-and-gold Sil-Grave Arm Guard offering a firm, steady grip to assist Rowenna down from her mount.

"I’ll take that as praise," Vespera remarked, carefully steadying Rowenna as the Grand Runemaster’s boots touched the turf. "A Lord has to surround himself with capable personnel if she expects to build an empire out here."
Rowenna offered Vespera a sweet devoted smile, smoothing down her arcanist robes before stepping back to stand half a pace behind her Lord in a quiet protective stance.
Once Rowenna was safely situated, Vespera turned back to Sky, cutting straight through the casual banter to address the core purpose of her visit.
"Let’s get down to business, Sky," Vespera stated firmly, folding her single arm over her chest. "Do you have Obsidian-Slate Stone in your material holds?"
Sky took a slow deliberate sip of his iced juice, adjusting his position in the hammock as he looked at her.

"Obsidian-Slate Stone?" Sky replied, tilting his head thoughtfully. "Ah, yes I do! I’ve got plenty of that sitting in my lower material holds. It’s high-density, fire-resistant granite from the deep quarry veins. Stuff is blast-proof and heavy as hell. How many units do you need for your territory?"
Vespera looked Sky directly in the eyes, stating her requirement clearly without a single shred of hesitation.
"I’m going to need a lot. Let’s say... a minimum of two thousand units."
"Ghk!"
Sky literally choked on his iced juice.
He sat up so violently in his hammock that the woven ropes swung wildly from side to side as he snatched off his dark sunglasses, staring at Vespera in shock.

"Two thousand units?!" Sky gasped out, coughing slightly as he wiped a stray drop of juice from his helmet. "Damn, Vespera! What the hell are you building over there, a nuclear fallout shelter... That’s a serious chunk of my heavy raw construction stock."
In truth, Silas didn’t technically need 2,000 units just to complete his immediate project. Or did he? He was not sure it was up to.
The blueprint for the Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters only required 300 units of Obsidian-Slate Stone to construct the main residential foundations for his Vanguard recruits.
However, Silas’s brain was thinking three steps ahead.

Securing a massive 2,000-unit surplus would allow him to permanently reinforce the Keep’s perimeter walls, lay granite foundations for high-tier defensive spell towers, supply Thora’s foundry with stone-alloys that she could probably use to cook something crazy, and expand the territory’s overall infrastructure without running out of material mid-build.
Sky swung his legs over the edge of the hammock, stepping down onto the grassy turf in his casual sandals.
He walked a slow appreciative circle around Vespera with his sharp eyes inspecting her outfit from top to bottom.
’Hm... Ah yes...’
He noticed that Vespera was wearing the exact set of high-grade modern Earth traveler’s apparel he had given to her during their previous meeting... This was only one of course.
A dark tailored traveler’s coat that draped over her broad frame, paired with fitted trousers and tall leather boots that complemented her single-armed posture and gleaming silver gauntlet.
Sky offered an appreciative charismatic smirk.

"Looking good in that gear, by the way," Sky added, gesturing with his hand toward her coat. "I wasn’t sure if modern Earth fashion would suit you, but you rock that single-armed coat look like a boss. The tailored cut really sells the mysterious traveler aesthetic."
Vespera glanced down at her sleeve, adjusting her collar with a cool indifferent flick of her wrist.
"It’s functional gear. It’s far better than clanking around in heavy obsolete iron plate."
Sky set his juice glass down on a nearby metal supply crate, stepping over to lean his shoulder casually against the trunk of a massive Ironwood tree.
He crossed his arms over his bright Hawaiian shirt, offering a sly business-driven merchant grin beneath his mask.

"Look, as I was saying..." Sky continued smoothly, his voice taking on the polished edge of a veteran content creator. "...I do have the two thousand units of Obsidian-Slate Stone sitting right down in my lower holds. I’m completely down to trade the whole lot over to you. But... you’re going to have to do me a little favor first."
Vespera’s eyes twitched slightly beneath her dark traveler’s hood.
"Another Stream?" Vespera asked dryly. She was well aware that this was what it was but still, why was Sky acting like this? Was the man perhaps drunk?
Sky snapped his fingers in the air with an explosive burst of enthusiasm, his face mask lighting up with a subtle digital indicator.
"Bingo!" Sky declared with a boisterous laugh. "Yes, actually! Another stream! Though it’s nothing serious, I promise!"
Sky stepped closer, throwing his hands up in excitement as he pitched the deal.

"Look, Vespera, my network chat numbers went absolutely nuclear the last time you appeared on my feed... The chat clips went viral across three different streaming platforms. My viewers and subscribers are practically begging to see the mysterious single-armed Lord again."
’I’m happy that he’s at least honest.’
Sky paced across the grass, gesturing animatedly as he continued.

"It’s just a simple five-minute co-host segment to hype up the network before our official Lord War next week! No combat required, no territory secrets revealed... just a quick Q&A banter session to drive my subscriber numbers through the roof. You get your two thousand units of high-density granite, and I get top-tier network engagement! It’s a win-win for both of us!"
Vespera stood in the grassy clearing, looking at the hyperactive streaming Lord, and let out a soft long sigh through her nose.
Inside Silas’s mind, a quick calculation took place.

2,000 units of high-density Obsidian-Slate Stone was an extraordinary logistical haul... one that would accelerate the Blessed Land’s development by a lot and for that structure, he really didn’t need UP as it was already good the way it was or so he thought.
Spending five minutes answering basic questions on a live broadcast revealed absolutely nothing about his hidden S-Ranks and SSS-Rank military roster.
It was a completely harmless exchange that secured an immense structural advantage for his territory.
Vespera looked Sky dead in the eyes, offering a cool and confident smirk from beneath her hood.
"Alright, Sky," Vespera agreed smoothly, resting her gauntleted right hand against her belt. "Bring out the camera."
"Do we really need to go this far with the outfit?" Vespera asked, tugging gently at the silk collar of the dark double-breasted suit jacket fitted across her shoulders.
She was currently sitting down on a cushioned leather chair set up right beside the massive, iron treads of The Unmovable Wall.
The modern, charcoal-black suit had been pulled directly from Sky’s high-end Earth apparel supply crates, tailored precisely to fit her commanding figure.
It gave her an aura that was equal parts corporate executive and a Lord, complemented by the gleaming silver-and-gold sheen of the Sil-Grave Arm Guard encasing her right forearm.
Directly beside her, Lord Sky was bustling around a folding wooden table, adjusting a secondary leather chair so it sat flush with hers.
He turned his head, his full-face streaming mask reflecting the morning light while the pair of dark designer sunglasses rested squarely over the mask’s eye-lenses.
Combined with his loud, tropical Hawaiian print shirt and casual shorts, he looked like an eccentric media mogul hosting a beachside talk show in the middle of the basin.
Sky stopped adjusting the table, leaning his hands on his hips as he looked at her outfit.

"Look, Vespera, we definitely have to look formal for this," Sky told her, waving a gloved hand dismissively. "After all, you are the Sovereign Lord of the Blessed Land... Even though this Q and A session is only going to be about five minutes long, it’s going to decide a lot of things for your territory’s standing. Image is everything when you’re dealing with the higher-ups."
Sky tilted his head slightly, his sunglasses glinting under the morning sun.
"Besides, you wanted to establish a line with the World Council and claim that bounty, right?"
Vespera rolled her shoulders, leaning back against the leather headrest with a dry smirk.
"Calling it a ’Bounty’ just makes it sound quite illegal," Vespera said, her deep, smooth voice carrying a cool edge beneath her hood.
Sky let out a loud jovial laugh, waving his hand off dismissively as he took his seat in the adjacent leather chair right next to her.

"Semantics, my friend! Just semantics..." Sky joked off easily, settling into his seat and leaning toward her. "In the eyes of the World Council, a Lord occupying a zone like the Umbral Basin is either a rogue element or a prime candidate for official integration. We’re just turning the formal process into a high-grade media event!"
Sky reached up, tapping the frame of his sunglasses as he glanced over at her. "So, Vespera... are you ready?"
Vespera let out a quiet breath through her nose, settling her single gauntleted hand over her lap.
"Well," Vespera told him, her purple eyes calm beneath her hood. "Better now than ever."
Over on the sidelines, ten paces away near the Blessed Wolf mounts, Rowenna stood watching silently.
The Grand Runemaster, looking breathtaking in her violet robes, caught Vespera’s gaze and gave her a warm, encouraging smile, raising a subtle thumb-up.
Vespera noticed the gesture, lifting her single gauntleted right hand in a calm wave back at Rowenna before turning her full attention back to the streaming Lord beside her.

"Alright, before I open the live signal, let me give you a quick heads-up on who’s actually attending this Q and A," Sky told her, leaning closer and lowering his voice slightly behind his mask. "There are going to be several high-ranking people tuning into the private feed, but the two notable people you need to pay attention to are real heavyweights."

He crossed his arms over his bright Hawaiian shirt, offering a sly business-driven merchant grin beneath his mask.
"Look, as I was saying..." Sky continued smoothly, his voice taking on the polished edge of a veteran content creator.
"...I do have the two thousand units of Obsidian-Slate Stone sitting right down in my lower holds.
I’m completely down to trade the whole lot over to you.
But... you’re going to have to do me a little favor first."
Vespera’s eyes twitched slightly beneath her dark traveler’s hood.
"Another Stream?" Vespera asked dryly.
She was well aware that this was what it was but still, why was Sky acting like this?
Was the man perhaps drunk?
Sky snapped his fingers in the air with an explosive burst of enthusiasm, his face mask lighting up with a subtle digital indicator.
"Bingo!" Sky declared with a boisterous laugh.
"Yes, actually!
Another stream!
Though it’s nothing serious, I promise!"
Sky stepped closer, throwing his hands up in excitement as he pitched the deal.
"Look, Vespera, my network chat numbers went absolutely nuclear the last time you appeared on my feed...
The chat clips went viral across three different streaming platforms.
My viewers and subscribers are practically begging to see the mysterious single-armed Lord again."
’I’m happy that he’s at least honest.’
Sky paced across the grass, gesturing animatedly as he continued.
"It’s just a simple five-minute co-host segment to hype up the network before our official Lord War next week!
No combat required, no territory secrets revealed... just a quick Q&A banter session to drive my subscriber numbers through the roof.
You get your two thousand units of high-density granite, and I get top-tier network engagement!
It’s a win-win for both of us!"
Vespera stood in the grassy clearing, looking at the hyperactive streaming Lord, and let out a soft long sigh through her nose.
Inside Silas’s mind, a quick calculation took place.

2,000 units of high-density Obsidian-Slate Stone was an extraordinary logistical haul... one that would accelerate the Blessed Land’s development by a lot and for that structure, he really didn’t need UP as it was already good the way it was or so he thought.
Spending five minutes answering basic questions on a live broadcast revealed absolutely nothing about his hidden S-Ranks and SSS-Rank military roster.
It was a completely harmless exchange that secured an immense structural advantage for his territory.
Vespera looked Sky dead in the eyes, offering a cool and confident smirk from beneath her hood.
"Alright, Sky," Vespera agreed smoothly, resting her gauntleted right hand against her belt.
"Bring out the camera."
"Do we really need to go this far with the outfit?" Vespera asked, tugging gently at the silk collar of the dark double-breasted suit jacket fitted across her shoulders.
She was currently sitting down on a cushioned leather chair set up right beside the massive, iron treads of The Unmovable Wall.
The modern, charcoal-black suit had been pulled directly from Sky’s high-end Earth apparel supply crates, tailored precisely to fit her commanding figure.
It gave her an aura that was equal parts corporate executive and a Lord, complemented by the gleaming silver-and-gold sheen of the Sil-Grave Arm Guard encasing her right forearm.
Directly beside her, Lord Sky was bustling around a folding wooden table, adjusting a secondary leather chair so it sat flush with hers.
He turned his head, his full-face streaming mask reflecting the morning light while the pair of dark designer sunglasses rested squarely over the mask’s eye-lenses.
Combined with his loud, tropical Hawaiian print shirt and casual shorts, he looked like an eccentric media mogul hosting a beachside talk show in the middle of the basin.
Sky stopped adjusting the table, leaning his hands on his hips as he looked at her outfit.
"Look, Vespera, we definitely have to look formal for this," Sky told her, waving a gloved hand dismissively.
"After all, you are the Sovereign Lord of the Blessed Land...
Even though this Q and A session is only going to be about five minutes long, it’s going to decide a lot of things for your territory’s standing.
Image is everything when you’re dealing with the higher-ups."
Sky tilted his head slightly, his sunglasses glinting under the morning sun.
"Besides, you wanted to establish a line with the World Council and claim that bounty, right?"
Vespera rolled her shoulders, leaning back against the leather headrest with a dry smirk.
"Calling it a ’Bounty’ just makes it sound quite illegal," Vespera said, her deep, smooth voice carrying a cool edge beneath her hood.
Sky let out a loud jovial laugh, waving his hand off dismissively as he took his seat in the adjacent leather chair right next to her.
"Semantics, my friend!
Just semantics..." Sky joked off easily, settling into his seat and leaning toward her.
"In the eyes of the World Council, a Lord occupying a zone like the Umbral Basin is either a rogue element or a prime candidate for official integration.
We’re just turning the formal process into a high-grade media event!"
Sky reached up, tapping the frame of his sunglasses as he glanced over at her.
"So, Vespera... are you ready?"
Vespera let out a quiet breath through her nose, settling her single gauntleted hand over her lap.
"Well," Vespera told him, her purple eyes calm beneath her hood.
"Better now than ever."
Over on the sidelines, ten paces away near the Blessed Wolf mounts, Rowenna stood watching silently.
The Grand Runemaster, looking breathtaking in her violet robes, caught Vespera’s gaze and gave her a warm, encouraging smile, raising a subtle thumb-up.
Vespera noticed the gesture, lifting her single gauntleted right hand in a calm wave back at Rowenna before turning her full attention back to the streaming Lord beside her.
"Alright, before I open the live signal, let me give you a quick heads-up on who’s actually attending this Q and A," Sky told her, leaning closer and lowering his voice slightly behind his mask.
"There are going to be several high-ranking people tuning into the private feed, but the two notable people you need to pay attention to are real heavyweights."

chapters.title: Chapter 288: Vespera On Stream [II]
paragraphs: Vespera raised a subtle eyebrow beneath her hood. "Who are we talking about?"

"First up is Etilga from the Bloom Clan," Sky explained smoothly. "She’s an influential matriarchal figure in high-tier council politics and the mother of the famous Seraphina Bloom... you know the prodigy Lord who went on that big Secret Realm expedition as of late?"
The moment Sky uttered those words, Vespera flinched a bit beneath her traveler’s hood.
Seraphina’s mother?!

Inside Vespera’s mind, Silas’s thoughts instantly began to race. He vividly remembered Seraphina from their past encounter... a loud superheated fire caster with an attitude that could melt concrete and a fuse shorter than a firecracker.

’Seraphina’s mother...?’ Silas imagined in his head with a massive sweatdrop forming behind his forehead. ’If Seraphina is already that intensely loud, obnoxious, and short-tempered, I can only imagine how her mother sounds... And do they have something against me too? Was Valerius able to calm her down?’
All of his hopes were on Valerius!
"And who’s the second person?" Vespera asked, keeping her external tone completely smooth and collected.

"The second person entering the Q and A is from the Sterling Family," Sky continued, clicking his tongue. "It’s the head of the house himself... a man who happens to be the father of the well-known Valerius Sterling. The guy is the owner and founder of one of the biggest corporate conglomerates in all of Lord Society... Lohan Sterling."
Valerius’s father?!
Vespera’s golden-ringed eyes flickered with genuine intrigue beneath her dark hood.
Speak of the devil, she had just been thinking about Valerius just now... Vespera couldn’t help but wonder what happened to him though, was he at home? At his territory?
They were friends after all, at least she thought they were... Since Valerius was like that, Vespera couldn’t help but wonder what his pops was like.
’Considering how chill Valerius turned out to be,’ Silas mused inwardly, ’I’m actually pretty damn intrigued about meeting his dad.’
Vespera turned her head toward Sky with her expression narrowing slightly.
"Is there anybody else I should know about that’s in this Q and A too? Having the heads of two major family clans feels a bit too heavy for a mere five-minute stream."
Sky chuckled, shaking his head casually behind his mask.
"Nope! Those are the only two people who bought out the private interview slot. I kept the panel small so we didn’t end up with a fifty-person political circus."
Vespera took a deep centering breath, letting her chest rise and fall beneath her suit jacket.
She was doing this strictly for the Obsidian-Slate Stone.
Nothing more, nothing less. Two thousand units of high-density granite was a massive structural upgrade for the Keep, and enduring a five-minute interview was a dirt-cheap price to pay...
Vespera turned her head back to Sky.
"I’m ready!"
"Alright, chat! Let’s make some history!" Sky declared with a grin.
Sky reached up and tapped the side of his head near his temple, triggering the stream interface.
HUMMM!
In an instant, three sleek silver streaming drones hovering above The Unmovable Wall dropped down in a smooth arc.
Their optical sensors enabled instantly, snapping into formation directly in front of the two chairs with glowing blue LED rings locking onto Vespera and Sky.

Vespera stiffened slightly as the high-definition camera lenses snapped right into her face, but she quickly forced her posture to remain completely relaxed, crossing her legs in her suit like an unshakeable ruler.
In front of them, a massive semi-transparent holographic screen projected into the air, displaying the live network broadcast interface.
The moment the stream started, the viewer counter in the top-right corner didn’t just tick up... it exploded instantly.
In the exact instant that the broadcast signal went live, it already had ten million viewers watching simultaneously?
Sky leaned toward her, whispering under his breath so the audio pick-up wouldn’t register.
"I scheduled the stream notification an hour ago. They’ve been waiting in the lobby the whole time."
Vespera let out a quiet internal sigh.
It was almost as if Sky had known all along that she was going to meet him for something today and had pre-marketed the entire visit to maximize his viewers.
’Can’t blame the player though... He is hustling.’
On the floating holographic screen, an avalanche of live stream comments greeted them, cascading down the window at blinding speed.
Sky flashed a brilliant, camera-ready smile, raising his gloved hand toward the central drone lens.

"Welcome back, everyone, to another emergency live broadcast!" Sky announced with infectious, practiced energy. "Today, we have an extraordinary co-host joining us live from the neutral border... the ruler of the Blessed Land, Lord Vespera!"
Vespera raised her single gauntleted right hand toward the camera, offering a calm composed wave to the audience.
"Good morning, everyone," Vespera greeted smoothly, her rich voice resonating clearly through the stream’s audio channels.

[Run_Fanatic]: SHE IS WEARING A SUIT?! A DOUBLE-BREASTED SUIT WITH A GOLD GAUNTLET IS ABSOLUTE DRIP!
[Gamer_Tag_44]: GOOD MORNING WARLORD VESPERA!

[Simp_For_Vespera]: It’s nighttime for me Mommy Vespera! I would really like it if Mommy Vespera gave me a goodnight kiss before I go to sleep! 😭❤️
Vespera’s sharp eyes caught that specific comment pointing out it was nighttime for him and asking for a goodnight kiss.
Her lips immediately thinned into a flat rigid line beneath her dark traveler’s hood.
Inside her head, Silas’s soul was screaming in aconfusion.

’This... this isn’t gay, is it?!’ Silas panicked internally, his mind doing rapid mental cartwheels. ’Technically I’m operating under the female Vespera persona right now, but I’m still a guy inside... Is blowing a kiss to a random male viewer on a live stream crossing a line?!’
Silas quickly forced himself to calm down.
Vespera was a public brand, and maintaining her fierce and beloved reputation was essential for long-term territory diplomacy.
Vespera let out a soft amused breath, lifting her single gauntleted hand to her lips and blowing a subtle elegant kiss toward the main camera drone.
"Sleep well then," Vespera added with a smooth playful smirk.
BOOM!
The chat box went feral.
[Simp_For_Vespera]: AHHHHHHHHHH SHE ACTUALLY DID IT! SHE BLEW ME A KISS! I AM ASCENDING TO HEAVEN!
[Runii_Tanc]: MOMMY ME TOO~!
[Vanguard_Watcher]: MOMMY ME TOO~ PLEASE BLOW ONE TO ME TOO!
[Shadow_Lover]: MOMMY ME TOO~ I NEED A GOODNIGHT KISS TOO!
[Glaze_Master_3000]: LORD VESPERA IS THE GREATEST LORD TO EVER EXIST! STEP ON ME MOMMY!
[No_Life_Lord]: BEST DAY OF MY ENTIRE LIFE HANDS DOWN!
[Sovereign_Watcher]: THE DRIP! THE VOICE! THE GAUNTLET! WE ARE NOT WORTHY!
Watching the endless waterfall of comments saying "Mommy me too~" and glazing her to an absurd degree, Silas sighed deeply in his own head.
’Damn...’ Silas grumbled internally, staring at the chaotic chat log. ’When the hell are these VIPs actually going to get here?’
Silas would really like it very much if he didn’t have to work so hard just to get a hold of the materials he needed.
Here he was, sitting in a suit in the middle of a forest, blowing kisses to random internet weirdos on a live stream, all for two thousand units of construction stone.
However, it seemed like just when he had started to get comfortable in this realm, the world had decided to show him its massive middle finger once again.
PING! PING!
Suddenly, the chat interface on the holographic screen was split to the side!
A pair of high-priority gold-bordered notification banners flashed across the top of the display with a loud audio chime.
[User ’SterlingLo’ has requested to join the stream stage!]
[User ’BLOOM’ has requested to join the stream stage!]
Sky’s eyes glinted behind his mask.
"They’re here..."
Vespera gave him a firm decisive nod.
"Accept them."
Sky tapped his mask interface, hitting the stage confirmation key.
HUMMM!
Two new video tabs came on screen instantly, expanding on either side of the central camera feed.
The left video tab illuminated, showing a middle-aged man who looked like a very elegant noble with pristine blond hair and sharp green eyes.
He was sitting inside a very luxurious white-marble room, dressed in an impeccably tailored expensive white suit with gold cufflinks.
Vespera stared at his video feed, her lips twitching slightly beneath her hood.
’Fucking rich dudes and showing off...’ Vespera thought dryly.
It was always them trying to show the whole world that they had unlimited funds.
Honestly, Silas knew in his heart that he only hated it because he wasn’t rich as well. If he was rich, he for sure would show it off just like this guy.
Vespera almost shook her head in frustration as another annoying thought crossed her mind.
Imagine being the most popular Lord in the New Category, capable of pulling these kind of viewers on a random broadcast, and not even earning a single dime off it!

Vespera would have already started asking this guy Sky to share stream income fifty-fifty, however Silas hadn’t even come close to finalizing a proper account or identity for Vespera in the real world outside the Sovereign Realm, so there was a lot of shit to clear up first.
’I seriously need guidance in that aspect...’ Vespera thought bitterly.
Though for that, she would need to trust someone capable with her real identity but who was she to trust in a world full of snakes and corporate vultures?
Trust Sky? He could turn that real-identity reveal straight into a viral stream or a three-part video series for extra views...
Or trust any other noble clan? They’d immediately use that information to blackmail, extort, or legally corner her territory in the real world...
Vespera almost clawed out her hair beneath her hood in pure frustration... Why did life have to be so damn confusing?
Her attention was abruptly yanked away as the second video tab on the right side of the screen fully loaded.
The second tab was with a crimson-haired woman who looked like an older, far more mature image of Seraphina.
Seraphina was a literal spitting image of her for sure.
She had long, fiery red hair cascading over her shoulders and what looked like a thin cigar in her mouth, puffing grey smoke into the air.
She was sitting down in a luxurious, red-velvet room, but the camera was zoomed away from her a bit... revealing that she was sitting down on someone.
Vespera had to wipe her eyes to see properly.
Was she... was she actually sitting on a living man?!
And wasn’t that man wearing high-tier formal robes? Wasn’t that a Magistrate of the World Council crawling on all fours beneath her boots like a human footstool?!
’Damn...’ Vespera thought in stunned disbelief. ’It seems women from the Bloom Family have a kink for shaming their husbands...’
However, regardless of their bizarre personal habits, they were all here for the Q and A now!
The moment both VIP streams synchronized with the main broadcast...
BOOM!
In an instant, the live viewer counter spiked to over one hundred million viewers!
The massive, nine-digit number flashed bright red on the display, making Vespera’s throat go a bit dry beneath her high collar.
She couldn’t even blame the viewers at this point.

Too many insane, incomprehensible things were happening on this stream all at once... a single-armed Lord in a suit, a masked streamer in Hawaiian shorts, a billionaire noble in a white suit, and a crimson-haired matriarch sitting on a World Council Magistrate like a couch.
On the right feed, the poor World Council Magistrate beneath Etilga shifted slightly, his face red with humiliation as he tried to speak up toward her camera lens.
"Etilga, please!" the Magistrate groaned with his voice trembling. "My spine is cramping, and we are broadcasting live! Let me at least sit up—"
THWACK!
Etilga didn’t even look down.
She casually lifted her booted heel and delivered a sharp violent stomp directly into his ribs, slamming him flat back onto the floor.

"Shut your pathetic mouth, Harold!" Etilga barked coldly, taking a slow drag from her cigar and exhaling smoke toward the screen. "Did I give you permission to open your mouth during my broadcast? Keep your back flat and be a proper cushion!"
