Beside her, Rowenna stepped up to her own mount, Luna, fluidly climbing into the saddle and taking the reins with ease.
"Let’s head home, Rowenna," Vespera instructed softly.
"Understood, My Lord," Rowenna replied sweetly.

With a sharp tug on the reins, the two riders turned their giant Blessed Wolves around, kicking up small clouds of dust as they trotted away from The Unmovable Wall, disappearing into the dense forest paths leading back toward the Blessed Land.
Standing near the edge of the clearing, Lord Sky stood watching their retreating backs as the two wolf riders disappeared into the dark Ironwood canopy.
Sky reached up, slowly sliding off his dark sunglasses, his full-face streaming mask reflecting the shadowy forest horizon.
Beneath his mask, Sky’s face twisted into an intensely frustrated stress-filled grimace.
"Fuck..." Sky muttered under his breath, his voice laced with deep simmering anxiety.
Sky was a master at reading people, but Vespera was an enigma.
Every single time she visited his territory, she brought along a completely new, absurdly powerful individual...
Last time, it had been that silent shadow assassin who radiated an overwhelming physical killing intent and next it had been the Jade Beauty with ice magic.
Today, she had brought along this breathtaking woman in arcanist robes.
And yet...
Sky hadn’t managed to catch even a brief, passing flicker of what class or elemental discipline this new woman actually possessed.

Sky possessed a high-tier passive sensory skill that allowed him to detect ambient magic signatures, but as he had watched Rowenna stand beside Vespera, her mana reserves had felt completely smooth and unreadable too.
Sky gripped his hair through his mask, feeling like he wanted to pull his hair out in frustration.
’Fuck!
She’s a mage, I know she’s a mage!’ Sky screamed internally. ’But what kind of mage is she?!
Fire?!
Ice?!
Spatial?!
Void?!
How the hell does Vespera keep finding these absurd S-Rank casters?!’
"Runes..." a quiet calm voice suddenly spoke from beside him.
Sky blinked, turning his head toward the training grounds.
Hiro was standing by his wooden training post, smoothly sheathing his steel sword into his scabbard with a soft sound.
CLICK!
The warrior walked over to Sky, pointing a long, callous finger toward the leather chair where Rowenna had been earlier.

chapters.title: Chapter 293: Why Is Everybody A Goddamn Virgin?!
paragraphs: Sky turned his eyes toward the grass... and his jaw subtly dropped beneath his mask.
Imprinted faintly upon the damp soil beneath where Rowenna’s boots had rested was a tiny microscopic glowing geometric pattern... a delicate violet-tinted Rune.

The rune was so microscopic that it was virtually invisible to the naked eye, and it emitted a magical signature so faint, so refined, and so absurdly compressed that Sky’s standard sensory abilities hadn’t even registered its presence while she was standing there.

"She’s a Rune Weaver... or a high-tier Arcanist," Hiro analyzed calmly with his senses inspecting the microscopic geometric pattern. "Same difference... The fact that she can passively anchor a rune into the soil through her boots without chanting or drawing a circle shows an absurd level of fine mana control. She is easily a High-Rank spellcaster."
Sky stared at the tiny glowing rune in the grass, his heart hammering against his ribs in utter horror.
FWOOSH!

Without a second of hesitation, Sky raised his gloved hand, unleashing a sudden violent burst of condensed Light Magic that completely incinerated the grass and eviscerated the tiny runic imprint into harmless ash.
Sky stood over the scorched dirt, his chest heaving as terror washed over him.
"Fuck... Fuck!" Sky cursed out loud, wiping cold sweat from his forehead beneath his mask. "I almost let this slip completely past me..."
...Though, as the initial panic faded, Sky took a deep shaky breath, forcing his mind to regain control.
At the very least, he now knew the truth.
Vespera’s newest companion was a high-tier Runic Arcanist.
And knowing your enemy’s discipline was half the battle in territory warfare.
In high-tier combat, the most effective way to handle a Rune Weaver depended entirely on their setup time.
There was Mana-Disruption Fields as the first method.
Runes relied on static environmental mana channels to anchor their geometric effects.
Deploying high-frequency mana-scrambling wards or raw shockwaves would shatter unanchored runes before they could complete their circuit.
There was also what was called as Blitz Aggro & Line-of-Sight Denial.

Runic Arcanists were devastating when given prep time to construct defensive fields, but exceptionally vulnerable to high-speed, close-range physical pressure that prevented them from tracing geometry.
And there was the last one which he had used...Targeted Dispel & Element Overwrite.
Counter-inscribing raw elemental mana directly over their anchor points would trigger a runic overload, causing the rune to backfire onto the caster.
... If the rune was connected to the Caster’s body though.
As for this one, he had merely used his Light magic to overwhelm it.
Sky stared off toward the dark forest horizon, his eyes narrowing into a sharp focus behind his mask.
"Speaking of which..." Sky muttered, his voice dropping into a grim uneasy tone as he turned toward Hiro. "Where the fuck are my scouts?"
Hiro paused, raising an eyebrow. "Your scouts?"

"I deployed a Hero stealth units to track Vespera’s perimeter earlier," Sky explained with anxiety gnawing at his gut. "One elven Guerilla Ranger and one human stealth scout. They were supposed to monitor those mages training in the Umbral Basin and report back ten minutes ago."
Sky looked out over the quiet dark Ironwood forest with a knot of dread tightening in his stomach.
"Where are they?" Sky whispered into the quiet breeze. "Are they even still alive...?"
Deep within the dark humid forest of the Umbral Basin...

A human woman clad in tight, dark-green stealth scouting clothes... the second scout deployed by Lord Sky was currently clinging to the bark of a massive Ironwood tree for dear life, hugging the trunk so tightly her knuckles were turning white!
Her heart was hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird, her eyes wide with pure terror as she stared down at the forest floor through the thick leaves.
Just fifty meters away... lay the crater.
A massive, twenty-foot wide, smoking crater had been blasted clean into the solid earth.
Sitting in the center of the crushed granite and shattered roots was her superior officer... the elite elven Guerilla Ranger who had been sent alongside her.
...Or rather, what was left of him.
Just seconds ago, the terrifying pirate commander had delivered a single casual down-handled pommel strike to the elven scout’s head!

The absurd physical force of that single strike had physically exploded the ground beneath him, creating a massive crater, completely dispersing his mana barrier, and knocking him instantly unconscious with a brain-shattering concussion.
It was horrifying...
This was a nightmare-inducing horror!
The human female scout trembled uncontrollably against the tree trunk, tears of panic welling in the corners of her eyes.
There was nowhere to run...
The mages were surrounding the entire perimeter, their staffs glowing with fire, ice, lightning, and wind, completely locking down every single physical escape route through the canopy.
Realizing that stealth was completely useless and that she was going to be hunted down next, the human scout’s survival instincts snapped.

’If I stay in this tree, they’re going to freeze me solid or burn me alive!’ the female scout panicked with her teeth chattering wildly. ’I have to fight my way out! I’ll feign a high-tier leaping attack at the commander, force her to parry, and use the recoil to vault backward through the upper canopy!’
SWISH!
The human woman drew her twin stealth daggers, channeling every single drop of her nature mana into her legs!
"DIE, YOU PIRATE WITCH!" the woman screamed at the top of her lungs, leaping out from the foliage with explosive force.
She turned into a high-speed green blur, diving straight down toward Morwenna with her twin daggers extended, closing the fifty-meter distance in less than a fraction of a second.
"Pirate witch huh, what’s a new one? Couldn’t you think of something better?"
Even Dread Queen was what one of her enemies had called her before she killed him and she liked it but she needed a better nick-name now.
’Ugh... Should I ask Captain?’
Morwenna was currently standing atop the lip of the smoking crater, her iron side-saber held loosely in her hand.
Her sharp face was twisted into a thoroughly flustered frown.
As the female scout plummeted down toward her head with lethal killing intent—
CLANG!
Morwenna didn’t even look up.
She casually raised her iron side-saber, effortlessly parrying the full-powered two-handed dagger strike as if it were a minor bug bouncing off an iron wall.
The violent shockwave tore through the air.
BOOM!
The force shattered the female scout’s daggers into a dozen flying metal shards.
The human scout gasped in utter terror mid-air.
The overwhelming physical pressure radiating from Morwenna felt like an entire ocean crashing down upon her spine, completely paralyzing her nervous system.
Before the scout could even attempt to trigger her recoil vault—
Morwenna turned her stormy gray eyes upward, staring directly into the terrified woman’s eyes.
Morwenna’s cheeks were flushed bright red with embarrassing frustration. She looked at the falling female scout and asked in an irritated voice.
"Are you a virgin?!"
The human scout’s brain completely short-circuited...
Facing a high ranked commander mid-combat, being asked such an absurd question left her unable to talk.
"Y-YES! YES I AM A VIRGIN!" the female scout screamed in terrified panic!
Morwenna’s face instantly twisted into an expression of soul-crushing rage and disappointment.
"ANOTHER ONE?!" Morwenna roared in utter despair.
FLASH!
Morwenna executed a single hyper-velocity horizontal slash with her side-saber.
VWOOSH... SLICE!
A blinding crescent of compressed blue magic sheared cleanly through the air, bisecting the human stealth scout completely in half mid-air before her boots could even touch the dirt.
THUD! THUD!
The two halves of the scout crashed into the damp moss, blood pooling into the soil as her soul dispersed into harmless ambient light.
Morwenna stood atop the lip of the smoking crater with her iron side-saber resting at her side, her face flushed red as she threw her head back and screamed at the top of her lungs to the heavens.
"WHY THE FUCK IS EVERY SINGLE PERSON IN THIS FOREST A VIRGIN YEARS AFTER MATURITY?! IS THERE NOT A SINGLE EXPERIENCED ADULT IN THIS ENTIRE REALM WHO CAN GIVE ME A STRAIGHT ANSWER?!"

Around the crater’s perimeter, the mages stood completely frozen in place, their mouths hanging wide open, their staffs trembling in their hands as they stared at their flustered screaming Dread Queen in the same horror.
They were virgins too. Were they going to die?
The wind stopped blowing and the forest fell dead silent.
Morwenna stood there in the quiet clearing, her cheeks burning red, panting as the echoing silence of the Umbral Basin answered her frantic scream.
’Fuck...’
The sun shone bright over the rugged border ridges of the Umbral Basin, casting long golden shadows across the dirt trail.
CLIP-CLOP... CLIP-CLOP.
The rhythmic thud of wolf paws echoed through the quiet valley as two massive, armored Blessed Wolves trotted side by side.

Riding atop the lead mount, Valkyrie, was Silas in his single-armed Vespera disguise wearing the charcoal-black, double-breasted suit beneath his dark traveler’s coat, with Thora’s custom silver-and-gold Sil-Grave Arm Guard glinting brilliantly under the morning light.
Riding beside her on the second Blessed Wolf, Luna, was Rowenna.
The newly evolved S-Rank Grand Runemaster looked breathtaking, her long silky dark hair flowing in violet-tinted waves over her shoulders as she let out a small sigh.
Vespera tilted her head beneath her traveler’s hood, adjusting her reins with her gauntleted right hand as she turned her golden-ringed gaze toward the Grand Runemaster.
"Rowenna," Vespera spoke smoothly. "Did you plant the runes?"

Before they had ridden out to The Unmovable Wall earlier that morning, Vespera had pulled up her status interface and noticed a set of high-tier [Listening Runes] unlocked under Rowenna’s expanded skill tree.

Recognizing an opportunity to gather intelligence on a rival Lord, the two of them had quietly formulated a covert plan... while Sky was distracted by whatever negotiation and the live stream broadcast, Rowenna would secretly anchor hidden listening runes throughout The Unmovable Wall to eavesdrop on Sky’s private communications afterward.
Rowenna turned her head, her deep blue eyes sparkling with a sweet, confident smile as she held Luna’s reins.

"I did, My Lord," Rowenna reported smoothly, her voice sweet yet full of pride. "During the twenty minutes we were inside the material holds and near the main treads, I successfully planted roughly fifty listening runes across his territory’s core infrastructure... excluding the single, obvious rune I deliberately left in the open for them to find."
Vespera’s neck trembled slightly beneath her high collar with an internal sweatdrop forming behind her forehead.
Fifty hidden runes?

She had been standing directly beside Sky the entire time... watching her walk through the fortress holds, talk to people, and interact with a lot of things; however Vespera hadn’t detected a single ripple of ambient mana or a single physical trace of rune placement.
To anchor fifty high-grade runes without triggering Sky’s automated perimeter wards or alerting his sensory power was a terrifying feat of magical stealth.
’Having an S-Rank Grand Runemaster in your territory is a cheat code...’ Vespera reflected in internal thought.

Not only was she able to fully utilize Rowenna’s absurd utility... mapping out enemy strongholds, anchoring hidden surveillance, and gathering real-time intelligence without raising an alarm but if an enemy ever deployed a runic caster of their own, Rowenna would be able to read through their techniques, dismantle their runes, and turn their own magic against them like an open book.
That was an overwhelming victory in Vespera’s book.
Honestly, it didn’t even matter that Lord Sky and his Hero, Hiro, had eventually discovered that single microscopic suppression rune on the grass near her chair. What did Sky want to do about it?

Rowenna possessed such versatility across the entire tab... from spatial suppression to a lot of things that even if Sky knew she was a Runic Arcanist, he wouldn’t have the slightest clue how to counter her actual setup.
Vespera wasn’t worried in the slightest.
"What are the runes picking up right now?" Vespera asked, her interest piqued. "What are they saying?"
Rowenna smiled, raising her slender right hand from the reins.
HUMMM!
A delicate glowing violet rune materialized smoothly above Rowenna’s palm, floating in the air like a tiny, intricate geometric snowflake.
Rowenna lightly tapped her manicured index finger against the edge of the floating matrix, tweaking its frequency channels to synchronize with the distant signal.
Instantly, a crisp clear audio projection erupted from the glowing rune.

"Fuck... Fuck!" Sky’s panicked, stress-filled voice echoed directly into the quiet forest, vibrating with anxiety! "I let this slip completely past me! The one Hero and the stealth scout I sent to monitor those Vanguard mages training in the Basin... they’re completely dark! Their comm-signals vanished! They’re dead! They’re fucking dead, Hiro!"
’As I said... I think he’s drunk.’

chapters.title: Chapter 294: Listening Runes
paragraphs: Hearing the frantic panic in the streaming Lord’s voice, Vespera almost let out a loud chuckle right there in her saddle.

At the end of the day, Vespera and Sky were currently business partners trading construction materials for stream engagement... but that didn’t change the cold fundamental reality that they were still rival Lords set to wage war next week.
Hearing that Morwenna had casually slaughtered his stealth scouts while they were attempting to spy on her field training was thoroughly entertaining.
There was no non-aggression rule between their territories stating that scouts caught lurking on Blessed Land soil couldn’t be executed on the spot. The same was for the other side.
Vespera shook her head with an amused smirk, waving her single gauntleted hand.
"Close the listening feed for now, Rowenna," Vespera instructed smoothly. "We’ll request a full playback review later when we’re back at the Keep."
"For sure, My Lord," Rowenna replied sweetly.
With a soft flick of her fingers, Rowenna closed her palm, and the glowing violet rune instantly dissolved into harmless ambient sparks.
The two Blessed Wolves picked up their pace, vaulting over fallen Ironwood roots and galloping smoothly across the final ridge leading toward the heart of the territory.

Up ahead, the massive towering translucent boundary of Eluned’s Barrier shimmered under the morning sun... a divine high-tier protective dome that completely encapsulated the Blessed Land, obscuring its inner layout from outside optical and satellite surveillance.
Valkyrie and Luna leaped straight through the shimmering barrier wall without slowing down, the divine nature mana washing over their armor like a warm, refreshing breeze.
Passing through the open iron gates of the outer perimeter, the wolves sprinted down the paved stone main road.
It took a couple of minutes to cover the distance from the outer forest boundary to the central district of the territory, where the Keep, the Foundry, the Library, and the Barracks were situated.
The once-barren dirt landscape had transformed into a thriving, bustling fortress territory... lined with lush green grass, blooming mana-fruit trees.
Reaching the central square beside the main courtyard, Vespera brought Valkyrie to a smooth halt and disembarked from her leather saddle with her suit-clad frame stepping onto the stone pavement.
’Ah I forgot... He didn’t tell me to return them.’
Rowenna dismounted gracefully from Luna a second later, smoothing down her arcanist robes.
Vespera reached out her gauntleted right hand, gently patting Valkyrie’s dark, furry head, then turned her eyes toward the Grand Runemaster.
"Thank you for following me today, Rowenna," Vespera expressed warmly. "Your presence made the entire trip infinitely smoother."
Rowenna’s blue eyes sparkled with pure devotion. She stepped closer, placing a hand over her heart as she bowed her head softly.
"I would always follow you anywhere, My Lord," Rowenna replied sweetly, her voice full of affection. "No matter where you go or what challenges arise, I am always by your side."
She paused, looking around the open central square, and asked gently.
"You are planning to construct the new living quarters now, right? Aeli told me about it."
Vespera nodded with a confident smirk touching her lips beneath her traveler’s hood as the two Blessed Wolves trotted off toward the stable pens.
"Yes," Vespera confirmed. "I’m going to start constructing them right away. Would you like to come along and see how the new residential complex will look?"
Rowenna’s eyes lit up with delight. "For sure! I would love to see it, My Lord."
Vespera reached up with her left hand, unclasping the Disguise Ring from her finger.
FLASH!
A subtle blinding ripple of golden light washed over her frame.
The suit-clad female Warlord persona instantly dissolved... shrinking back down into Silas Graves’s true physical form.
’It seems once again the clothes in the other form stay there, this truly is amazing.’
Silas stood on the stone pavement wearing his comfortable dark tunic, leather trousers, and boots with his sharp blue eyes clear and his dark hair shifting in the breeze.
He stretched his shoulders, letting out a long sigh of relief as he rolled his neck.
"Man..." Silas groaned, shaking his head. "Wearing a double-breasted suit and acting like a corporate executive for twenty minutes is way more exhausting than fighting a Tier 3 monster."
Rowenna giggled softly, stepping up beside him with an affectionate, comforting smile.
Silas looked toward the northern district of the territory, pointing a finger toward a wide clearing.
"Come on. I think we’ll start building the new quarters a bit away from the main Barracks."
As they walked side by side down the paved stone pathway, Silas mentally reviewed his territory’s current logistical breakdown.
The Tier 3 Barracks was a solid reinforced military structure that had served them well.
It was currently housing all the women an the Barracks could easily handle over seventy women living together under its roof, but Silas wasn’t content with just providing basic military cots.
Silas was planning long-term.

Not only did he want these women to have high-tier, private living spaces, but he also wanted to prepare luxurious high-capacity housing for the new recruits that would inevitably flood into the Blessed Land after they won the upcoming territory war against Lord Sky.

"Once the new residential complex is built," Silas said. "the old Barracks can be permanently converted into an intensive physical training hub and advanced armory. It already has a massive high-pressure hot-spring bathhouse attached to it. It’ll be the perfect staging facility to house brand-new recruits for initial drill conditioning before they earn the right to move into the private quarters."
Rowenna listened intently to his explanation, nodding her head vigorously in agreement.

"That is a brilliant logistical strategy, My Lord. Structuring a clear progression between basic conditioning and private luxury will motivate new recruits to push their physical limits during training."
Now she would no longer have to bear Brida’s smell!
"Exactly," Silas smirked.
They arrived at the designated building site... a massive grassy clearing located a safe distance away from the noisy heat-spewing Warlord Foundry, but pleasantly close to the Library.
Looking over toward the Library, Silas could see several women through the wide glass windows sitting quietly at wooden study tables, reading through magical scrolls and strategy books.

The entire Library structure had been built with thick, soundproof runic insulation, meaning the peaceful quiet inside would never be disrupted by the people living in the adjacent residential buildings, nor would daily residential noise disturb the scholars inside.
Silas pulled up his sovereign system interface, opening the [Territory Construction & Blueprints] tab.
’Show me full details.
[BLUEPRINT UNLOCKED: Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters]
+ STRUCTURE TYPE: Residential Complex
+ CAPACITY: 40 Private Suites per Building
+ MATERIAL REQUIREMENTS (PER BUILDING):
- Obsidian-Slate Stone: 300 / 300 Units [AVAILABLE]
- Ironwood Beams: 600 / 600 Units [AVAILABLE]
Silas inspected the blueprint specifications, tapping his chin thoughtfully.

’Since each of these Tier 2 Living Quarters houses forty private luxury suites...’ Silas calculated, ’...if I erect four of them, that will give us a total capacity of 160 private rooms. That’s more than enough space for our current roster and the upcoming post-war recruit expansion.’
He checked his resource reserves.

Thanks to Sky’s generous bonus transfer, Silas currently had a staggering 4,000 units of Obsidian-Slate Stone sitting safely in his Lord Inventory... far more than the 1,200 total units needed to erect four living quarters.
...However, his eyes caught the second material requirement... Ironwood Beams.
While he had plenty of it right now, he was currently short on processed Ironwood timber to make more than one.

’Well, that’s not a major issue,’ Silas thought casually. ’I can always tell Eluned to fell a few dozen Ironwood trees for me, or assign Valeria and the team to run a timber harvesting drill in the forest.’

Though, considering the strength of ancient Ironwood trees which were notoriously as tough as solid iron... having Eluned use her SSS-Rank Nature Magic to cleanly slice and process the timber was by far the faster, more efficient choice.
Silas looked out toward the lush forest surrounding the Keep.
Ever since the territory expanded, most of the surrounding trees had begun producing massive glowing mana-fruits like magical apples and golden plums.
However, there were still vast swathes of un-enchanted Ironwood trees deeper in the Basin that could easily be harvested for high-grade construction timber.
A sudden, intriguing thought flickered through Silas’s mind.

’Wait a second...’ Silas paused, his blue eyes narrowing as he analyzed the territory’s mechanics. ’Considering that the Territory automatically regenerates damaged territory structures and natural land features easily... do harvested trees grow back automatically too?’

If natural resources like Ironwood timber regenerated within the territory boundary after being harvested, that would mean the Blessed Land possessed a literally endless infinite supply of high-grade construction timber...
They could build entire cities without ever depleting their forestry reserves.
Silas turned his head, looking down at Rowenna as they stood on the grassy plot. Well if they were made out of meat.

"What do you think of this specific position for the residential complex, Rowenna?" Silas asked, gesturing toward the open land with his hand. "It has easy access to the Library, sits away from the Foundry’s heat, and has a direct path to the mess hall."
Rowenna looked around the clearing, taking in the pleasant breeze and the peaceful view of the distant mountains, her blue eyes shining with genuine admiration.

"It is an absolutely wonderful location, My Lord," Rowenna praised softly, her voice filled with delight. "It feels peaceful, dignified, and extremely convenient. I truly cannot wait to see how the complex looks once you finish constructing it!"
Silas let out a quiet, satisfied sigh, closing the construction tab for a brief second.
The Tier 2 Living Quarters blueprints sounded exceptionally comfortable on their own... featuring private baths, insulated stone walls, broad glass windows, and spacious bedroom layouts.

’I won’t bother using Upgrade Points to upgrade the residential buildings just yet,’ Silas reasoned internally. ’The base Tier 2 design is already luxurious enough for human living. I need to strictly save my UP reserves to upgrade critical defensive assets like the Watch Tower, boost Fenna’s combat stats, and then upgrade the rest of the Vanguard girls before the war.’
It was going to be an extraordinarily busy intense week leading up to the official Lord War, for sure.
But Silas was completely confident in his strategy.
He had the resources, he had the talent, and he had the foresight to lock everything down before the broadcast cameras rolled again.

’And speaking of preparations...’ Silas reflected with a dry smirk, ’...I’m going to have to make an official announcement to all the girls soon regarding my Vespera disguise. It would be a complete, embarrassing waste to go through the trouble of acquiring a high-tier disguise ring if my own troops accidentally call me "Lord Graves" in front of Sky’s streaming drones during the war.’
FWOOSH!
Suddenly, out of nowhere... a fiery energetic streak of silver and copper blurred across the ground.
Before Silas could even finish his thought, a solid, heavy weight leaped straight out of the air, crashing directly onto his chest and throwing her arms tightly around his neck.
"MY LORD!" a boisterous cheerful voice yelled out.
Silas stumbled back half a step, catching the sudden flying attacker in his arms.
He looked down to see Thora... the territory’s Master Smith grinning up at him with mischievous delight.
’Isn’t she mad I spanked her or something?’
She wore her leather blacksmith’s apron over her sports top and shorts with her hair tied back and her cheeks lightly smudged with soot from the Foundry.
Before Silas could even say a word—
SMACK!
Thora leaned up on her tiptoes and planted a loud and enthusiastic kiss directly onto Silas’s right cheek.
"Heh..." Silas laughed smoothly, steadying her on her feet as Rowenna chuckled softly beside them. "What’s going on, Thora?"
Thora let go of his neck, wiping her soot-stained cheek with the back of her leather glove, her eyes sparkling with intense curiosity.
"I saw you ride back into the territory with Rowenna!" Thora greeted excitedly, pointing a finger toward his hand. "Give me the Disguise Ring! Let me see it for a second!"

chapters.title: Chapter 295: Lord Sky’s Secret?
paragraphs: Silas blinked, raising an eyebrow.
’Does she already have an upgrade forged for the ring?’

Thinking that her dwarven blacksmithing genius had discovered a way to enhance the ring’s disguise parameters or boost its mana efficiency, Silas reached into his tunic pocket, pulled out the sleek Disguise Ring, and handed it over to her.
Thora caught the ring, bringing it right up to her face.
She squinted her eyes, turning the metallic band over in her fingers, inspecting the intricate internal rune channels etched along the inner curve.
"Hmm..." Thora hummed thoughtfully, rubbing her chin with a serious expression. "Hmm... yep. Just as I thought."
After three long seconds of intense inspection, Thora casually tossed the Disguise Ring right back into Silas’s waiting palm.
Silas caught the ring, looking at her in total, deadpan confusion.
"So...?" Silas asked, tilting his head. "You don’t have an upgrade for the ring or something?"
Thora shook her head, offering a cheerful, completely unbothered grin.
"Nope! What were you expecting, My Lord? The ring’s disguise is already perfectly forged! I can’t upgrade something that’s already at max efficiency!"
Silas’s lips twitched slightly. "Then why did you jump on me and ask to inspect it?"
Thora’s expression shifted, taking on a surprisingly sharp glint as she leaned in closer to him.

"Because inspecting the ring confirmed a theory I had," Thora explained, her voice dropping slightly so it wouldn’t carry across the clearing. "I discovered something extremely specific about that ring’s origin craft... and I need to lay it on you."
Silas straightened his posture, his blue eyes sharpening instantly.
"Alright. Lay it on me."
Thora crossed her arms over her leather apron, looking Silas directly in the eyes.
"Remember when we were looking for materials and saw my sister, Brenna, working as a smtihy inside Lord Sky’s territory?" Thora asked seriously.
Silas nodded firmly.
"Yeah. I remember. What does Brenna have to do with this disguise ring?"
Thora tapped the silver ring sitting in Silas’s hand with her voice dead serious.

"Well I remembered the specific spatial rune geometry etched inside this disguise ring isn’t a standard template... It is a proprietary royal dwarven forgery technique created exclusively by our Father back in the Underground Mountain Realm like I said before but this ring is part of a paired set!"
Silas raised an eyebrow. "A paired set?"
"Yes!" Thora nodded vigorously. "Father only ever forged two items like this, I completely forgot! The first item is this silver ring you’re holding right now..."
Thora paused, pointing her finger toward the distant border horizon where The Unmovable Wall was stationed.
"...And the second item is the exact full-face streaming helmet that Lord Sky wears over his head!"
Silas stood completely still on the grassy field.
His brain halted entirely as he stared at Thora with a completely blank deadpan expression.
Thora leaned in closer, whispering with certainty.

"Father forged those two artifacts specifically to allow high-ranking individuals to completely invert their physical gender, voice, and facial features under a flawless disguise! Meaning... I heavily suspect that ’Lord Sky’ is using that helmet to operate under a male disguise..."
Thora looked Silas dead in the eyes and concluded:
"...Which means Lord Sky is actually a WOMAN!"
Silas stared at her blankly with his right eye violently twitching beneath his brow.
So, in short...
What Thora was saying... was that the hyperactive, Hawaiian-shirt-wearing, iced-juice-drinkingstream-obsessed Lord Sky...
...MIGHT ACTUALLY BE A FEMALE LORD OPERATING UNDER A MALE DISGUISE THIS ENTIRE TIME?!
Silas stood under the morning sun with his jaw set flat.
’Damn...’
He was a lot more surprised than he let on, after all, what kind of woman acted like that.

"Or..." Thora added, rubbing her soot-stained chin with a thoughtful squint-eyed expression, "...it might just be a man disguising himself as another man. Hell, Boss, there are plenty of possibilities so we shouldn’t excuse that too."
POK!
Silas didn’t even hesitate. He reached out his right hand and delivered a sharp energetic finger-flick directly to the middle of Thora’s forehead.
"Ow!" Thora yelped, wincing and clapping a hand over her forehead, though her dense dwarven skull barely registered the physical impact.
"Stop making me panic like that," Silas grumbled, his eyes narrowing into a deadpan glare.
Silas rolled his shoulders, staring out toward the northern horizon where The Unmovable Wall was parked in the distance.
He ran his hand through his short dark hair, letting out a long, heavy breath through his nose.

Regardless of whether Lord Sky was actually a woman operating under a masculine disguise helmet, or just an eccentric guy wearing a tropical Hawaiian shirt and designer sunglasses over a face mask... it didn’t change a single damn thing.
So what if Sky was a woman...?
That didn’t magically wipe the ledger clean.
Sky still owed Silas sixty percent of the massive stream ad revenue generated from today’s broadcast and future broadcast too... Was he supposed to let that go because the fucker was a woman?
FUCK NO!
And more importantly, their territories were still locked into an official Lord War scheduled to erupt next week.
Was Silas supposed to suddenly take it easy on a rival territory ruler just because he suspected there might be a woman under that armor?
HELL NAH!
In the ruthless dog-eat-dog ecosystem of the Sovereign Realm, mercy toward an opponent was just a fast track to getting your own territory annexed and your resources looted.
Business was business, and war was war.
Thora stepped closer, leaning her shoulder against Silas’s waist.
She looked up at him with a wicked suggestive grin spreading across her soot-smudged face, whispering like a literal devil directly into his ear.
"So... don’t you want to fuck her, Boss~?"
Silas’s right eyebrow twitched violently.

"I mean, think about it~" Thora purred, her voice dripping with unhinged, degenerate mischief. "You’ve already done the deed with Eluned! You’ve already taken a Nature Goddess into your bed! So what’s stopping you from adding a streaming Lord to your personal harem, huh~?"
Thora aggressively nudged his hip with her elbow, nodding enthusiastically.

"Though, of course, before you go around conquering rival Lords outside our border, you should definitely breed all of the women in our territory first... That’s just proper logistics, Boss! Keep the bloodline strong at home before expanding the empire~"
Silas raised his palm, placing it flat against Thora’s cheeky face, and forcefully shoved her back a full step.
"I want to win the war, Thora," Silas stated flatly. "Nothing more, nothing less."
Thora stumbled back, letting out a boisterous booming laugh that echoed across the clearing.
She wiped her nose with the back of her leather blacksmith’s apron and gave him a thumbs-up.

"Bah! Don’t you worry about that, Boss! We’re gonna crush those fuckers!" Thora declared arrogantly, slapping her broad chest. "We’ll win the war hands down! Now come on... stop standing around talking about Sky’s pants! I want to watch you build!"
Silas looked down at the dwarven smith with a smirk touching his lips.
"Alright, alright," Silas muttered. "Watch and learn."
Silas turned around, stepping out into the middle of the wide, flat grassy field located between the Territory Library and the Warlord Foundry.
He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, clearing his mind, and mentally commanded his personal system to open.
HUMMM.
A familiar and minimalist digital interface materialized directly in his mind’s eye, projecting a brilliant blue holographic display into his eyes.
Silas navigated past his core attributes, passing his Vitality and Mana meters, and clicked directly into the [Territory Management] sub-menu.
Directly beneath his main territory statistics, a glowing golden icon pulsed with raw energy... the [Build Tab].
The second Silas’s finger touched the holographic prompt—
SHRRRRR!
The ambient atmosphere in the grassy clearing violently shifted and a hum of spatial mana rippled through the air as the Sovereign Realm synchronized with his location.
’I wasn’t able to notice these before...’
A massive glowing light-blue architectural grid expanded across the field.
The translucent grid lines mapped out the physical terrain with mathematical precision, highlighting elevation, soil density, and structural clearance in glowing numbers.
’Or did the interface change because I’m in second stage of Core Advancement.

Silas scrolled through his unlocked blueprint catalog, skipping past basic wooden palisades, automated defense turrets, and resource storage vaults, until he locked onto the specific civic structure he had planned for today.
[BLUEPRINT SELECTED: Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters]
[STRUCTURE TYPE: High-Density Luxury Residential Complex]
[CAPACITY: 40 Private Luxury Suites / En-Suite Bathrooms]
A high-definition three-dimensional holographic wireframe of the building materialized above the blue grid.

It showed a sprawling, three-story architectural marvel... built with heavy, dark obsidian stone walls, thick ironwood support columns, wide glass windows, and a high-gabled slate roof designed to withstand extreme weather.
Silas grabbed the floating holographic wireframe with his mind, dragging it across the grid until it aligned perfectly with the stone pathway leading toward the Library.
[RESOURCE CHECK IN PROGRESS...]
- Obsidian-Slate Stone: 300 / 300 Units [AVAILABLE]
- Ironwood Support Beams: 600 / 600 Units [AVAILABLE]
[CONFIRM CONSTRUCTION OF TIER 2 LIVING QUARTERS?]
Silas looked at the glowing resource confirmation window.
Thanks to the 4,000 units of Obsidian he had just hauled from Sky’s mobile fortress, his stone supply was practically overflowing.
’Construct.’ Silas commanded silently.
BOOM!
The exact second his mental command triggered the prompt, a blinding shockwave of golden sovereign light exploded outward from his chest.
The air in the clearing vibrated so violently that the surrounding grass bent flat against the soil.
THUD! THUD! THUD!
Massive precision-cut blocks of pitch-black Obsidian-Slate Stone materialized out of thin air, crashing down from the sky with deafening, rhythmic impacts that shook the earth beneath their boots.
The dark granite blocks stacked upon one another with automated, mechanical perfection, locking together with heavy interlocking masonry grooves.
CRACK! CRACK!
Thick, polished beams of dense, dark-brown Ironwood slotted seamlessly into the stone foundations, forming a massive earthquake-proof internal skeleton.
HISSSSSSS!

Streams of liquid steel alloy and tempered iron poured from the ether, wrapping around the wooden support joints and window frames like molten armor, cooling instantly with loud pressurized bursts of white steam.

High above, heavy slate tiles rained down onto the high-vaulted roof structure, snapping into place row by row, while thick enchanted glass panes forged themselves into the window frames without a single crack.
The entire construction process took less than ten seconds.
FLASH!
A brilliant blinding wave of pure white light washed over the newly formed structure, signaling the final culmination of the Sovereign Realm’s automated building process.
When the glowing light faded and the steam cleared... a towering magnificent three-story residential complex stood proudly upon the grass.
The building was breathtaking.
The dark polished Obsidian-Slate walls radiated a subtle, luxurious purple sheen under the sunlight.
Ironwood accents framed the double-oak front doors, and wide glass balconies lined the upper two floors.
"By the Ancestors..." Thora breathed out, her small mouth hanging wide open as she looked up at the massive building. "Now that is some serious dwarven-grade masonry!"
Rowenna stepped up beside Silas, her deep blue eyes sparkling with genuine admiration.
"It is magnificent, My Lord. The mana flowing through those granite walls is exceptionally stable."
Silas smiled, rolling his shoulders as he took a step toward the entrance.
"Come on," Silas said, gesturing toward the heavy oak doors. "Let’s go explore inside."
They walked up the short flight of polished stone steps leading to the main entrance.
Silas pushed open the thick oak doors, revealing a grand sunlit foyer lined with smooth, polished hardwood flooring that gleamed like glass.
Just inside the threshold was a long, recessed stone shoe rack.
Silas stopped, looking down at his boots. "Shoes off, everyone. Let’s keep the new floors clean."

sentences.text: Silas blinked, raising an eyebrow.
’Does she already have an upgrade forged for the ring?’

Thinking that her dwarven blacksmithing genius had discovered a way to enhance the ring’s disguise parameters or boost its mana efficiency, Silas reached into his tunic pocket, pulled out the sleek Disguise Ring, and handed it over to her.
Thora caught the ring, bringing it right up to her face.
She squinted her eyes, turning the metallic band over in her fingers, inspecting the intricate internal rune channels etched along the inner curve.
"Hmm..." Thora hummed thoughtfully, rubbing her chin with a serious expression.
"Hmm... yep.
Just as I thought."
After three long seconds of intense inspection, Thora casually tossed the Disguise Ring right back into Silas’s waiting palm.
Silas caught the ring, looking at her in total, deadpan confusion.
"So...?" Silas asked, tilting his head.
"You don’t have an upgrade for the ring or something?"
Thora shook her head, offering a cheerful, completely unbothered grin.
"Nope!
What were you expecting, My Lord?
The ring’s disguise is already perfectly forged!
I can’t upgrade something that’s already at max efficiency!"
Silas’s lips twitched slightly.
"Then why did you jump on me and ask to inspect it?"
Thora’s expression shifted, taking on a surprisingly sharp glint as she leaned in closer to him.
"Because inspecting the ring confirmed a theory I had," Thora explained, her voice dropping slightly so it wouldn’t carry across the clearing.
"I discovered something extremely specific about that ring’s origin craft... and I need to lay it on you."
Silas straightened his posture, his blue eyes sharpening instantly.
"Alright.
Lay it on me."
Thora crossed her arms over her leather apron, looking Silas directly in the eyes.
"Remember when we were looking for materials and saw my sister, Brenna, working as a smtihy inside Lord Sky’s territory?" Thora asked seriously.
Silas nodded firmly.
"Yeah.
I remember.
What does Brenna have to do with this disguise ring?"
Thora tapped the silver ring sitting in Silas’s hand with her voice dead serious.
"Well I remembered the specific spatial rune geometry etched inside this disguise ring isn’t a standard template...
It is a proprietary royal dwarven forgery technique created exclusively by our Father back in the Underground Mountain Realm like I said before but this ring is part of a paired set!"
Silas raised an eyebrow.
"A paired set?"
"Yes!" Thora nodded vigorously.
"Father only ever forged two items like this, I completely forgot!
The first item is this silver ring you’re holding right now..."
Thora paused, pointing her finger toward the distant border horizon where The Unmovable Wall was stationed.
"...And the second item is the exact full-face streaming helmet that Lord Sky wears over his head!"
Silas stood completely still on the grassy field.
His brain halted entirely as he stared at Thora with a completely blank deadpan expression.
Thora leaned in closer, whispering with certainty.
"Father forged those two artifacts specifically to allow high-ranking individuals to completely invert their physical gender, voice, and facial features under a flawless disguise!
Meaning...
I heavily suspect that ’Lord Sky’ is using that helmet to operate under a male disguise..."
Thora looked Silas dead in the eyes and concluded:
"...Which means Lord Sky is actually a WOMAN!"
Silas stared at her blankly with his right eye violently twitching beneath his brow.
So, in short...
What Thora was saying... was that the hyperactive, Hawaiian-shirt-wearing, iced-juice-drinkingstream-obsessed Lord Sky...
...MIGHT ACTUALLY BE A FEMALE LORD OPERATING UNDER A MALE DISGUISE THIS ENTIRE TIME?!
Silas stood under the morning sun with his jaw set flat.
’Damn...’
He was a lot more surprised than he let on, after all, what kind of woman acted like that.
"Or..." Thora added, rubbing her soot-stained chin with a thoughtful squint-eyed expression, "...it might just be a man disguising himself as another man.
Hell, Boss, there are plenty of possibilities so we shouldn’t excuse that too."
POK!
Silas didn’t even hesitate.
He reached out his right hand and delivered a sharp energetic finger-flick directly to the middle of Thora’s forehead.
"Ow!" Thora yelped, wincing and clapping a hand over her forehead, though her dense dwarven skull barely registered the physical impact.
"Stop making me panic like that," Silas grumbled, his eyes narrowing into a deadpan glare.
Silas rolled his shoulders, staring out toward the northern horizon where The Unmovable Wall was parked in the distance.
He ran his hand through his short dark hair, letting out a long, heavy breath through his nose.

Regardless of whether Lord Sky was actually a woman operating under a masculine disguise helmet, or just an eccentric guy wearing a tropical Hawaiian shirt and designer sunglasses over a face mask... it didn’t change a single damn thing.
So what if Sky was a woman...?
That didn’t magically wipe the ledger clean.
Sky still owed Silas sixty percent of the massive stream ad revenue generated from today’s broadcast and future broadcast too...
Was he supposed to let that go because the fucker was a woman?
FUCK NO!
And more importantly, their territories were still locked into an official Lord War scheduled to erupt next week.
Was Silas supposed to suddenly take it easy on a rival territory ruler just because he suspected there might be a woman under that armor?
HELL NAH!
In the ruthless dog-eat-dog ecosystem of the Sovereign Realm, mercy toward an opponent was just a fast track to getting your own territory annexed and your resources looted.
Business was business, and war was war.
Thora stepped closer, leaning her shoulder against Silas’s waist.
She looked up at him with a wicked suggestive grin spreading across her soot-smudged face, whispering like a literal devil directly into his ear.
"So... don’t you want to fuck her, Boss~?"
Silas’s right eyebrow twitched violently.
"I mean, think about it~" Thora purred, her voice dripping with unhinged, degenerate mischief.
"You’ve already done the deed with Eluned!
You’ve already taken a Nature Goddess into your bed!
So what’s stopping you from adding a streaming Lord to your personal harem, huh~?"
Thora aggressively nudged his hip with her elbow, nodding enthusiastically.
"Though, of course, before you go around conquering rival Lords outside our border, you should definitely breed all of the women in our territory first...
That’s just proper logistics, Boss!
Keep the bloodline strong at home before expanding the empire~"
Silas raised his palm, placing it flat against Thora’s cheeky face, and forcefully shoved her back a full step.
"I want to win the war, Thora," Silas stated flatly.
"Nothing more, nothing less."
Thora stumbled back, letting out a boisterous booming laugh that echoed across the clearing.
She wiped her nose with the back of her leather blacksmith’s apron and gave him a thumbs-up.
"Bah!
Don’t you worry about that, Boss!
We’re gonna crush those fuckers!" Thora declared arrogantly, slapping her broad chest.
"We’ll win the war hands down!
Now come on... stop standing around talking about Sky’s pants!
I want to watch you build!"
Silas looked down at the dwarven smith with a smirk touching his lips.
"Alright, alright," Silas muttered.
"Watch and learn."
Silas turned around, stepping out into the middle of the wide, flat grassy field located between the Territory Library and the Warlord Foundry.
He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, clearing his mind, and mentally commanded his personal system to open.
HUMMM.
A familiar and minimalist digital interface materialized directly in his mind’s eye, projecting a brilliant blue holographic display into his eyes.
Silas navigated past his core attributes, passing his Vitality and Mana meters, and clicked directly into the [Territory Management] sub-menu.
Directly beneath his main territory statistics, a glowing golden icon pulsed with raw energy... the [Build Tab].
The second Silas’s finger touched the holographic prompt—
SHRRRRR!
The ambient atmosphere in the grassy clearing violently shifted and a hum of spatial mana rippled through the air as the Sovereign Realm synchronized with his location.
’I wasn’t able to notice these before...’
A massive glowing light-blue architectural grid expanded across the field.
The translucent grid lines mapped out the physical terrain with mathematical precision, highlighting elevation, soil density, and structural clearance in glowing numbers.
’Or did the interface change because I’m in second stage of Core Advancement.

Silas scrolled through his unlocked blueprint catalog, skipping past basic wooden palisades, automated defense turrets, and resource storage vaults, until he locked onto the specific civic structure he had planned for today.
[BLUEPRINT SELECTED: Tier 2 Multi-Floor Living Quarters]
[STRUCTURE TYPE: High-Density Luxury Residential Complex]
[CAPACITY: 40 Private Luxury Suites / En-Suite Bathrooms]
A high-definition three-dimensional holographic wireframe of the building materialized above the blue grid.

It showed a sprawling, three-story architectural marvel... built with heavy, dark obsidian stone walls, thick ironwood support columns, wide glass windows, and a high-gabled slate roof designed to withstand extreme weather.
Silas grabbed the floating holographic wireframe with his mind, dragging it across the grid until it aligned perfectly with the stone pathway leading toward the Library.
[RESOURCE CHECK IN PROGRESS...]
- Obsidian-Slate Stone: 300 / 300 Units [AVAILABLE]
- Ironwood Support Beams: 600 / 600 Units [AVAILABLE]
[CONFIRM CONSTRUCTION OF TIER 2 LIVING QUARTERS?]
Silas looked at the glowing resource confirmation window.
Thanks to the 4,000 units of Obsidian he had just hauled from Sky’s mobile fortress, his stone supply was practically overflowing.
’Construct.’ Silas commanded silently.
BOOM!
The exact second his mental command triggered the prompt, a blinding shockwave of golden sovereign light exploded outward from his chest.
The air in the clearing vibrated so violently that the surrounding grass bent flat against the soil.
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
Massive precision-cut blocks of pitch-black Obsidian-Slate Stone materialized out of thin air, crashing down from the sky with deafening, rhythmic impacts that shook the earth beneath their boots.
The dark granite blocks stacked upon one another with automated, mechanical perfection, locking together with heavy interlocking masonry grooves.
CRACK!
CRACK!
Thick, polished beams of dense, dark-brown Ironwood slotted seamlessly into the stone foundations, forming a massive earthquake-proof internal skeleton.
HISSSSSSS!

Streams of liquid steel alloy and tempered iron poured from the ether, wrapping around the wooden support joints and window frames like molten armor, cooling instantly with loud pressurized bursts of white steam.

High above, heavy slate tiles rained down onto the high-vaulted roof structure, snapping into place row by row, while thick enchanted glass panes forged themselves into the window frames without a single crack.
The entire construction process took less than ten seconds.
FLASH!
A brilliant blinding wave of pure white light washed over the newly formed structure, signaling the final culmination of the Sovereign Realm’s automated building process.
When the glowing light faded and the steam cleared... a towering magnificent three-story residential complex stood proudly upon the grass.
The building was breathtaking.
The dark polished Obsidian-Slate walls radiated a subtle, luxurious purple sheen under the sunlight.
Ironwood accents framed the double-oak front doors, and wide glass balconies lined the upper two floors.
"By the Ancestors..." Thora breathed out, her small mouth hanging wide open as she looked up at the massive building.
"Now that is some serious dwarven-grade masonry!"
Rowenna stepped up beside Silas, her deep blue eyes sparkling with genuine admiration.
"It is magnificent, My Lord.
The mana flowing through those granite walls is exceptionally stable."
Silas smiled, rolling his shoulders as he took a step toward the entrance.
"Come on," Silas said, gesturing toward the heavy oak doors.
"Let’s go explore inside."
They walked up the short flight of polished stone steps leading to the main entrance.
Silas pushed open the thick oak doors, revealing a grand sunlit foyer lined with smooth, polished hardwood flooring that gleamed like glass.
Just inside the threshold was a long, recessed stone shoe rack.
Silas stopped, looking down at his boots.
"Shoes off, everyone.
Let’s keep the new floors clean."
"Right on it, Boss!" Thora agreed cheerfully.
Silas, Thora, and Rowenna unlaced their footwear, placing their leather boots neatly into the wooden cubbies near the entrance before stepping onto the cool, smooth hardwood floor in their socks.

chapters.title: Chapter 296: Talira’s Request
paragraphs: Walking through the ground-floor hallway, Silas was genuinely impressed by the interior craftsmanship.
The corridor was wide, high-ceilinged, and illuminated by soft, enchanted lighting crystals embedded along the crown molding... eliminating the need for smoky oil torches.
Silas opened the first door on the left, stepping into a Private Suite.
"Woah..." Thora muttered, stepping past him into the room.
The suite was remarkably spacious. It featured a plush, king-sized bed with a thick down mattress, clean linen sheets, and heavy woolen blankets.

Against the far wall sat a polished ironwood writing desk paired with a cushioned leather chair, a tall double-door wardrobe for clothing storage, and a wide glass window overlooking the green forest.

"This is incredible, My Lord," Rowenna praised softly, running a delicate hand over the smooth wooden desk. "The insulation spell built into the walls completely blocks out external wind and noise. Anyone resting in this room will enjoy total privacy."
"Let’s check the bathroom," Silas said, walking toward a secondary door on the right side of the suite.
He turned the brass handle and pushed the door open, revealing a private, fully tiled En-Suite Bathroom.
The bathroom was pristine.
Pale white stone tiles covered the floor and walls, giving the space a clean, modern aesthetic.
On the left sat a deep clawfoot porcelain-lined soaking tub with brass fixtures, while on the right was a glass-walled rainfall shower stall.
A polished mirror hung above a double-basin stone sink, complete with enchanted runic faucets.
Thora’s eyes went completely wide.
"Is that... a personal bath in every single room?!"
"Yep," Silas smirked, stepping over to the shower stall. He reached in and turned the brass handle.
PFT-SHHH!
Instantly, a smooth heavy stream of perfectly heated, purified water cascaded down from the rainfall showerhead, venting a light cloud of warm steam into the air.
The runic water pumps built into the building’s foundation operated flawlessly, drawing from the reservoir without a single hitch.
’Or at least that’s what I’m guessing... the Barracks and every other building that has water were connected to the major one in the center of the territory.
"Hahaha! The pressure is amazing!" Thora cheered out loud...
Before Silas or Rowenna could even process what she was doing—
THUD!

Thora kicked off her leather apron, unbuttoned her shorts, and literally vaulted herself straight over the porcelain rim of the deep clawfoot soaking tub, landing inside the empty tub with a loud clatter!
"Thora!" Silas sweatdropped hard, clapping a hand over his face. "What the hell are you doing?!"
"Testing the equipment, Boss!" Thora yelled back from inside the tub, her muscled legs kicking up over the edge.
She reached over and yanked the tub faucet handle to full blast!
FWOOSH!
Steaming hot water began pouring rapidly into the tub, filling the basin in seconds.
Thora leaned her head back against the porcelain rim, letting out a loud contented groan of bliss as the hot water submerged her shoulders.

"Ahhhhh~ This is divine!" Thora giggled, splashing water over her arms. "The enchantment in the pipes heats the water instantly! The craftsmanship on these brass valves is top-tier! Boss, I’m never leaving this tub!"
Rowenna covered her mouth with her hand, letting out a soft melodic chuckle at the dwarf’s antics.
Silas shook his head in deadpan exasperation, turning back toward the door.
"Get out of the tub and put your apron back on, you crazy dwarf. We’re finishing the tour."
"Fine, fine!" Thora grumbled playfully, turning off the faucet and grabbing a thick white towel from the warming rack.
After Thora dried off and put her apron back on, the three of them spent another fifteen minutes exploring the upper two floors.
Every single one of the forty private suites was identically equipped with plush bedding, insulated walls, spacious wardrobes, and private heated bathrooms.
It was a massive dramatic step up from standard military barracks living.
Exiting through the double oak front doors, Silas sat down on the top stone step, pulling his leather boots back on and tying his laces.
Rowenna and Thora sat beside him, slipping their shoes on as well.
Silas looked back up at the magnificent three-story building, letting out a satisfied breath.

"This turned out even better than I expected," Silas remarked, pulling his laces tight. "I plan to build three more of these residential complexes over the next few hours to hit our target of one hundred and sixty private suites... but for now, I need to go find Elu."
Rowenna and Thora stood up beside him, nodding in agreement.
"That is a wise decision, My Lord," Rowenna agreed warmly. "Lady Eluned has been waiting in the Keep since morning."
Thora, however, puffed out her chest, crossing her arms over her apron with an intensely smug grin.

"Hey, Boss~" Thora pitched slyly, winking at him. "Since I’m the Master Smith of the entire territory and the one who tests all your plumbing... I think I deserve two whole private suites in this new building, don’t you think~? One for sleeping, and one to store my extra anvil collection~"
Silas stood up, looked at her smug face, and immediately raised his hand...
CHOP!
He delivered a swift affectionate karate chop directly onto the top of her head!
"Ow!" Thora yelped again, rubbing her head with a toothy grin.
"You get one suite just like everyone else, Thora," Silas replied with a dry smirk. "If you want extra inventory space, build a secondary shed in your Foundry."
"Bah! You’re a stingy landlord, Boss!" Thora laughed loudly.
Thora then turned her head, grabbing Rowenna by the sleeve of her arcanist robes and tugging her forcefully down the stone path toward the Foundry.

"Come on, Rowenna!" Thora cheered excitedly, dragging the Grand Runemaster along. "You promised to help me! I’ve got a whole crate of newly forged broadswords and heavy shields down at the shop, and I need you to etch hidden offensive explosion runes onto the crossguards... When Sky’s troops try to parry our blades during the war next week, those fuckers are gonna get a face full of runic fire! Hahaha~"
Rowenna stumbled along beside her, letting out a sweet, helpless laugh as she was dragged away.
"Alright, Thora, alright! Lead the way!"
Silas stood in the grassy clearing, watching the two women walk off toward the Foundry together.
As he watched Thora’s energetic, muscular frame lead Rowenna down the path, a quiet, contemplative expression settled across Silas’s face.
’Thora really is the literal backbone of our territory’s industrial power,’ Silas thought deeply.
Without her tireless work at the forges, his troops wouldn’t have refined steel armor and his territory wouldn’t possess special gadgets.
She worked day and night with unyielding enthusiasm, never once complaining about fatigue.
’Seriously... she hasn’t complained seriously, she always jokes around with it.’
’I really have to use my System UP to upgrade Thora soon...’ Silas resolved internally. ’She deserves a major stat boost, higher-tier forging skills, and better hammer techniques.’
And more importantly... Silas knew that running a massive expanding territory’s industrial sector was too much work for a single dwarf.
Thora desperately needed a dedicated team of dwarven assistants and apprentice smiths to help her manage the bellows, pour the molten steel, and fold the alloy billets.
Silas turned his eyes toward the northern horizon, a sharp, confident smirk touching his lips.
’I’ll capture a whole squad of skilled dwarven craftsmen from Sky’s territory after we win the war,’ Silas planned. ’That will give Thora a full crew to command.’
With a long relaxing sigh, Silas turned away from the new residential complex and began walking across the paved stone central square toward the Keep.
The territory was alive with quiet, productive energy.
As he walked past the central courtyard, he saw Gunnhild leading a group of girls through physical stance drills near the armory.
Over by the garden plots, Aeliana was carefully inspecting a row of blooming mana-fruit trees with her white robes fluttering gently in the breeze.
Reaching the massive, reinforced oak-and-iron doors of the Keep, Silas pushed the heavy handles open, stepping inside the quiet interior.
"Elu?" Silas called out, his voice echoing cleanly off the polished stone walls of the main entrance hall. "Eluned?"
There was no immediate answer from the foyer.

Knowing her morning habits, Silas walked down the wide stone corridor, heading straight toward the Keep’s spacious kitchen area where she usually spent her mornings preparing tea or organizing food supplies like she had.
Silas pushed open the swinging wooden kitchen doors and stepped inside—
CLINK!
The soft sound of glass against stone echoed near the central obsidian prep island.
Silas paused, looking over at the counter.
Standing beside the prep island was Talira, the dragon.
Talira looked stunning.
She wore her fitted dark combat tunic, her slender dragon tail swaying nervously behind her legs, while two sleek dark dragon horns emerged gracefully from her hair.
She was currently holding a heavy glass pitcher filled with a vibrant deep-purple mana-fruit juice that Aeliana had freshly squeezed earlier that morning.
A small glass cup sat on the counter beside a large crystal jug where Aeli usually stored the leftover beverages.
Talira was in the middle of pouring herself a drink, but the exact second Silas stepped through the door...
WHOOSH!
Talira startled so violently that her dragon tail shot straight up into the air...
She nearly dropped the glass pitcher with her hands trembling as her pale face turned bright red.
"M-MY LORD!" Talira squeaked out in panicked embarrassment, frantically setting the pitcher down onto the counter.
’She calls me my Lord? And why the hell is she so shy too? It’s kind of cute...’
She raised both of her hands in front of her chest, waving them wildly as she stumbled over her words.
"I-I wasn’t stealing! I promise I wasn’t stealing the juice! I just... I was thirsty from training and I saw Aeliana leave the jug here and I—"
’Training too? Seems like the Loss did a number on her.
Silas couldn’t help but let out a soft warm chuckle, stepping into the kitchen and waving his hand placatingly.
"Relax, Talira," Silas smiled gently. "You don’t have to explain yourself. You’re part of this territory now. Anything in the kitchen is yours to drink whenever you want."
Talira blinked her wide reptilian-slitted eyes, her chest heaving with a sigh of immense relief.
"R-really...?"
"Really," Silas confirmed, walking over to the counter. "Go ahead, pour yourself a full glass."
Talira swallowed nervously, her cheeks still flushed a pretty shade of pink.
She carefully lifted the glass pitcher, filled her cup with the cold purple juice, and took a slow delicate sip.
The refreshing, sweet mana-fruit juice instantly invigorated her, and a soft contented expression touched her features.
Silas leaned against the edge of the prep island, looking down at her.
"By the way, Talira, do you know where Eluned is? I called for her in the foyer, but she wasn’t down here."
Talira wiped a tiny drop of purple juice from her lip, setting her cup down as she looked up at him.

"Lady Eluned is upstairs, My Lord," Talira answered softly, gesturing toward the staircase behind the kitchen wall. "She went up to your private Lord office about twenty minutes ago to review something."
"Ah, got it. Thanks, Talira," Silas nodded warmly.
Silas turned on his heel, taking a step toward the kitchen doors to head upstairs toward his office.
...However, before his boots could even cross the threshold—
TUG!
Silas stopped in his tracks. He felt a soft gentle pressure pulling at the fabric of his dark shirt sleeve.
Silas paused, turning his head back around to look down.
Talira was standing right behind him. She was holding onto the cuff of his sleeve with her delicate claw-tipped fingers and her head bowed low.
Her face was completely flushed bright red... from the tips of her pointed ears all the way down to her neck.
Her slender dragon tail was curling tightly around her leg in agonizing nervousness.
Silas raised an eyebrow with his gentle.
"What’s wrong, Talira?"
Talira fidgeted with her fingers, her heart hammering so loudly against her ribs that Silas could practically hear it.
She squeezed her eyes shut, took a deep, trembling breath, and finally mustered the courage to look up into his blue eyes.
"M-My Lord..." Talira stuttered out nervously, her voice barely above a shy whisper, "...c-could you... train me?"
