Without her tireless work at the forges, his troops wouldn’t have refined steel armor and his territory wouldn’t possess special gadgets.
She worked day and night with unyielding enthusiasm, never once complaining about fatigue.
’Seriously... she hasn’t complained seriously, she always jokes around with it.’
’I really have to use my System UP to upgrade Thora soon...’ Silas resolved internally. ’She deserves a major stat boost, higher-tier forging skills, and better hammer techniques.’
And more importantly...
Silas knew that running a massive expanding territory’s industrial sector was too much work for a single dwarf.
Thora desperately needed a dedicated team of dwarven assistants and apprentice smiths to help her manage the bellows, pour the molten steel, and fold the alloy billets.
Silas turned his eyes toward the northern horizon, a sharp, confident smirk touching his lips.
’I’ll capture a whole squad of skilled dwarven craftsmen from Sky’s territory after we win the war,’ Silas planned. ’That will give Thora a full crew to command.’
With a long relaxing sigh, Silas turned away from the new residential complex and began walking across the paved stone central square toward the Keep.
The territory was alive with quiet, productive energy.
As he walked past the central courtyard, he saw Gunnhild leading a group of girls through physical stance drills near the armory.
Over by the garden plots, Aeliana was carefully inspecting a row of blooming mana-fruit trees with her white robes fluttering gently in the breeze.
Reaching the massive, reinforced oak-and-iron doors of the Keep, Silas pushed the heavy handles open, stepping inside the quiet interior.
"Elu?" Silas called out, his voice echoing cleanly off the polished stone walls of the main entrance hall.
"Eluned?"
There was no immediate answer from the foyer.

Knowing her morning habits, Silas walked down the wide stone corridor, heading straight toward the Keep’s spacious kitchen area where she usually spent her mornings preparing tea or organizing food supplies like she had.
Silas pushed open the swinging wooden kitchen doors and stepped inside—
CLINK!
The soft sound of glass against stone echoed near the central obsidian prep island.
Silas paused, looking over at the counter.
Standing beside the prep island was Talira, the dragon.
Talira looked stunning.
She wore her fitted dark combat tunic, her slender dragon tail swaying nervously behind her legs, while two sleek dark dragon horns emerged gracefully from her hair.
She was currently holding a heavy glass pitcher filled with a vibrant deep-purple mana-fruit juice that Aeliana had freshly squeezed earlier that morning.
A small glass cup sat on the counter beside a large crystal jug where Aeli usually stored the leftover beverages.
Talira was in the middle of pouring herself a drink, but the exact second Silas stepped through the door...
WHOOSH!
Talira startled so violently that her dragon tail shot straight up into the air...
She nearly dropped the glass pitcher with her hands trembling as her pale face turned bright red.
"M-MY LORD!" Talira squeaked out in panicked embarrassment, frantically setting the pitcher down onto the counter.
’She calls me my Lord?
And why the hell is she so shy too?
It’s kind of cute...’
She raised both of her hands in front of her chest, waving them wildly as she stumbled over her words.
"I-I wasn’t stealing!
I promise I wasn’t stealing the juice!
I just...
I was thirsty from training and I saw Aeliana leave the jug here and I—"
’Training too?
Seems like the Loss did a number on her.
Silas couldn’t help but let out a soft warm chuckle, stepping into the kitchen and waving his hand placatingly.
"Relax, Talira," Silas smiled gently.
"You don’t have to explain yourself.
You’re part of this territory now.
Anything in the kitchen is yours to drink whenever you want."
Talira blinked her wide reptilian-slitted eyes, her chest heaving with a sigh of immense relief.
"R-really...?"
"Really," Silas confirmed, walking over to the counter.
"Go ahead, pour yourself a full glass."
Talira swallowed nervously, her cheeks still flushed a pretty shade of pink.
She carefully lifted the glass pitcher, filled her cup with the cold purple juice, and took a slow delicate sip.
The refreshing, sweet mana-fruit juice instantly invigorated her, and a soft contented expression touched her features.
Silas leaned against the edge of the prep island, looking down at her.
"By the way, Talira, do you know where Eluned is?
I called for her in the foyer, but she wasn’t down here."
Talira wiped a tiny drop of purple juice from her lip, setting her cup down as she looked up at him.
"Lady Eluned is upstairs, My Lord," Talira answered softly, gesturing toward the staircase behind the kitchen wall.
"She went up to your private Lord office about twenty minutes ago to review something."
"Ah, got it.
Thanks, Talira," Silas nodded warmly.
Silas turned on his heel, taking a step toward the kitchen doors to head upstairs toward his office.
...However, before his boots could even cross the threshold—
TUG!
Silas stopped in his tracks.
He felt a soft gentle pressure pulling at the fabric of his dark shirt sleeve.
Silas paused, turning his head back around to look down.
Talira was standing right behind him.
She was holding onto the cuff of his sleeve with her delicate claw-tipped fingers and her head bowed low.
Her face was completely flushed bright red... from the tips of her pointed ears all the way down to her neck.
Her slender dragon tail was curling tightly around her leg in agonizing nervousness.
Silas raised an eyebrow with his gentle.
"What’s wrong, Talira?"
Talira fidgeted with her fingers, her heart hammering so loudly against her ribs that Silas could practically hear it.
She squeezed her eyes shut, took a deep, trembling breath, and finally mustered the courage to look up into his blue eyes.
"M-My Lord..." Talira stuttered out nervously, her voice barely above a shy whisper, "...c-could you... train me?"

chapters.title: Chapter 297: Emulate Your Lord’s Seriousness
paragraphs: Silas stood frozen by the kitchen door, staring down at the blushing dragon girl with her cute dragon horns twitching in nervous anticipation.
Looking at her flushed adorable face, Silas’s mind completely stalled and a single thought echoed through his soul.
’Why the hell are all of these girls in my territory so damn cute...?’
Silas stood near the entrance of the Keep’s kitchen, staring down at the dragon girl holding the cuff of his dark shirt sleeve.
’Did some sort of evil spirit get into her...?’
He remembered the last Evil spirit that tried to enter Thora, it was of course handled by Elu but who was to say that it didn’t go after her next though.
’Well meh, not to mention Dragons are extremely powerful everywhere, but still, what’s wrong with her?’
Talira’s face was completely flushed in a deep vivid shade of crimson.
Her dark dragon horns twitched nervously against her hair, and her slender, scaled tail was wrapped so tightly around her thigh it looked like a vice grip.
Looking at her timid blushing posture, Silas couldn’t help but feel a wave of deadpan confusion wash over his mind.
Wasn’t she a dragon?

In every myth, legend, and text he had ever read back in Valoria City, dragons were supposed to be arrogant, condescending and overwhelmingly prideful creatures that looked down on lower races from atop mountains of gold.
When he had first brought her here, even with the spar, he had half-expected an uncontrollable fiery monster that would require an iron fist to keep in line.
Yet looking at her face right now, Silas couldn’t find a single trace of dragon pride in her eyes.
’I guess getting completely outmaneuvered and slammed into the dirt during our duel yesterday broke that stubborn shell pretty fast,’ Silas mused inwardly with a smirk touching his lips.
That explained it...
Winning that duel hadn’t just secured her loyalty... it had completely recalibrated her perspective on power.
In the eyes of a dragon, strength was the only law that mattered, and Silas had demonstrated a level of dominance that left no room for arrogant defiance.
Silas folded his arms across his chest, leaning his shoulder casually against the wooden doorframe as he looked down at her.

"What kind of training are we talking about, Talira?" Silas asked smoothly, his tone calm and curious. "And why do you even need training from me in the first place? You’re a Dragon. You were born with legendary physical stats, dragon-scale defense, and a lot of mana."
Talira swallowed hard, her reptilian-slitted eyes shifting nervously before locking onto his chest.
She tightened her grip on his sleeve with her voice trembling slightly as she confessed her reasoning.

"T-The last time we fought..." Talira began, her cheeks burning even hotter, "...you weren’t even in your true physical form. You used your female body... that single-armed woman disguise to completely dismantle my combat style."
She paused, taking a ragged breath, her dragon tail flicking against her leg.

"And... and it’s obvious to me now that you aren’t nearly as strong or as fast in your female body as you are in your true male form," Talira continued, her voice gaining a desperate earnest edge. "You beat me while holding back your primary physical vessel... If I can’t even overcome your suppressed disguise, how am I supposed to stand proudly beside the other heroes in your territory?"
Silas remained silent, watching her intently as she poured her heart out.
Talira looked up into his eyes, her expression shifting from timid embarrassment to a sharp burning resolve.

"You reminded me that we are about to enter an official Lord War," Talira stated firmly, her small hands clenching into tight fists against her sides. "You told me that I would be deployed on the front lines alongside the Vanguard. I... I want to train with you to get stronger! I need to protect my pride as a dragon, and I want to prove to the entire Sovereign Realm that your territory... The Blessed Land is truly superior to every rival human out there!"
Silence settled over the Keep’s kitchen for a long moment.
Silas looked down at the fiery determination burning in her eyes. Despite her timid, cute reactions, the heart of a true warrior still beat within her chest.
She wasn’t asking for special treatment or luxurious accommodations... she wanted to earn her place on his battlefield through blood and sweat.
A warm genuine smile broke across Silas’s face.
He reached out his broad right hand, placing his palm directly onto her head, right between her sleek dragon horns, and gently patted her hair.
Talira completely lost her breath!
The sudden intimate physical touch caused her entire body to freeze up like a statue.
Her heart hammered against her ribs like a runaway engine with her breath hitching in her throat as a bright explosive blush spread all the way to the tips of her pointed ears.
For three seconds, she stood entirely paralyzed under his palm.
Then, her dragon pride reflexively flared up.
She stubbornly shifted her head backward, pulling out from under his hand while pouting up at him with narrow, teary eyes.

"S-Stop treating me like a pet dog!" Talira huffed out loud with her chest heaving as she tried to regain her composure. "I am a Dragon Warrior! I am not some cute creature you can just pat on the head whenever you feel like it!"
Silas chuckled smoothly, dropping his hand back to his side and winking at her.
"You’re a good girl, Talira," Silas told her, his voice warm yet commanding. "And your mindset is exactly what I need on my front lines."
Talira blinked, her pout melting away into a look of quiet awe as his words registered.

"I need a lot of physical condition refinement before the war starts next week anyway," Silas continued, turning his body toward the kitchen exit. "So consider your request granted. We’ll set up intensive sparring sessions starting tomorrow morning. I’ll call for you at the training grounds when it’s time... Call Aeli too though before we do too much."
Talira let go of his shirt sleeve completely, stepping back and bowing her head deep in a formal stance.
"T-Thank you, My Lord!" Talira voiced out, her tone filled with immense relief and deep gratitude. "I will not let you down!"
Silas paused at the doorway, turning his head back over his shoulder to give her one last reassuring look.
"Don’t worry," Silas said with a confident smirk. "You’re going to do great."
With that, Silas stepped out of the kitchen, leaving the blushing dragon warrior standing by the prep island with a silly happy smile spreading across her face.
"What’s wrong with me?!"
Silas made his way across the foyer of the Keep, his leather boots making quiet taps against the polished stone floor.
He headed straight for the grand staircase, climbing the curving flight of stairs up to the second floor where his private Lord office was located.
Reaching the thick Ironwood doors of his office, Silas grabbed the brass handle and pushed the door open—
CREAK!
The scene inside the office caused Silas to freeze dead in his tracks. Sitting behind his massive oak desk was Eluned.

The SSS-Rank Nature Goddess was dressed in one of Silas’s oversized white cotton shirts... which draped comically over her figure, sliding off one of her delicate shoulders and leaving her smooth skin exposed down to her collarbone.
Her long shimmering emerald hair cascaded over the back of the leather executive chair, floating gently in the ambient mana of the room.
...However, it wasn’t her outfit that caught Silas completely off guard. It was what she was doing.
Eluned had both of her elbows propped up on his oak desk, her chin resting firmly on her clasped hands.
Her face was twisted into an absurdly rigid deadpan frown as she stared blankly at the empty stone wall across the room.
She narrowed her emerald eyes, cleared her throat, and attempted to imitate Silas’s deep voice out loud.

"Hmm... yes. We need more Stone," Eluned grunted, trying to make her voice sound raspy while maintaining a rigid flat expression. "I need more power and more money... But why are nobles always trying to show off their money? If I don’t get three thousand units of building material by tomorrow, I’m going to chop someone’s head off... yeah. That’s how I roll."
She adjusted her posture, puffing out her chest in the oversized shirt, and narrowed her eyes even further at the wall.

"Morwenna, shut up," Eluned continued her impression, deepening her frown to match Silas’s signature deadpan glare. "Thora, stop trying to turn the Keep into an anvil. I am the Lord of this territory, and if anyone complains, I’m using my authority to upgrade their training drills until they cry... yeah. Very logical."
Standing by the open doorway, Silas’s jaw literally dropped to the floor.
He stood there for five full seconds, staring at his SSS-Rank Goddess sitting in his executive chair, wearing his shirt, and performing a deadpan impression of his secret thoughts.
"PFT-HAHAHAHAHA!"
Silas couldn’t hold it in any longer.
A loud, boisterous burst of laughter exploded from his chest, echoing wildly off the office walls.
"Huh?!"
Eluned stiffened so violently that her emerald hair flared out like a startled cat.
She snapped her head toward the doorway with her wide green eyes locking onto Silas standing there doubled over with laughter.
She had been so intensely focused on perfecting her imitation of her beloved hubby that she had completely forgotten to maintain her passive sensing magic.
She hadn’t heard him open the door at all!
"S-SILAS?!" Eluned shrieked out, her divine composure shattering into a million pieces.
A bright, deep shade of crimson flushed across her cheeks, traveling all the way down to her exposed shoulder.
She frantically scrambled out of the heavy leather chair with her hands flying to smooth down the oversized white shirt as she stumbled over her desk!
"H-How long have you been standing there?!" Eluned stammered out, her voice rising a bit in embarrassment! "I-I wasn’t doing anything! I was just... inspecting your office!"
Silas wiped a tear of laughter from the corner of his eye, leaning against the doorframe as his shoulders shook with amusement.
"’Yeah... very logical,’" Silas quoted her with a massive smirk, stepping into the room. "Is that really how I sound to you, Elu?"
Eluned pouted heavily, covering her blushing face with both of her hands as she groaned in embarrassment.
’That’s what you muttered in your sleep dummy...’
"Ahhhh! Stop it! You weren’t supposed to hear that! I was just... I was trying to understand how your brain works when you sit at this big scary desk!"
Silas walked up to her, wrapping his arms around her waist and pulling her soft shirt-clad body flush against his chest.
He leaned down and planted a sweet firm kiss on her blushing cheek, causing her to let out a quiet, contented sigh as she wrapped her arms around his neck.
"You’re ridiculous, Elu," Silas smiled warmly, resting his forehead against hers. "But it was pretty damn cute."
"Hmph," Eluned huffed playfully, her emerald eyes sparkling with affection. "You’re just lucky I love you."
Silas chuckled, smoothing a stray lock of emerald hair behind her ear before transitioning back to territory business.

"Alright, jokes aside," Silas said, his tone turning to the usual. "I just finished constructing the first Tier 2 Living Quarters down near the Library. But I need to harvest a massive supply of Ironwood timber so we can erect three more buildings before the war starts next week. It costs six hundred units of Ironwood Beams per building, so I need at least eighteen hundred units fast."
Eluned’s eyes lit up with immediate understanding.
"You want me to help you fell and process the Ironwood trees in the outer forest?"

"Exactly," Silas nodded. "Your Nature power can harvest the timber cleanly without ruining the wood fiber but before we head out... is there anything specific you want to build in the territory, Elu? I’m expanding our infrastructure anyway, so tell me what you need."
Eluned left his arms, stepping back and tapping her chin thoughtfully as a dreamy wistful expression touched her face.

"Well..." Eluned mused softly, looking out the office window toward the green landscape below, "...back in the ancient Land of Elves, before I was summoned into your realm, every major territory possessed an Open Sanctuary Garden."

chapters.title: Chapter 298: Use ’That’
paragraphs: She turned back to Silas, gesturing with her hands.

"Not just a basic crop farm, but a wide, open-air botanical pavilion filled with ancient mana-blooms, glowing moonlight lilies, soft grass terraces, and stone fountains. A place where the girls can sit, meditate, recover their mana, and relax after heavy combat training. It acts as a natural spatial anchor that purifies the ambient atmosphere of the entire territory."
Silas raised an eyebrow, genuinely intrigued by the concept.
An open-air garden pavilion that provided passive mana recovery and spatial purification for his troops sounded like an exceptional utility structure.
"An Open Sanctuary Garden..." Silas reflected out loud. "Alright. I’ll search through the System blueprint database later tonight and see what botanical designs we can use."
They already had the Verdant place but more places wouldn’t be so bad.
Eluned gave him a sweet, radiant smile, stepping up to kiss his chin.
"Thank you, my Lord."
"Come on," Silas said, taking her hand. "Let’s go chop some trees."
Leaving the Keep behind, Silas and Eluned walked side by side down the stone pathway, heading toward the eastern perimeter of the territory where the dense Ironwood forest bordered the inner valley.

The morning sun was warm, casting a golden glow over the lush landscape. As they walked, their fingers naturally intertwined... Silas’s broad calloused hand gripping Eluned’s soft, delicate fingers in a comfortable affectionate hold.
Walking hand-in-hand through his territory, Silas felt a rare sense of peace settle over his mind.
For a few brief minutes, he wasn’t worrying about Lord Sky’s mobile fortress, the World Council’s eyes, or the upcoming broadcast war.
He was just a man walking through a beautiful forest with the woman that was his wife.
’And her smell... it’s so calmi---’
Silas sighed shaking his head of such thoughts before he started ramming into her again out here.
They reached the tree line, stepping off the paved stone path and onto the soft damp moss of the forest floor.
Up ahead stood a colossal ancient Ironwood tree. Its trunk was as wide as a wagon, its bark dark and dense as solid iron stretching nearly eighty feet into the sky.
Eluned stopped beside the massive trunk, releasing Silas’s hand to gently place her palm against the rough bark.
A subtle pulse of green mana radiated from her skin, flowing into the tree’s internal vascular system.

"This is a remarkably healthy tree," Eluned evaluated softly, her emerald eyes scanning the towering canopy. "It has absorbed mineral nutrients from the soil, but notice how no fruits or flowers are growing from its branches."
Silas looked up at the dense green leaves. "So it’s a pure timber tree which is perfect for beams."
While inspecting the surroundings, Eluned glanced over at an adjacent tree twenty yards away... a lush mana-apple tree heavy with ripe, glowing red apples.
With a subtle flick of her wrist, Eluned channeled a delicate strand of nature power into the soil.
SWISH!

A pair of thin green vines sprouted instantly from the grass beneath the apple tree! The vines coiled gracefully up the trunk, gently plucking three massive perfectly ripe mana-apples from the high branches, and carried them back across the air, floating them down right into Silas’s waiting hands!
Silas caught the glowing red apples, raising an eyebrow with a smirk.
"Snack time?"
"Always," Eluned giggled softly.
Silas took a big, crunchy bite out of one of the apples. The crisp sweet juice exploded across his tongue, bursting with rich, refreshing mana that instantly restored his energy.
He chewed happily, looking over at the dozens of fruit-heavy trees scattered across the forest edge.

"Man..." Silas said with a sigh, taking another bite, "...we really need to assign a dedicated harvesting squad of girls to pluck these apples every morning. Leaving high-grade mana-fruit sitting on branches to rot is a complete waste of territorial resources."
Eluned nodded in complete agreement, taking a delicate bite of her own apple.
"I’ll have Gunnhild organize a daily harvesting rotation starting tomorrow. We can store the excess fruit in cold preservation vaults."
Finishing her apple, Eluned turned her full attention back to the colossal Ironwood tree before them.
Her gentle expression instantly shifted into that of a supreme SSS-Rank Nature Goddess.
HUMMM!
An overwhelming suffocating aura of brilliant green divine mana erupted from Eluned’s body.
The grass beneath her boots began to bloom with tiny white flowers as ambient nature energy answered her call...
Eluned raised both of her hands toward the sky with her emerald hair floating wildly in the air.
"Up," Eluned commanded softly.
RUMBLE! RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
The entire forest floor violently shook as the colossal eighty-foot Ironwood tree... weighing tens of thousands of pounds began to lift straight out of the ground.
Its massive, iron-dense root network slid cleanly out of the soil as if pulled by an invisible giant hand.
As the tree floated gracefully twenty feet in the air, a soft shower of bright green leaves rained down through the canopy.
Eluned reached out her hand, catching three large, perfectly shaped leaves as they drifted down.

With a cute, playful flick of her fingers, she channeled a tiny thread of mana into the leaves, weaving them together into a charming, elegant little green leaf-hat, and placed it neatly atop her head.
She turned toward Silas, tilting her head with a beaming, adorable smile.
"How do I look?"
Silas sweatdropped hard, looking at the goddess wearing a leafy hat while holding a multi-ton tree suspended in mid-air.
"You look amazing, Elu," Silas smirked, pointing toward the floating trunk. "Now... how are we splitting this beast?"
Eluned’s smile turned confident. "Tell me what dimensions you need, My Lord."
"We need clean Ironwood support beams like the ones you did before," Silas instructed clearly. "Cut them into standard twelve-foot structural lengths. We need as many as this trunk can yield."
"Consider it done," Eluned declared.
FLASH!
Lines of razor-sharp concentrated green mana blades materialized around the floating tree.

With mathematical precision, the nature mana sliced through the iron-dense timber... stripping the outer bark, trimming the branches, and slicing the massive trunk into hundreds of pristine, squared Ironwood beams.
THUD! THUD! THUD!
Stack after stack of perfectly processed Ironwood beams rained down onto the grass, forming a massive, neatly organized timber pile that triggered Silas’s system inventory counter.
[RESOURCE HARVESTED: Ironwood Beams +800 Units]
Silas looked at the massive timber pile, a deep satisfied breath escaping his chest.
Watching Eluned effortlessly process an entire forest giant in seconds, Silas folded his arms, his blue eyes narrowing as his mind shifted toward the bigger picture.
’Eight hundred units from a single tree...’ Silas calculated internally. ’With two more trees, we’ll have more than enough timber to finish erecting all living quarters today.’
He looked out toward the northern horizon with his jaw setting into a firm unyielding line.

’Huu...’ Silas sighed silently in his thoughts. ’We really need to prepare properly for this war. Sky might act like a casual streamer, but anyone commanding a mobile fortress of that scale has hidden cards waiting to be played.’
Meanwhile... deep within the luxurious high-tech command suite of The Unmovable Wall...
The interior of Lord Sky’s private quarters was dimly lit, illuminated only by the soft, ambient blue luminescence of floating screens and server arrays.
Standing near the central holotable was Brenna... the master dwarven artificer and older sister of Thora.
Brenna was clad in her heavy leather work vest, holding a digital diagnostic scanner in her hand as she addressed the figure sitting in the shadow of the main leather lounge chair.
"The diagnostic scan on Lord Vespera’s equipment is complete," Brenna reported, her voice quiet and serious. "I cross-referenced the frequency logs recorded by your mask sensors during the stream."
The figure in the chair didn’t speak, remaining perfectly still.

"Vespera’s ring..." Brenna revealed, pointing a finger at her scanner screen, "...is a high-tier Disguise Artifact. It was forged using a dual-polarity disguise. To be precise... it was crafted by my Father back in the Underground Mountain Realm."
Brenna looked up at the chair with her eyes glinting.
"It is the exact paired counterpart to the masculine disguise helmet you wear."
Silence hung in the room for a long tense moment.
"Oh...?" a quiet voice echoed from the chair.
PFT-SHHH!
A soft pressurized release of blue spatial mana vented from the neck seam of the heavy full-face streaming helmet.
The figure raised two delicate slender hands, grabbing the sides of the heavy helmet, and smoothly lifted it off her head.
FLASH.
A subtle wave of blue light washed over her physical form.
The masculine broad-shouldered silhouette dissolved completely... revealing a stunning breathtaking young woman.
She possessed long, silky black hair that fell down her back smooth porcelain skin, and sharp, captivating dark eyes that radiated a mixture of intense intelligence and deep fatigue.
She was dressed in an oversized dark-grey Earth traveler’s hoodie and comfortable trousers, looking far more like a stressed brilliant young strategist than a boisterous streaming Lord.
This was Lord Sky’s true identity.
Sky let out a long, heavy sigh, running her manicured fingers through her messy black hair, letting the cool air hit her face.
’Fuck I shouldn’t have gotten drunk...’
The last time that happened, she accidentally spewed her identity and had to kill a man’s whole family for that reason. Never again...
"So..." Sky spoke wearily. "...is Vespera actually a man or a woman beneath that disguise, Brenna?"
Brenna tapped her chin, analyzing the data on her pad.

"Given the strict rules of the Blessed Land which Vespera told us where no male combatants have ever been sighted... it is very possible that the person beneath that disguise is a woman too. She likely uses the single-armed male persona to hide her true capabilities and avoid unwanted political pressure from high-society noble families."
Sky leaned back against her plush leather chair, a smirk touching her lips.
She remembered Vespera saying something similar during their negotiations earlier... about how navigating noble diplomacy was an utterly exhausting chore.

"It makes sense..." Sky murmured, staring at the ceiling. "If she broadcasted her true identity to the World Council, vultures like Lohan Sterling and Etilga Bloom would be swarming her house day and night trying to force corporate contracts or betrothals on her. Using a mysterious disguise keeps everyone guessing."
Sky reached into the pocket of her grey hoodie, pulling out a slim silver case and a sleek plasma lighter.
She popped open the case, pulled out a thin cigarette, and placed it between her lips.
CLICK! FWOOSH!
A tiny blue flame ignited the tip. Sky took a long, slow drag, letting the warm smoke fill her lungs, before exhaling a thin, drifting plume of grey smoke toward the ceiling lights.
"At this point..." Sky said softly, watching the smoke drift away, "...we are not going to win against the Blessed Land in a standard head-on military engagement."
Brenna blinked, surprised by her Lord’s blunt admission. "My Lord?"

"Both of us have been keeping our true cards hidden," Sky explained, tapping her cigarette over a crystal ash tray. "Vespera brought along a high-tier Runic Arcanist today who anchored a rune into the dirt right under my nose without triggering my primary wards and when I sent my two stealth scouts to monitor her perimeter..."
Sky paused, her eyes narrowing in the dim light.
"...They were completely dark within the interview minutes. There was no distress signal and no emergency recall. Whoever Vespera has commanding her forward lines is a monster."
Sky took another drag from her cigarette, her sharp black eyes locking onto Brenna with cold decision.
"Which means..." Sky commanded firmly, "...it’s time to stop holding back. Go tell the forge team and the tactical vanguard to engage ’That’... once it’s time."
Brenna’s jaw subtly dropped.
Her eyes widened in genuine shock.

"A-Are you sure, My Lord?!" Brenna asked with her voice trembling slightly. "Deploying ’That’ will consume eighty percent of our mobile fortress’s core energy reserves! If the execution fails, our territory will be left completely vulnerable for weeks!"
Sky exhaled a slow stream of smoke, offering a smirk.

"I’m completely sure," Sky stated firmly. "All’s fair in love and war, Brenna. And this upcoming battle is going to be one of the biggest, most viral Lord War streams in human history! It wouldn’t make a damn bit of sense for The Unmovable Wall to go down easily without putting on the greatest show this realm has ever seen!"
Brenna stared at her Lord for a second, then snapped into a crisp military salute.
"Understood, My Lord!" Brenna declared. "I will inform the team immediately!"
Brenna turned on her heel and ran out of the command suite, the heavy blast doors sliding shut behind her.
Left alone in the quiet, dimly lit room, Sky leaned her head back against the leather headrest, bringing the cigarette back to her lips.
She took another slow deep wisp of smoke, letting the calming chemical wash over her frayed nerves.
That was the sole reason she smoked... it was the only thing that helped calm her hyperactive over-analytical mind when the pressure of governing a territory got too intense.
She held the smoke in her chest for three seconds, then slowly let it out into the quiet room.
Sky stared into the dark, her eyes burning with fierce unshakeable determination as she whispered into the empty air.
"We of The Unmovable Wall will not lose..."
She clenched her free hand into a tight, white-knuckled fist.
"...We will... win."

chapters.title: Chapter 299: School Project!
paragraphs: Sky closed her eyes, a memory flickering through her mind as a quiet bitter thought echoed in her soul.
’If I win this war... if I pull off the greatest stream in history... maybe my brother will finally look at me properly... maybe he’ll like me a little bit more.’
[A Week Later]
’It’s been such a long time since I saw Big Brother...’
Lia sat quietly at her polished wooden desk inside Junior Cohort Class Three at Valoria Academy with her chin resting in the palm of her hand as she stared wistfully out the high glass window.
Outside, the bright morning sun illuminated the pristine white-marble walkways and manicured hedges of the academy’s central quad.
In truth, it hadn’t even been that long at all.
It had only been a little over a week since Silas had gone through the gate into the Sovereign Realm to establish his territory in the Umbral Basin.
But to a eleven-year-old girl who had spent at least seven years of her life practically glued to her older brother’s side, a week felt like an eternity.
’Especially when I know he’s okay...’
She was worried about him.
She was deeply agonizingly worried.
The Sovereign Realm was notorious across Earth’s media networks for being a brutal, blood-soaked graveyard for Lords.
Every single day, news broadcasts aired reports of new awakeners getting overrun by monster tides, ambushed by rogue Lords, or legally crushed under the corporate foot of high-society noble families.
A terrible terrifying thought occasionally crept into the dark corners of her mind: What if Big Brother died in the Sovereign Realm?
Lia vigorously shook her head, her dark pigtails swaying back and forth as she forcefully squashed the thought.
’No,’ Lia declared stubbornly in her mind. ’No, Big Brother did not die. He’s too smart, too strong, and too stubborn to die out there.’
Why would he die and leave her all alone in this massive unforgiving world?

Silas had dragged her out of the cold gutters when she was just a tiny child, working three dead-end jobs at a time just to feed her, buy her medicine, and now... he had secured her a spot at the most prestigious academy in Valoria City despite the fact that she had betrayed his trust.
He wouldn’t abandon her now... She refused to even entertain the thought...
At the front of the grand lecture hall, the male professor in formal grey suit trousers stepped up to the digital chalkboard.
He tapped a long wooden pointer against a complex glowing geometric diagram of internal mana pathways.

"And so, as we observe in the second-order Mana Circuit theory," the professor lectured, his voice droning on through the silent classroom, "the alignment of a Blue Core requires precise spatial synchronization before external spellcasting can be achieved without mana backlash—"
The professor paused, his sharp eyes scanning the rows of seated students until his gaze landed squarely on the distracted ten-year-old girl by the window.
"Lia Graves!" the professor called out sharply with his voice echoing off the high stone arches.
Lia startled slightly, snapping her head back toward the front of the room.
The professor crossed his arms, offering a stern demanding look.

"Since you appear far more interested in the morning weather than my lecture, perhaps you can answer the question currently displayed on the board? What is the core formula required to stabilize a mana circuit during ambient environmental interference?"
The surrounding students in the classroom turned their heads, a few arrogant noble heirs snickering under their breath, expecting the young girl to stumble.
Lia didn’t even blink.
The exact second her eyes locked onto the complex geometric diagram on the digital chalkboard, her sharp mind processed the variables instantly.
She had already thoroughly studied and mastered Beginner Mana a week ago using the high-tier textbooks Silas had bought for her.

"The core formula requires multiplying the environmental mana density coefficient by the frequency, then dividing the product by the caster’s core resistance threshold," Lia answered smoothly, her sweet voice sounded perfectly calm. "If the environmental interference exceeds three hundred units, an auxiliary node must be inscribed on the secondary circuit to prevent channel rupture."
Silence fell over the classroom.
The professor blinked in genuine surprise, lowering his wooden pointer. He cleared his throat, adjusting his spectacles.
"That... is completely correct, Miss Graves," the professor admitted, gesturing with his hand. "You may sit down."
Lia offered a polite nod, settling back into her wooden chair.
The professor turned back to the digital chalkboard, tapping the glass interface to clear the diagram and pull up a fresh glowing gold assignment tab.

"Now, class, before we wrap up today’s session, we have a major curriculum requirement to address," the professor announced, his voice echoing through the lecture hall. "Next week, you will be completing a comprehensive practical research project on Territory Logistics..."
He gestured toward the screen as a list of rules materialized.

"This is a mandatory group project. There are exactly twenty-one students in this class, meaning you will be automatically structured into seven groups of three. You have the remainder of this period to organize yourselves into your three-person teams. Please sort yourselves out without making unnecessary noise before the closing bell."
The lecture hall instantly erupted into a flurry of quiet hushed chatter as students stood up, shuffling across the floor to form groups with their wealthy noble friends and high-tier academic peers.
Lia let out a soft defeated sigh, leaning back in her chair and pulling her textbook closer.
Predictably, nobody approached her desk.
Nobody rushed over to ask the quiet girl in simple clothes to join their group.
Lia picked up her pen, tracing the corner of her notebook.
She was a bit of a nerd, so what?

She didn’t care about the shallow social politics of Valoria Academy’s wealthy elite... She was deliberately milking every single bit of the academic opportunity Silas had given her, pushing herself to become the best and most intelligent version of herself so that when her Big Brother returned, he would be proud of the sister he had put money in to raise.
Suddenly, a pair of warm arms wrapped gently around Lia’s shoulders from behind.
"Don’t be so grumpy, Lia~!" a cheerful, energetic voice giggled directly in her ear! "I’ll be your partner!"
Lia gasped, turning her head to see Kaede... a breathtakingly cute ten-year-old girl with dark, shiny hair tied in neat side-ribbons and bright expressive eyes.

A few seats down, several wealthy noble boys who had been walking over to ask Kaede to join their group froze in their tracks, looking deeply disappointed as Kaede completely ignored their hopeful gestures.
Lia pouted slightly, a soft blush touching her cheeks as Kaede squeezed her in a tight hug.
"Th-Thanks, Kaede..."
Before the boys could even recover from Kaede’s rejection—
STEP! STEP!
A second girl stepped up to Lia’s desk.
She possessed silky vibrant purple hair styled in elegant twin pigtails, striking violet eyes, and a sharp haughty posture that radiated natural noble authority.
It was Penelope.
Penelope folded her arms over her chest, leaning her hip against the side of Lia’s wooden desk.

Before any of the nearby students could even open their mouths to offer her a spot in their groups, Penelope shot them a fierce, razor-sharp glare that made them immediately turn around and walk away.
Penelope turned back to Lia, gently reaching out with her manicured fingers and playfully pinching Lia’s soft cheek.

"Cheer up, Lia," Penelope remarked, her tone carrying a light arrogant huff that couldn’t hide her genuine warmth. "Who on earth did you think I wanted to be partners with before the professor even made the announcement? You’re stuck with us."
Lia bit her lower lip, her eyes sparkling with quiet, immense happiness as she looked at the two girls standing beside her desk.
"Thanks, guys..." Lia muttered softly with a genuine smile breaking across her face.
In her heart, Lia felt a wave of sweet relief.

Her Big Brother wouldn’t mind her having friends, right? Over the past week, as Silas had been away building his territory, these two had stuck by her side, eating lunch with her, studying in the library, and protecting her from the sneering comments of arrogant upperclassmen.
They had become truly close friends.
RIIIIING!
The sharp ringing chime of the closing bell echoed through the academy halls!
The professor stepped away from his desk, raising his voice over the sound of packing bags.
"Class dismissed! Remember, your group project is due next week Monday! That gives you exactly seven days! Work hard, and do not leave the research to the last minute!"
"Yes, Professor!" the class responded in unison.
Students quickly grabbed their leather satchels and headed for the double exit doors.
Lia, Kaede, and Penelope packed their notebooks into their backpacks, stepping out into the wide, sunlit hallway together.
Kaede stretched her arms high above her head, letting out a dramatic sigh. "Man, how much homework do we even have today?"
Lia pulled out a small pocket planner, checking her neat handwriting. "We have two other assignments from Basic Magic Spells and Geography... plus the big group project, of course."
Kaede’s eyes lit up as she clapped her hands together.

"Well, today is Monday, so the project isn’t due until next Monday! That means we have the whole week and the entire weekend to work on it! Hey... would you guys like to come over to my place today after school so we can get started?"
Kaede leaned in closer, her dark eyes sparkling with wild excitement.
"And plus... we can watch the Blessed Land Stream together on my big screen!"
The moment the words "Blessed Land Stream" left Kaede’s mouth, Penelope’s eyes widened with intense interest.
Over the past week, the entire global network had gone completely, utterly insane over the news of the upcoming territory war...

The hype surrounding Lord Vespera and the Blessed Land had reached such a mind-boggling peak that almost everyone and their mother across Earth and the Sovereign Realm was on standby, waiting for the live broadcast signal to go live.
Lia didn’t hate the Blessed Land at all... she was actually a massive fan of Lord Vespera’s viral stream clips, captivated by the mysterious single-armed Warlord in the suit.
But in her heart, Lia would always root for her Big Brother’s territory first... as soon as Silas finally actually told her the official name of his territory.
Penelope adjusted her backpack strap, offering a calm composed nod. "I don’t mind going to your place, Kaede. My older sister is exceptionally busy at the moment anyway..."
Hearing Penelope mention her older sister, both Lia and Kaede paused, offering her a quiet, deeply sympathetic look.
Over the past few days, Penelope’s family had been rocked by massive, high-profile tragedy.
Her older sister had been publicly accused of murdering their father by blasting him off the top floor of the LAB Building facility that was in the city center.
Though the police investigation had never proven the murder allegations true, the father’s death had left Penelope’s sister as the sole legal inheritor of the family’s vast corporate fortune.
In less than a week, Penelope’s family had transitioned from wealthy citizens to high-tier influential Lords in Awakened Society, but the emotional weight and media scandal had been immense.
They both felt deeply sorry for what Penelope was going through...
Lia pulled out her smartphone from her pocket, swiping open her screen.
"I need to take permission from Martha first before I agree."
Lia dialed the home landline, placing the phone to her ear.
After two rings, the sweet maternal voice of Martha... Silas’s dedicated housekeeper back at their luxury apartment answered the call.
"Hello, Lia dear! Are you finished with classes?"
"Hi, Martha!" Lia greeted warmly. "Yes, class just ended! Where are you?"

"Ah, I’m so sorry, sweetie, I’m currently stuck in heavy traffic near the central boulevard," Martha explained with the distant hum of car horns audible through the speaker. "An armaments transport truck stalled on the bridge, so the pick-up line is completely backed up. I’ll be there in about twenty minutes!"
"It’s okay, Martha!" Lia reassured her quickly. "Actually... my friends invited me to go over to Kaede’s house today to work on a group project and watch a stream! Can I go with them until...?"
Lia turned her head, mute-covering the phone mic, and looked at Kaede.
"Until when?"
"Until the evening!" Kaede answered with a bright smile. "My butler can drop you off, or Martha can pick you up from my place later!"
Lia unmuted the phone. "Until this evening! Is that okay?"

sentences.text: Sky closed her eyes, a memory flickering through her mind as a quiet bitter thought echoed in her soul.
’If I win this war... if I pull off the greatest stream in history... maybe my brother will finally look at me properly... maybe he’ll like me a little bit more.’
[A Week Later]
’It’s been such a long time since I saw Big Brother...’
Lia sat quietly at her polished wooden desk inside Junior Cohort Class Three at Valoria Academy with her chin resting in the palm of her hand as she stared wistfully out the high glass window.
Outside, the bright morning sun illuminated the pristine white-marble walkways and manicured hedges of the academy’s central quad.
In truth, it hadn’t even been that long at all.
It had only been a little over a week since Silas had gone through the gate into the Sovereign Realm to establish his territory in the Umbral Basin.
But to a eleven-year-old girl who had spent at least seven years of her life practically glued to her older brother’s side, a week felt like an eternity.
’Especially when I know he’s okay...’
She was worried about him.
She was deeply agonizingly worried.
The Sovereign Realm was notorious across Earth’s media networks for being a brutal, blood-soaked graveyard for Lords.
Every single day, news broadcasts aired reports of new awakeners getting overrun by monster tides, ambushed by rogue Lords, or legally crushed under the corporate foot of high-society noble families.
A terrible terrifying thought occasionally crept into the dark corners of her mind: What if Big Brother died in the Sovereign Realm?
Lia vigorously shook her head, her dark pigtails swaying back and forth as she forcefully squashed the thought.
’No,’ Lia declared stubbornly in her mind. ’No, Big Brother did not die.
He’s too smart, too strong, and too stubborn to die out there.’
Why would he die and leave her all alone in this massive unforgiving world?

Silas had dragged her out of the cold gutters when she was just a tiny child, working three dead-end jobs at a time just to feed her, buy her medicine, and now... he had secured her a spot at the most prestigious academy in Valoria City despite the fact that she had betrayed his trust.
He wouldn’t abandon her now...
She refused to even entertain the thought...
At the front of the grand lecture hall, the male professor in formal grey suit trousers stepped up to the digital chalkboard.
He tapped a long wooden pointer against a complex glowing geometric diagram of internal mana pathways.

"And so, as we observe in the second-order Mana Circuit theory," the professor lectured, his voice droning on through the silent classroom, "the alignment of a Blue Core requires precise spatial synchronization before external spellcasting can be achieved without mana backlash—"
The professor paused, his sharp eyes scanning the rows of seated students until his gaze landed squarely on the distracted ten-year-old girl by the window.
"Lia Graves!" the professor called out sharply with his voice echoing off the high stone arches.
Lia startled slightly, snapping her head back toward the front of the room.
The professor crossed his arms, offering a stern demanding look.
"Since you appear far more interested in the morning weather than my lecture, perhaps you can answer the question currently displayed on the board?
What is the core formula required to stabilize a mana circuit during ambient environmental interference?"
The surrounding students in the classroom turned their heads, a few arrogant noble heirs snickering under their breath, expecting the young girl to stumble.
Lia didn’t even blink.
The exact second her eyes locked onto the complex geometric diagram on the digital chalkboard, her sharp mind processed the variables instantly.
She had already thoroughly studied and mastered Beginner Mana a week ago using the high-tier textbooks Silas had bought for her.

"The core formula requires multiplying the environmental mana density coefficient by the frequency, then dividing the product by the caster’s core resistance threshold," Lia answered smoothly, her sweet voice sounded perfectly calm.
"If the environmental interference exceeds three hundred units, an auxiliary node must be inscribed on the secondary circuit to prevent channel rupture."
Silence fell over the classroom.
The professor blinked in genuine surprise, lowering his wooden pointer.
He cleared his throat, adjusting his spectacles.
"That... is completely correct, Miss Graves," the professor admitted, gesturing with his hand.
"You may sit down."
Lia offered a polite nod, settling back into her wooden chair.
The professor turned back to the digital chalkboard, tapping the glass interface to clear the diagram and pull up a fresh glowing gold assignment tab.
"Now, class, before we wrap up today’s session, we have a major curriculum requirement to address," the professor announced, his voice echoing through the lecture hall.
"Next week, you will be completing a comprehensive practical research project on Territory Logistics..."
He gestured toward the screen as a list of rules materialized.
"This is a mandatory group project.
There are exactly twenty-one students in this class, meaning you will be automatically structured into seven groups of three.
You have the remainder of this period to organize yourselves into your three-person teams.
Please sort yourselves out without making unnecessary noise before the closing bell."
The lecture hall instantly erupted into a flurry of quiet hushed chatter as students stood up, shuffling across the floor to form groups with their wealthy noble friends and high-tier academic peers.
Lia let out a soft defeated sigh, leaning back in her chair and pulling her textbook closer.
Predictably, nobody approached her desk.
Nobody rushed over to ask the quiet girl in simple clothes to join their group.
Lia picked up her pen, tracing the corner of her notebook.
She was a bit of a nerd, so what?
She didn’t care about the shallow social politics of Valoria Academy’s wealthy elite...

She was deliberately milking every single bit of the academic opportunity Silas had given her, pushing herself to become the best and most intelligent version of herself so that when her Big Brother returned, he would be proud of the sister he had put money in to raise.
Suddenly, a pair of warm arms wrapped gently around Lia’s shoulders from behind.
"Don’t be so grumpy, Lia~!" a cheerful, energetic voice giggled directly in her ear!
"I’ll be your partner!"
Lia gasped, turning her head to see Kaede... a breathtakingly cute ten-year-old girl with dark, shiny hair tied in neat side-ribbons and bright expressive eyes.

A few seats down, several wealthy noble boys who had been walking over to ask Kaede to join their group froze in their tracks, looking deeply disappointed as Kaede completely ignored their hopeful gestures.
Lia pouted slightly, a soft blush touching her cheeks as Kaede squeezed her in a tight hug.
"Th-Thanks, Kaede..."
Before the boys could even recover from Kaede’s rejection—
STEP!
STEP!
A second girl stepped up to Lia’s desk.
She possessed silky vibrant purple hair styled in elegant twin pigtails, striking violet eyes, and a sharp haughty posture that radiated natural noble authority.
It was Penelope.
Penelope folded her arms over her chest, leaning her hip against the side of Lia’s wooden desk.

You’re stuck with us."

chapters.title: Chapter 300: Thor In Midgard
paragraphs: On the other end of the line, Martha smiled softly.
Knowing Kaede and Penelope’s families well, and taking her responsibility as the household guardian seriously while her Master was away in the Sovereign Realm, Martha gave her immediate approval.

"That is completely fine, Lia dear," Martha replied warmly. "You work hard on your project, and I will drive over to Kaede’s estate in the evening to pick you up... Just make sure to leave your phone’s GPS location turned on so I can track your route."
"I will! Thank you, Martha! You’re the best!" Lia cheered sweetly.
Beside her, Kaede leaned her head right next to the phone mic, yelling out playfully.
"Thank you, Martha! You’re a sweetheart!"
Martha let out a merry chuckle over the speaker. "Have fun, girls! Stay safe!"
Lia cut the call, slipping her phone back into her pocket as the three girls walked out through the grand arched front gates of Valoria Academy.
Outside, the wide entrance plaza was packed with luxury hover-limousines, private security transports, and parents picking up their children from school.
Penelope held her leather bag, looking around the busy street.
"So... how are we getting to your house, Kaede? Did your guardian call a cab?"
Before Kaede could even answer—
VWOOSH!
A sleek midnight-black luxury sedan adorned with silver crests smoothly pulled up to the curb right in front of them!
The rear door opened, and a tall, impeccably dressed butler wearing white gloves stepped out, bowing deeply at a ninety-degree angle to the ten-year-old girl.
"Welcome back from classes, Lady Kaede," the butler greeted with absolute, flawless professional decorum. "I have prepared the vehicle for your companions."
Penelope blinked her violet eyes, looking at the blindingly expensive luxury vehicle, and deadpanned.
"You really have a lot of money, huh?"
Kaede giggled, leaning in close between Lia and Penelope, whispering in a dramatic conspiratorial tone.
"Well, I did tell you guys... I’m technically the princess of the Shogunate Isles!"
Lia and Penelope both looked at her with totally flat unamused deadpan expressions, nodding along blankly.
"Uh-huh... sure you are."
Kaede puffed out her cheeks in an instant, pouting furiously at them! "Hey! Why do you guys look at me like that?! You don’t believe me?!"
Of course they didn’t believe her!

Why on earth would the royal ruling family of the distant Shogunate Isles send their precious, legitimate royal princess to attend a standard middle-tier academy in Valoria City without a fifty-man royal guard escort?!

Besides, global media broadcasts frequently showed images of the Shogunate Isles’ royal family... and the Shogunate Lord’s young Daughter was legendary across the eastern continent as one of the most breathtaking and peerlessly beautiful young child in the entire world.
Kaede was undeniably adorable and cute, but there was no way this playful ten-year-old girl sitting in front of them could hold a candle to that legendary royal beauty’s natural, god-tier elegance.
"Get in, get in! You’ll see!" Kaede huffed playfully, ushering them into the plush leather back seats of the luxury sedan.
The butler carefully closed the heavy door behind them, stepping into the driver’s seat.
"Please secure your positions, young ladies," the butler instructed smoothly.
The moment he pressed the ignition button, automatic leather seatbelts glided smoothly across their shoulders, locking them securely into place.
Soft relaxing ambient classical music began playing through the high-end cabin speakers as the sedan glided effortlessly into the city traffic.
Lia bobbed her head to the gentle rhythm of the music, looking out the tinted window as they drove through the high-end residential districts of Valoria City.
After a fifteen-minute drive past manicured parks and private security gates, the sedan turned down a long, private driveway lined with high stone walls and armed security posts.
The vehicle came to a smooth stop in front of a beautiful, traditional two-story estate surrounded by cherry blossom trees and stone lanterns.
Kaede stepped out of the vehicle first, throwing her arms wide open with supreme pride.
"Welcome to my humble abode! This is where I’m staying!"
Penelope and Lia stepped out onto the gravel driveway, looking up at the sprawling, gorgeous estate... and then turned to look at Kaede with deeply strange, deadpan expressions.
Kaede noticed their looks and quickly added with a casual wave of her hand.
"I mean, it’s pretty tiny and cramped compared to my main family palace back in the Shogunate Isles, but it’s cozy enough for living in Valoria City!"
Penelope stared at the massive two-story estate, thinking in utter deadpan disbelief.
’Tiny?! Cramped?! This estate is three times bigger than me and my sister’s high-rise luxury apartment!’
Lia stared at the manicured gardens, thinking in deadpan amazement.
’This place is literally four times bigger than Big Brother’s entire apartment!’
And to make matters even more absurd... there was a full staff of househelp waiting.
A row of four polite maids in crisp black-and-white uniforms and two head butlers stood by the entrance, bowing respectfully as the three girls stepped onto the porch.
"Welcome home, Lady Kaede! Welcome, honored guests!" the maids greeted in unison.

The househelp stepped forward with gentle efficiency, assisting Lia and Penelope in removing their shoes, placing their backpacks into leather storage cubbies, and guiding them into a grand, sunlit living room.
The living room featured a massive plush leather sectional sofa, a pristine mahogany coffee table, and wide glass doors opening to a private garden koi pond.

Within two minutes of sitting down on the soft sofa, the maids brought out an elaborate silver tray laden with an overwhelming assortment of treats... fresh strawberry shortcakes, imported chocolate truffles, iced berry teas, and warm honey pastries.
Lia held a delicate porcelain cup, feeling completely, utterly babied by the service.
Kaede sank into the plush sofa cushion, letting out a boisterous laugh as she popped a chocolate truffle into her mouth.
"Hahaha! Don’t look so embarrassed, Lia! This isn’t even the full royal treatment! I’m not going to let you guys leave my house today until you’re both fat and happy!"
Kaede then turned her head toward the head butler standing near the doorway, waving her hand energetically.
"Sebastian! Turn on the main wall display!" Kaede ordered excitedly. "Put it directly on the Blessed Land Stream Channel!"
"Right away, Lady Kaede," the butler replied, bowing smoothly.
The butler picked up a sleek glass remote, tapping the screen.
HUMMM.
The entire far wall of the living room illuminated, transforming into a massive eighty-inch ultra-high-definition holographic television display.
The broadcast signal connected instantly to the global LordTube network, pulling up the official live stream channel for the Blessed Land Territory War!

The screen was currently displaying a sleek glowing purple standby window, featuring a countdown timer running against the backdrop of a dramatic animated banner of The Unmovable Wall facing off against the shadowy silhouette of Lord Vespera.
Right beneath the standby window, the live viewer counter flashed in brilliant gold numbers.
[250,000,000 CONCURRENT VIEWERS ON STANDBY!]
Two hundred and fifty million people were sitting in the virtual waiting room before the broadcast had even started.
Kaede pumped her fist in the air with delight.
"Alright! Perfect timing! We didn’t miss a single second! Let’s go, Blessed Land!"
Kaede leaned over the sofa armrest, looking at Lia and Penelope with wide, excited eyes: "So, guys... who are you supporting in this war?!"
Penelope adjusted her purple pigtails, holding her cup of tea as she spoke in a calm, matter-of-fact tone.
"I support The Unmovable Wall. Lord Sky is the underdog in this engagement, and I prefer supporting underdogs."
The exact second Penelope said she liked supporting underdogs... Lia and Kaede both turned their heads simultaneously, staring at Penelope with a single synchronized thought echoing in their minds.
’But... don’t you usually hate commoners and underdogs...?’
Lia quickly shook off the thought, smiling softly as she hugged her throw pillow.
"Well... I support the Blessed Land! Lord Vespera is just way too cool!"
Kaede instantly lunged across the sofa, throwing her arms around Lia in a tight ecstatic hug.
"YESSSS!" Kaede cheered out loud, rubbing her cheek against Lia’s.
"BLESSED LAND GIRLIES FOR THE WIN! LORD VESPERA IS GOING TO CRUSH THEM!"

And as the three girls sat together in the luxurious living room, enjoying their pastries and cheering for the broadcast, the countdown timer on the massive screen hit zero... and the greatest Lord War stream in history officially went live.
In an ultra-luxurious, six-star private dining pavilion suspended hundreds of feet above the sparkling neon-lit skyline of Rhyx City, Thor sat slumped in a massive gilded mahogany chair.
She was dressed in a simple, skin-tight white singlet and dark cargo trousers with her massive heavily muscled arms resting flat against the pristine marble tabletop.

Her long unkempt blonde hair fell in wild waves over her broad shoulders, and her sharp, storm-blue eyes stared intently at a floating golden holographic screen suspended in the center of the private dining suite.
GWWWRRRRLLLLL!
A sound like rolling thunder erupted from her stomach. The violent vibration was so loud that the crystal chandeliers hanging from the high ceiling subtly rattled.
"Bah!" Thor grumbled out loud, slamming her broad calloused fist flat against the armrest with enough force to crack the polished wood. "Where is the feast?! My gut is eating itself alive!"
Thor glared at the floating holographic screen in front of her.

The display was showing a glowing countdown timer ticking down to zero on the global LordTube network, set against the dramatic high-definition banner of The Unmovable Wall facing off against The Blessed Land.
The numbers on the digital clock flickered in real time:
Thor squinted her storm-blue eyes at the timer, crossing her massive, corded arms over her broad chest.
Watching live broadcasts on floating magic mirrors was a thoroughly bizarre experience for a Norse deity.
Back in the golden hall of Valhalla in Asgard, if warriors wanted to watch a war, they didn’t sit in soft velvet chairs staring at glowing glass panels.
They grabbed their war hammers, mounted giant armored goats, tore through the clouds, and smashed their enemies’ skulls in person.
She couldn’t help but reflect on how peculiar streaming was in this world.
Why on Midgard didn’t they have this kind of magic back in Asgard?
It would have saved her thousands of leagues of flying across the realms just to watch Odin kick a frost giant king into a frozen ravine.
Seated directly beside Thor in an equally opulent velvet chair was a young woman radiating an aura of divine undeniable royalty.
She possessed long shimmering royal-blue hair that cascaded past her slender waist like a liquid sapphire waterfall, elegant porcelain features, and piercing azure eyes.
She wore an intricate, silk-embroidered gown adorned with gold imperial crests... the legitimate, high-ranking Princess of the Lord World.
Hearing Thor’s stomach roar like a starving dragon, the Princess let out a soft, elegant laugh, covering her smiling lips with a delicate silk-embroidered fan.
"Are you truly that ravenous, Lady Thor?" the Princess asked smoothly, her melodic voice carrying the refined voice of royalty. "I thought we were here primarily to observe the broadcast."
Thor turned her head, her storm-blue eyes flashing with blunt unyielding conviction.

"I am a God of Thunder!" Thor declared loudly, slamming her hand flat onto the marble table again. "I do not watch battles on an empty belly! Seeing flesh get torn and spells exploding makes a true warrior thirsty and hungry! I want to see this war while tearing through a mountain of meat!"
The royal-blue-haired Princess smiled warmly, waving her delicate, ringed hand toward the double oak doors of the private suite.
"At once, then..." the Princess commanded softly to the waiting staff.
CLICK.
The double doors swung open instantly!
A line of twelve high-tier imperial butlers clad in pristine black tailcoats and white gloves marched into the private suite in perfect synchronized precision.
Each butler carried a massive, silver-domed serving tray stacked three feet high with legendary culinary dishes prepared by Rhyx City’s top-tier master chefs.
CLINK! CLINK! CLINK!
The butlers set the heavy platters down onto the massive marble table, uncovering silver domes one after another in a rapid sequence.
The aroma that erupted into the air was intoxicating.

Roast hydra legs glazed in golden mana-honey, roasted wyvern ribs seasoned with crushed fire-peppers, giant kraken tentacles seared in spiced butter, steaming bowls of aromatic mana-rice, and entire roasted wild boars glistening with savory crackling juices.
Within ten seconds, a literal mountain of high-tier food stood piled before Thor.

Besides, global media broadcasts frequently showed images of the Shogunate Isles’ royal family... and the Shogunate Lord’s young Daughter was legendary across the eastern continent as one of the most breathtaking and peerlessly beautiful young child in the entire world.
Kaede was undeniably adorable and cute, but there was no way this playful ten-year-old girl sitting in front of them could hold a candle to that legendary royal beauty’s natural, god-tier elegance.
"Get in, get in!
You’ll see!" Kaede huffed playfully, ushering them into the plush leather back seats of the luxury sedan.
The butler carefully closed the heavy door behind them, stepping into the driver’s seat.
"Please secure your positions, young ladies," the butler instructed smoothly.
The moment he pressed the ignition button, automatic leather seatbelts glided smoothly across their shoulders, locking them securely into place.
Soft relaxing ambient classical music began playing through the high-end cabin speakers as the sedan glided effortlessly into the city traffic.
Lia bobbed her head to the gentle rhythm of the music, looking out the tinted window as they drove through the high-end residential districts of Valoria City.
After a fifteen-minute drive past manicured parks and private security gates, the sedan turned down a long, private driveway lined with high stone walls and armed security posts.
The vehicle came to a smooth stop in front of a beautiful, traditional two-story estate surrounded by cherry blossom trees and stone lanterns.
Kaede stepped out of the vehicle first, throwing her arms wide open with supreme pride.
"Welcome to my humble abode!
This is where I’m staying!"
Penelope and Lia stepped out onto the gravel driveway, looking up at the sprawling, gorgeous estate... and then turned to look at Kaede with deeply strange, deadpan expressions.
Kaede noticed their looks and quickly added with a casual wave of her hand.
"I mean, it’s pretty tiny and cramped compared to my main family palace back in the Shogunate Isles, but it’s cozy enough for living in Valoria City!"
Penelope stared at the massive two-story estate, thinking in utter deadpan disbelief.
’Tiny?!
Cramped?!
This estate is three times bigger than me and my sister’s high-rise luxury apartment!’
Lia stared at the manicured gardens, thinking in deadpan amazement.
’This place is literally four times bigger than Big Brother’s entire apartment!’
And to make matters even more absurd... there was a full staff of househelp waiting.
A row of four polite maids in crisp black-and-white uniforms and two head butlers stood by the entrance, bowing respectfully as the three girls stepped onto the porch.
"Welcome home, Lady Kaede!
Welcome, honored guests!" the maids greeted in unison.

The househelp stepped forward with gentle efficiency, assisting Lia and Penelope in removing their shoes, placing their backpacks into leather storage cubbies, and guiding them into a grand, sunlit living room.
The living room featured a massive plush leather sectional sofa, a pristine mahogany coffee table, and wide glass doors opening to a private garden koi pond.

Within two minutes of sitting down on the soft sofa, the maids brought out an elaborate silver tray laden with an overwhelming assortment of treats... fresh strawberry shortcakes, imported chocolate truffles, iced berry teas, and warm honey pastries.
Lia held a delicate porcelain cup, feeling completely, utterly babied by the service.
Kaede sank into the plush sofa cushion, letting out a boisterous laugh as she popped a chocolate truffle into her mouth.
"Hahaha!
Don’t look so embarrassed, Lia!
This isn’t even the full royal treatment!
I’m not going to let you guys leave my house today until you’re both fat and happy!"
Kaede then turned her head toward the head butler standing near the doorway, waving her hand energetically.
"Sebastian!
Turn on the main wall display!" Kaede ordered excitedly.
"Put it directly on the Blessed Land Stream Channel!"
"Right away, Lady Kaede," the butler replied, bowing smoothly.
The butler picked up a sleek glass remote, tapping the screen.
HUMMM.
The entire far wall of the living room illuminated, transforming into a massive eighty-inch ultra-high-definition holographic television display.
The broadcast signal connected instantly to the global LordTube network, pulling up the official live stream channel for the Blessed Land Territory War!

The screen was currently displaying a sleek glowing purple standby window, featuring a countdown timer running against the backdrop of a dramatic animated banner of The Unmovable Wall facing off against the shadowy silhouette of Lord Vespera.
Right beneath the standby window, the live viewer counter flashed in brilliant gold numbers.
[250,000,000 CONCURRENT VIEWERS ON STANDBY!]
Two hundred and fifty million people were sitting in the virtual waiting room before the broadcast had even started.
Kaede pumped her fist in the air with delight.
"Alright!
Perfect timing!
We didn’t miss a single second!
Let’s go, Blessed Land!"
Kaede leaned over the sofa armrest, looking at Lia and Penelope with wide, excited eyes: "So, guys... who are you supporting in this war?!"
Penelope adjusted her purple pigtails, holding her cup of tea as she spoke in a calm, matter-of-fact tone.
"I support The Unmovable Wall.
Lord Sky is the underdog in this engagement, and I prefer supporting underdogs."
The exact second Penelope said she liked supporting underdogs...
Lia and Kaede both turned their heads simultaneously, staring at Penelope with a single synchronized thought echoing in their minds.
’But... don’t you usually hate commoners and underdogs...?’
Lia quickly shook off the thought, smiling softly as she hugged her throw pillow.
"Well...
I support the Blessed Land!
Lord Vespera is just way too cool!"
Kaede instantly lunged across the sofa, throwing her arms around Lia in a tight ecstatic hug.
"YESSSS!" Kaede cheered out loud, rubbing her cheek against Lia’s.
"BLESSED LAND GIRLIES FOR THE WIN!
LORD VESPERA IS GOING TO CRUSH THEM!"

And as the three girls sat together in the luxurious living room, enjoying their pastries and cheering for the broadcast, the countdown timer on the massive screen hit zero... and the greatest Lord War stream in history officially went live.
In an ultra-luxurious, six-star private dining pavilion suspended hundreds of feet above the sparkling neon-lit skyline of Rhyx City, Thor sat slumped in a massive gilded mahogany chair.
She was dressed in a simple, skin-tight white singlet and dark cargo trousers with her massive heavily muscled arms resting flat against the pristine marble tabletop.

Her long unkempt blonde hair fell in wild waves over her broad shoulders, and her sharp, storm-blue eyes stared intently at a floating golden holographic screen suspended in the center of the private dining suite.
GWWWRRRRLLLLL!
A sound like rolling thunder erupted from her stomach.
The violent vibration was so loud that the crystal chandeliers hanging from the high ceiling subtly rattled.
"Bah!" Thor grumbled out loud, slamming her broad calloused fist flat against the armrest with enough force to crack the polished wood.
"Where is the feast?!
My gut is eating itself alive!"
Thor glared at the floating holographic screen in front of her.

The display was showing a glowing countdown timer ticking down to zero on the global LordTube network, set against the dramatic high-definition banner of The Unmovable Wall facing off against The Blessed Land.
The numbers on the digital clock flickered in real time:
Thor squinted her storm-blue eyes at the timer, crossing her massive, corded arms over her broad chest.
Watching live broadcasts on floating magic mirrors was a thoroughly bizarre experience for a Norse deity.
Back in the golden hall of Valhalla in Asgard, if warriors wanted to watch a war, they didn’t sit in soft velvet chairs staring at glowing glass panels.
They grabbed their war hammers, mounted giant armored goats, tore through the clouds, and smashed their enemies’ skulls in person.
She couldn’t help but reflect on how peculiar streaming was in this world.
Why on Midgard didn’t they have this kind of magic back in Asgard?
It would have saved her thousands of leagues of flying across the realms just to watch Odin kick a frost giant king into a frozen ravine.
Seated directly beside Thor in an equally opulent velvet chair was a young woman radiating an aura of divine undeniable royalty.
She possessed long shimmering royal-blue hair that cascaded past her slender waist like a liquid sapphire waterfall, elegant porcelain features, and piercing azure eyes.
She wore an intricate, silk-embroidered gown adorned with gold imperial crests... the legitimate, high-ranking Princess of the Lord World.
Hearing Thor’s stomach roar like a starving dragon, the Princess let out a soft, elegant laugh, covering her smiling lips with a delicate silk-embroidered fan.
"Are you truly that ravenous, Lady Thor?" the Princess asked smoothly, her melodic voice carrying the refined voice of royalty.
"I thought we were here primarily to observe the broadcast."
Thor turned her head, her storm-blue eyes flashing with blunt unyielding conviction.
"I am a God of Thunder!" Thor declared loudly, slamming her hand flat onto the marble table again.
"I do not watch battles on an empty belly!
Seeing flesh get torn and spells exploding makes a true warrior thirsty and hungry!
I want to see this war while tearing through a mountain of meat!"
The royal-blue-haired Princess smiled warmly, waving her delicate, ringed hand toward the double oak doors of the private suite.
"At once, then..." the Princess commanded softly to the waiting staff.
CLICK.
The double doors swung open instantly!
A line of twelve high-tier imperial butlers clad in pristine black tailcoats and white gloves marched into the private suite in perfect synchronized precision.
Each butler carried a massive, silver-domed serving tray stacked three feet high with legendary culinary dishes prepared by Rhyx City’s top-tier master chefs.
CLINK!
CLINK!
CLINK!
The butlers set the heavy platters down onto the massive marble table, uncovering silver domes one after another in a rapid sequence.
The aroma that erupted into the air was intoxicating.

Roast hydra legs glazed in golden mana-honey, roasted wyvern ribs seasoned with crushed fire-peppers, giant kraken tentacles seared in spiced butter, steaming bowls of aromatic mana-rice, and entire roasted wild boars glistening with savory crackling juices.
Within ten seconds, a literal mountain of high-tier food stood piled before Thor.
